rows.summary:
SEBI has issued Circular No. **SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHS-PoD-2/I/11700/2026 dated May 15, 2026**, which governs the **permitted use of fresh borrowings by Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs)** in situations where **Net Borrowings exceed 49% of the value of InvIT assets**. The notice does not restate the detailed borrowing conditions, but it makes clear that this is a compliance requirement for the affected InvITs and related listed entities, and that the full circular is attached for reference.

The circular is stated to be **effective immediately**, meaning there is **no waiting period or deferred implementation date**. Compliance teams should treat the new SEBI direction as already in force from the date of the circular and should review any fresh borrowing activity by InvITs against the new SEBI instructions to ensure it is used only in the manner permitted under the circular. The exchange notice specifically advises **listed entities to take note and comply accordingly**, so any listed InvIT or listed entity with exposure to InvIT borrowing arrangements should assess whether its current or proposed borrowings fall within the >49% Net Borrowings threshold and align internal approvals, treasury actions, and disclosure/compliance processes with the SEBI circular.

rows.title: XBRL based filing for Violations related to Code of Conduct (CoC) under SEBI PIT Regulations, 2015
rows.desc: NOTICE NoticeNo. 20260504-17 NoticeDate 04May2026 Category CircularsListedCompanies Segment General Department ListingCompliance-Monitoring Subject XBRLbasedfilingforViolationsrelatedtoCodeofConduct(CoC) underSEBIPITRegulations,2015 Attachments NoAttachment To, Compliance Officers, All Listed Entities/Intermediaries/Fiduciaries Subject: XBRL based filing for Violations related to Code of Conduct (CoC) under SEBI PIT Regulations, 2015 SEBI, vide Circular No. SEBI/HO/ISD/ISD/CIR/P/2020/135 dated July 23, 2020, prescribed the format for reporting violations of the Code of Conduct under the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations 2015 (SEBI PIT Regulations 2015). To enhance accuracy and efficiency in disclosures, the Exchange has introduced an XBRL utility for reporting such violations through the Listing Centre, with effect from May 05, 2026. Listed entities/intermediaries/fiduciaries shall submit the reporting through the following paths: • To download XBRL Utility: Listing Centre > Listing Compliance Module > XBRL > Download XBRL Utility • For submission: Listing Centre > Listing Compliance Module > XBRL > E-filing > Violation related to Code of Conduct (CoC) It may be noted that reporting shall be made only in XBRL mode, without submission of any PDF file. Further, any unlisted entity reporting in the capacity of Intermediary or Fiduciary shall continue to submit the disclosures through email at corp.relations@bseindia.com, as per Exchange Circular No. 20200724-10 dated 24 July 2020. Accordingly, the existing filing path i.e. Compliance Module > Non quarterly submissions > Reporting of Code of Conduct violations SEBI PIT Regulations 2015; as specified under Exchange Circular No. 20201223-8 dated December 23, 2020, shall be discontinued. The disclosures pertaining to violations of the Code of Conduct shall not be disseminated on the Exchange website. All listed entities are advised to mandatorily submit the reporting through the Listing Centre only. Submission through any other mode(s) shall not be taken on record and shall be considered as invalid submission. Listed entities/intermediaries/fiduciaries are advised to take note of the above and comply accordingly. Shyamsingh Bhagirath Yashaswini Verma Manager Deputy Manager Listing Compliance and Operations Listing Compliance and Operations
rows.summary:
This notice changes the filing method for reporting violations of the Code of Conduct under the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015. SEBI had originally prescribed the reporting format in Circular No. SEBI/HO/ISD/ISD/CIR/P/2020/135 dated July 23, 2020, and the Exchange is now moving those disclosures to an XBRL-based process to improve accuracy and efficiency. The new XBRL utility is available through the Listing Centre and becomes effective on May 05, 2026.

For listed entities, intermediaries, and fiduciaries, the reporting path is now: Listing Centre > Listing Compliance Module > XBRL > Download XBRL Utility for the utility itself, and Listing Centre > Listing Compliance Module > XBRL > E-filing > Violation related to Code of Conduct (CoC) for submission. The notice explicitly says these disclosures must be filed only in XBRL mode and must not be accompanied by any PDF attachment. Any submission made through any other mode will not be taken on record and will be treated as invalid.

There is one exception: an unlisted entity filing in the capacity of an intermediary or fiduciary must continue to send the disclosure by email to corp.relations@bseindia.com, in line with Exchange Circular No. 20200724-10 dated July 24, 2020. At the same time, the older filing path under Compliance Module > Non quarterly submissions > Reporting of Code of Conduct violations SEBI PIT Regulations 2015, as mentioned in Exchange Circular No. 20201223-8 dated December 23, 2020, is being discontinued. The notice also states that these Code of Conduct violation disclosures will not be disseminated on the Exchange website, and listed entities are instructed to file mandatorily through the Listing Centre only.

This notice updates the “single filing system” that was introduced under Exchange notice no. 20240930-60 dated September 30, 2024 by extending the API-based integration between stock exchanges to additional XBRL-based disclosures. The new capability becomes available **from May 5, 2026** for certain events, while some other disclosure categories were already brought into the single-filing utility on earlier dates in **2024 and 2025** as listed in the notice. The practical compliance effect is that, for covered filings, a listed entity can file once through the integrated system and have the disclosure shared across exchanges, rather than separately filing on each exchange, subject to the category-specific availability noted below.

For **May 5, 2026**, the system is extended to cover, for applicable entities, **Initiation of forensic audit** under Regulation 30 read with sub-para 17 of Para A Part A of Schedule III; **Prohibition of Insider Trading** reporting under Regulation 7(2) of the SEBI PIT Regulations; **Outcome of Board Meeting for dividend, buyback, bonus, and voluntary delisting events** under Regulation 30 read with sub-para 4 of Para A; **Agreements/Contracts/Arrangements/MOU** disclosures under Regulation 30 read with sub-paras 5 and 5A; **Notice of shareholders’ meeting** under sub-para 12; **Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process events** under sub-para 16; **issuance/allotment/alteration/restriction on transferability of securities** under sub-para 2; **award/bagging/receipt/amendment/termination of orders not in the normal course of business** under sub-para 4 of Para B; **loss of share certificate / issue of duplicate share certificate** under Regulation 39; **annual report in XBRL** under Regulation 34; **acquisition/amalgamation/merger/demerger/sale or disposal/other restructuring** under sub-para 1; **changes in directors, KMPs, senior management, auditors, compliance officer, registrar and share transfer agent** under sub-paras 7 and 8, with the utility specifically allowing submission of resignation details and resignation letters required under sub-paras **7A, 7B and 7C**; **resignation of statutory auditor** under sub-para 7A; and **resignation of independent director/director/KMP/SMP/compliance officer** under sub-paras 7B and 7C.

The notice also records earlier rollout dates for other filing types: **Annual Report – XBRL** from **April 20, 2026**; **Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report** from **March 31, 2026**; **Prior intimation for Board Meeting** from **March 7, 2026**; **Fraud/Default/Arrest** from **February 21, 2026**; **Integrated Filing – Financials** from **January 3, 2026**; **Annual Secretarial Compliance Report** from **September 15, 2025**; **Integrated Filing (Governance)** from **March 1, 2025**; **Meetings of shareholders and voting results** from **December 28, 2024**; and **Reconciliation of Share Capital Audit Report** from **November 15, 2024**. The notice also references already-covered categories such as **closure of trading window**, **corporate debt restructuring**, **resolution plans/restructuring for bank/financial institution borrowings and OTS**, and **Issue Summary Document for buyback open and tender route**, with the integration intended for listed entities using XBRL or other prescribed digital filing formats.

Applicability is specified by entity type in the table: many disclosures are available for **only equity** and **equity + debt** listed companies, while some are also shown as available for **REITs and INVITs** where marked. The notice therefore requires compliance teams to check the category of each event and the entity type before relying on single-filing functionality, because not every disclosure is available for every class of issuer, and some entries in the table indicate that availability for certain entity categories will be communicated later. In short, this is an operational filing-system update rather than a new substantive disclosure rule, but it materially changes the filing process for covered disclosures and should be built into internal event-reporting and compliance workflows from the specified effective dates.

rows.summary:
This notice updates the “single filing system” by extending the API-based integration between stock exchanges to additional XBRL filings, effective **April 25, 2026**. The immediate compliance change is that listed entities covered by the specified categories may now submit certain disclosures once through the integrated utility/API and have them flow through the single filing system, rather than filing separately with each exchange, subject to the entity-type applicability shown in the notice.

For **equity-listed and equity+debt listed companies**, the expanded API-enabled disclosures from **April 25, 2026** include: outcome of board meeting for **dividend, buyback, bonus, and voluntary delisting** under **Regulation 30 read with para A(4) of Schedule III**; **agreements/contracts/arrangements/MOUs** under **Regulation 30 read with para A(5) and (5A)**; **notice of shareholders’ meetings** under **Regulation 30 read with para A(12)**; **corporate insolvency resolution process events** under **Regulation 30 read with para A(16)**; **issuance/allotment/alteration/restriction on transferability of securities** under **Regulation 30 read with para A(2)**; **awards/orders not in the ordinary course of business** under **Regulation 30 read with para B(4)**; **loss of share certificate / issue of duplicate share certificate** under **Regulation 39**; **annual report XBRL** under **Regulation 34**; **acquisition/amalgamation/merger/de-merger/sale or disposal/other restructuring** under **Regulation 30 read with para A(1)**; and **changes in directors, KMPs (including MD, CEO, CFO, CS, etc.), senior management, and related resignation filings** under **Regulation 30 read with para A(7), (8), (7A), (7B), and (7C)**. The notice specifically says the utility also provides an option for the **Auditor and Compliance Officer / Registrar and Share Transfer Agent** to submit the details of resignation and the resignation letters required under **sub-paras 7A, 7B, and 7C**.

Several filing categories already have earlier effective dates and continue under the single filing system for **equity and equity+debt** listed companies: **Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR)** under **Regulation 34(2)(f)** effective **March 31, 2026**; **prior intimation for board meeting** under **Regulation 29** effective **March 7, 2026**; **fraud/default/arrest** under **Regulation 30 read with para A(6)** effective **February 21, 2026**; **integrated filing – financials** under **Regulation 23(9), Regulation 30 read with Section V-B of the Master Circular, and Regulations 32(1) and 33(3)** effective **January 3, 2026**; **meetings of shareholders and voting results** under **Regulation 44(3)** effective **December 28, 2024**; **reconciliation of share capital audit report** under **Regulation 76** effective **November 15, 2024**; and **corporate governance report** under **Regulation 27(2)** effective **March 1, 2025**. The notice also includes **closure of trading window** filings under the **SEBI PIT Regulations** as part of the single filing utility, and lists **corporate debt restructuring**, **resolution plans/restructuring relating to loans or borrowings from banks/financial institutions (including Inter-Creditors Agreement and OTS)**, and **Issue Summary Document (ISD) for buyback via open and tender route** as additional API-integrated filing types for the applicable equity/equity+debt entities.

The applicability table indicates that these API-based single filings are generally available for **Only Equity** and **Equity+Debt** listed companies, while the table shows **no applicability** for **Exclusively Debt** and **REITs/InvITs** for the newly listed items shown in the notice. The effective dates are staggered by category, so compliance teams should map each disclosure type to its specific go-live date rather than assuming one universal date. The notice is an extension of the earlier exchange notice **No. 20240930-60 dated September 30, 2024**, and the operational requirement is to use the exchange-provided single filing/API integration for the covered disclosures once the relevant effective date has arrived.

rows.summary:
This notice extends the stock-exchange “single filing system” based on API integration to additional XBRL disclosures, effective April 20, 2026, for all listed entities, with the applicability matrix differing by issuer type. The update adds single-filing functionality for: Annual Report in XBRL under Regulation 34 for equity and equity+debt listed entities; corporate actions such as acquisition, amalgamation, merger, de-merger, sale/disposal, and other restructuring under Regulation 30 read with Para A, Part A, sub-para 1 of Schedule III; changes in directors, KMPs (including MD, CEO, CFO, Company Secretary), senior management, auditor, compliance officer, registrar/transfer agent under Regulation 30 read with Schedule III sub-paras 7 and 8; resignation of statutory auditor under sub-para 7A; resignation of independent director/director/KMP/SMP/compliance officer under sub-paras 7B and 7C; and several other disclosure types listed below, again only for equity and equity+debt companies unless otherwise stated. The notice also extends single filing for closure of trading window under SEBI PIT Regulations; fraud/default/arrest disclosures under Regulation 30 Schedule III sub-para 6; corporate debt restructuring and loan/borrowing restructuring/one-time settlement disclosures under Regulation 30 Schedule III sub-paras 9 and 10; issue summary document for buyback under the SEBI circular on ISD; integrated filing – financials under Regulations 23(9), 30 read with Section V-B of the Master Circular, 32(1), and 33(3) from January 3, 2026; annual secretarial compliance report under Regulation 24A(2) from September 15, 2025; integrated filing (governance) under Regulations 13(3), 27(2), and 30 from March 1, 2025; shareholder meeting/voting results under Regulation 44(3) from December 28, 2024; reconciliation of share capital audit report under Regulation 76 from November 15, 2024; and corporate governance/investor grievance reporting in the earlier framework from October 26, 2024 and October 1, 2024 respectively, though governance reporting was merged into Integrated Filing – Governance pursuant to the SEBI circular dated December 31, 2024.  

The notice also provides important exclusions and continued obligations: for certain items marked with an asterisk, listed entities must continue PDF filing at both exchanges and those disclosures are not yet covered under single filing until further notice. Specifically, this continued PDF-only treatment applies to Regulation 29, Regulation 30, Regulation 34(1)(a), and trading window disclosures, even though some of these are partly covered in the single-filing system for the limited XBRL events listed in the table. For Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report under Regulation 34(2)(f), effective March 31, 2026, the entity must continue PDF filing at both exchanges because it is not covered by single filing, even though the notice shows XBRL availability for equity and equity+debt companies.  

The notice is also explicit that, except for the newly listed XBRL events above, all other disclosures under Regulations 29, 30, and 34 not included in the table must still be filed separately on all exchanges, in both PDF and XBRL wherever applicable. The applicability table shows no single-filing coverage for exclusively debt issuers or REITs/InvITs for the newly added items shown here, and the “√” marks indicate the feature is available only for equity and equity+debt listed companies. Companies should therefore review whether each disclosure falls within the newly enabled API-based single-filing categories or remains subject to the existing dual-filing requirement, and should continue to make PDF filings at both exchanges wherever the notice expressly says single filing does not yet apply.

rows.title: Master Circular for compliance with the provisions of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015 on non-compliance with the Minimum Public Shareholding (MPS) requirements
rows.desc: NOTICE NoticeNo. 20260409-3 NoticeDate 09Apr2026 Category CircularsListedCompanies Segment Equity Department ListingCompliance-Monitoring Subject MasterCircularforcompliancewiththeprovisionsoftheSEBI (LODR)Regulations,2015onnon-compliancewiththeMinimum PublicShareholding(MPS)requirements Attachments RelaxationfromtheapplicabilityofSEBIMasterCircularLODR To All Listed Companies This has reference to the SEBI circular No. HO/49/14/14(13)2026-CFD-POD2/ I/8772/2026 dated April 07, 2026, regarding relaxation from the applicability of SEBI Master Circular for compliance with the provisions of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 on non-compliance with the Minimum Public Shareholding (MPS) requirements. On account of capital market volatility arising from ongoing geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, SEBI decided to grant one-time relaxation from the applicability of penal provisions under the Master Circular for listed entities whose due date for compliance with MPS requirements falls during the period from April 1, 2026, to September 30, 2026. The circular shall be applicable with immediate effect. The aforesaid circular is attached for reference. All listed company are requested to take note and comply accordingly. Yours faithfully, Jayshree Soni Shyam Bhagirath Deputy Vice President - Listing Compliance Manager -Listing Compliance
rows.summary:
This circular advises all listed companies of a one-time SEBI relaxation from the penal provisions in the SEBI Master Circular governing non-compliance with the Minimum Public Shareholding (MPS) requirements under the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015. The relaxation was issued by SEBI through circular No. HO/49/14/14(13)2026-CFD-POD2/I/8772/2026 dated April 07, 2026, and is specifically linked to capital market volatility caused by ongoing geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. It applies only to listed entities whose due date for meeting MPS requirements falls between April 1, 2026 and September 30, 2026.

The practical effect is that the penal provisions under the Master Circular will not be applied to those entities during that window, providing a temporary compliance relief from the usual sanctions for MPS shortfall. The notice states that the circular is effective immediately, meaning listed companies should assess whether their MPS compliance deadline falls within the April 1, 2026 to September 30, 2026 period and, if so, rely on the relaxation for purposes of penalty exposure. No separate filing procedure, threshold change, or new compliance deadline is created in this notice; instead, it instructs all listed companies to take note of the SEBI relaxation and comply accordingly.

This notice updates the Stock Exchanges’ “single filing system” through API-based integration, extending it to additional XBRL-based disclosures from **March 31, 2026** onward. For **equity and equity+debt listed companies**, the single-filing/API process will now apply to the **Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR)** under **Regulation 34(2)(f) of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015**; however, the notice specifically states that **PDF filing of the BRSR will continue at both Exchanges** and it is **not covered under single filing until further notice**. The notice also shows that single filing already applies, for eligible listed entities, to several other disclosures with their respective effective dates, including **Prior Intimation for Board Meeting under Regulation 29** (effective **March 7, 2026**), **Fraud/Default/Arrest disclosures under Regulation 30 / Para A(6) of Schedule III** (effective **February 21, 2026**), **Integrated Filing – Financials** (effective **January 3, 2026**), **Annual Secretarial Compliance Report under Regulation 24A(2)** (effective **September 15, 2025**), **Integrated Filing (Governance)** (effective **March 1, 2025**), **Shareholders’ meeting and voting results under Regulation 44(3)** (effective **December 28, 2024**), **Reconciliation of Share Capital Audit Report under Regulation 76** (effective **November 15, 2024**), and **Investor Grievance Report under Regulation 13(3)** (effective **October 1, 2024**, noted as pursuant to the SEBI circular dated **December 31, 2024**).  

The notice distinguishes between categories of listed entities: for many of the listed disclosures, the table indicates applicability to **only equity** and **equity+debt** listed companies, while **exclusively debt listed companies, REITs, and INVITs** are generally marked as not covered for the items shown. It also identifies several disclosures that remain outside single filing and still require separate submissions on all Exchanges: **Regulation 29 and Regulation 30 disclosures and trading window closure disclosures** must continue to be filed in **PDF at both Exchanges**, and for non-XBRL events not included in the table, listed entities must continue submitting the required **PDF and XBRL filings separately on all Exchanges** wherever applicable. The notice further clarifies that **Corporate Governance Report under Regulation 27(2)** has been **merged into “Integrated Filing – Governance”** and that the Exchanges will communicate the effective date for some items later, including **Integrated Filing – Financials**, **Annual Secretarial Compliance Report**, **Integrated Filing (Governance)**, and **Investor Grievance Report** for the categories shown as “shall be communicated later.”  

Operationally, the Exchanges are instructing listed entities to **avoid multiple filings of the same disclosure on both Exchanges** because the purpose of the API-based single filing framework is to enable one filing to be shared between exchanges. If, after submission, **any one Exchange seeks clarification**, the listed entity must respond **only to the Exchange that raised the query**. Compliance teams should therefore ensure their filing workflows distinguish between disclosures that are now part of single filing, disclosures still requiring separate PDF/XBRL submissions, and disclosures for which the single-filing coverage remains limited or deferred; for questions, the notice directs listed entities to contact the BSE helpdesk or email **bse.regulation30@bseindia.com**.

rows.title: Adherence to Compliance Requirements for Handling Unpublished Price Sensitive Information (UPSI) under the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015
rows.desc: Non-Confidential Circular Department: LISTING Circular Ref. No.: NSE/CML/2026/19 Date: August 07, 2026 To, All Listed Entities Subject: Adherence to Compliance Requirements for Handling Unpublished Price Sensitive Information (UPSI) under the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 Suggested Best Practices SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 “(PIT Regulations)”, as amended from time to time, and the relevant circulars issued by SEBI and the Stock Exchanges detail, inter-alia, the manner in which the listed companies are required to deal with Unpublished Price Sensitive Information (UPSI). The provisions of the PIT Regulations are further supplemented and clarified through the Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) issued by SEBI. In light of the observations made in certain cases, it is considered imperative that listed companies diligently adhere to best practices to ensure full compliance with the PIT Regulations as amended from time to time including the following: 1. Listed companies shall maintain a structured digital database containing the nature of UPSI, the names and PANs (or any other identifier authorized by law) of persons who have shared the information, and the names and PANs of persons with whom such information has been shared. In case where UPSI is shared with a listed company, intermediaries, or fiduciaries, the names and identifier of the individuals handling such information shall be recorded. 2. Listed companies shall diligently implement and periodically review internal policies designed to prevent the leakage of UPSI. Such measures must be in alignment with the statutory and regulatory provisions prescribed under the PIT Regulations. 3. To ensure a culture of compliance, companies shall conduct periodic training and awareness programs for all employees and fiduciaries regarding the prescribed manner of handling UPSI. 4. Listed companies shall ensure compliance with the Code of Conduct formulated by the company with respect to the PIT Regulations, ensuring that the same is effectively operationalized. 5. Listed entities are advised to implement any other such measures as may be necessary to ensure that the objectives of the PIT Regulations are achieved. This is for your information please. For and on behalf of National Stock Exchange of India Limited Mandar Walavalkar Vice President
rows.summary:
This circular, dated **August 07, 2026** and issued as **NSE/CML/2026/19** by the National Stock Exchange of India Limited to **all listed entities**, reiterates and emphasizes compliance expectations for handling **Unpublished Price Sensitive Information (UPSI)** under the **SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 (PIT Regulations)**, as amended, together with SEBI and stock exchange circulars and SEBI FAQs. It does **not** create a new quantified threshold, filing deadline, or rate, but it reinforces that listed companies must strictly follow existing PIT requirements and “best practices” in light of compliance observations made in certain cases.

A key requirement highlighted is that listed companies must maintain a **structured digital database** recording: the **nature of the UPSI**, the **names and PANs (or any other legally authorized identifier)** of persons who shared the information, and the **names and PANs** of persons with whom the information was shared. Where UPSI is shared with a **listed company, intermediary, or fiduciary**, the database must also capture the **names and identifiers of the individuals actually handling the information**.

The circular also says listed companies must **diligently implement and periodically review internal policies** designed to prevent UPSI leakage, and those policies must align with the statutory and regulatory framework under the PIT Regulations. In addition, companies must conduct **periodic training and awareness programs** for **all employees and fiduciaries** on the prescribed manner of handling UPSI, to build a culture of compliance.

Finally, listed entities are instructed to ensure their **company-specific Code of Conduct under the PIT Regulations is actually operationalized**, not merely adopted on paper, and to implement **any other measures necessary** to achieve the objectives of the PIT Regulations. The document is framed as an informational reminder rather than a new enforcement rule, but compliance teams should treat it as a prompt to confirm that UPSI registers, identifier capture, policy review cycles, training programs, and Code of Conduct implementation are all in place and functioning effectively.

rows.summary:
This NSE FAQ document explains how listed companies must file and manage **Record Date** disclosures for corporate actions under **Regulation 42 of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015**. The key compliance point is that **all listed entities** may fix a Record Date for a corporate action, but for **InvITs and REITs** the Record Date must be disclosed under the applicable SEBI regulations **at least two working days before the Record Date**, excluding both the date of intimation and the Record Date itself.

For filing on NSE’s **NEAPS** platform, the intimation must be submitted only through **NEAPS > COMPLIANCE > Announcements > Corporate Action > Submission**. The FAQ is explicit that submissions made through any other path will **not be taken on record**. It also states that, under the updated approach, the Exchange will recognize **only the Record Date**; companies should **not rely on or substitute a cut-off date or book closure date**. Simply selecting the “Record Date” radio button or uploading a PDF that does not expressly state “Record Date” does **not** satisfy Regulation 42, and any submission that refers to “cut-off date” or “book closure date” instead of “Record Date” will be rejected and may attract an **applicable fine**.

The document clarifies that companies do **not** need to set a record date for an **AGM or EGM**, because such meetings are **not treated as a corporate action by the Exchange**. It also says that if a company needs to **revise or cancel** an already-intimated Record Date, it may do so on NEAPS only if the revision/cancellation is submitted **at least two working days before the previously intimated Record Date**; otherwise, the change will not be recorded. Any revised intimation or cancellation must again be routed through the same NEAPS corporate action submission path and must remain compliant with Regulation 42.

The FAQ further states that the Record Date under **Regulation 42(2)** cannot be the same date as the board meeting scheduled to decide the corporate action under **Regulation 42(1)**; instead, there must be a **minimum gap of three working days after board or shareholder approval, as applicable**. For **capital reduction, schemes, restructuring, and similar actions**, the document indicates that a Record Date cannot be intimated on only **3 days’ notice**; more advance notice is required, although the excerpt provided cuts off before giving the exact timing rule. The document is marked **updated on 07/07/2026**, and it includes a circular reference dated **07/02/2025** for the detailed Exchange notice supporting these requirements.

rows.title: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) on the submission of the Quarterly Integrated Filing – Governance
rows.desc: 1 Circular Department: Listing Circular Ref No: NSE/CML/2026/16 Date: June 12, 2026 To, All Listed Entities, Sub: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) on the submission of the Quarterly Integrated Filing – Governance. With reference to the submission of Integrated Filing – Governance (Formerly known as Corporate Governance Report), please find annexed the Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) for your reference and guidance purpose. All the listed entities are requested to take note of the same and comply accordingly. For and on behalf of National Stock Exchange of India Limited Raksha Jain Senior Manager Encl: Annexure - FAQs 2 ANNEXURE Disclaimer: These guidelines are issued for guidance purpose only for submission of the quarterly Integrated Filing – Governance via XBRL utility. These guidelines are not and should not be construed as substitution/clarification/explanation on any matter on which provision of Law, Regulation or SEBI/Exchange circular were issued. FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS Sr. No. Particulars Page no. 1. General Submission Requirements 3 - 4 2. Part- I: Composition of Board of Directors 5 - 9 3 Part -II: Composition of Committees 10 4. Part -III: Meeting of Board of Directors 11 5. Part- IV: Meeting of Committees 12 6. Part V: Others 13 - 14 7. 1. Quarterly disclosures: Under Schedule III of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015 15 - 16 3 General Submission Requirements: a. What is the due date for submission of the quarterly Integrated Filing – Governance Report? Integrated Filing – Governance Report shall be submitted within 30 days from the end of each quarter as prescribed under Regulation 27 (2) of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations. b. From which date should a newly listed entity shall submit the Integrated Filing – Governance Report? A newly listed entity is required to submit the Integrated Filing – Governance report from the quarter ending immediately after the date of listing. c. What are the conditions under Regulation 4 of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015 for dissemination of adequate and timely information to recognized stock exchange(s)? The following provisions are to be taken care of by the companies while submitting the Integrated Governance report: 4(1)(d) the listed entity shall provide adequate and timely information to recognized stock exchange(s) and investors. 4(1)(e) the listed entity shall ensure that disseminations made under provisions of these regulations and circulars made thereunder, are adequate, accurate, explicit, timely and presented in a simple language. 4(1)(i) filings, reports, statements, documents and information which are event based or are filed periodically shall contain relevant information. d. Whether Corporate Governance provisions are applicable to SME Listed entities and how does Regulation 280 of SEBI (ICDR) Regulations impact? As per regulation 280 of SEBI (ICDR) Regulations 2018 as amended on March 8, 2025, if a listed SME’s post issue paid up exceeds Rupees 25 crore, it shall comply with corporate governance provisions under SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015 including submission of the Integrated Filing – Governance Report. 4 e. What are the conditions stipulated under the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015 for the continued applicability and compliance of Corporate Governance provisions by Listed entities? As per Regulation 15 of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015 once corporate governance provisions as specified in regulations 17 to 27, clauses (b) to (a) and (t) of sub-regulation (2) of regulation 46 and para C, D and E of Schedule V become applicable to a listed entity, they shall continue to remain applicable till such time the equity share capital and the net-worth of such entity reduces and remains below the specified threshold for a period of three consecutive financial years, even if they subsequently fall outside the specified ranking. f. When will Corporate Governance provisions under SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015 become applicable to a listed entity entering the Top 1000/Top 2000 based on Average market capitalization for the first time? For a listed entity entering the Top 1000/Top 2000 based on average market capitalization, the corporate governance provisions shall become effective after a period of three months from December 31 (i.e., April 1) or from the beginning of the immediately next financial year, whichever is later. Illustration: Particulars Financial year ending March June September December Average market capitalisation December 31 Status of the listed entity Enters Top 1000/2000 for first time Date of applicability for Top 1000/2000 Corporate Governance provisions April 01 July 01 October 01 April 01 5 Part- I: Composition of Board of Directors 1. What should be mentioned if DIN is not available to a director? If DIN is not available for the Director(s), the Company needs to mention the dummy DIN (99999999), along with the detailed reason in remark column for not having DIN. 2. What should be mentioned if PAN is not applicable to a director(s)
rows.summary:
This NSE circular (Ref. No. **NSE/CML/2026/16**, dated **June 12, 2026**) advises all listed entities that the **Quarterly Integrated Filing – Governance** (formerly the **Corporate Governance Report**) must be submitted using the **XBRL utility**, and that the attached FAQs are for guidance only. The circular expressly says the FAQs are **not a substitute for the SEBI/Exchange law, regulations, or circulars**, so listed entities must still comply with the underlying legal provisions even if the FAQ language is incomplete or interpretive. NSE directs all listed entities to note the guidance and comply accordingly.

The FAQs reiterate the core filing deadline: the **Integrated Filing – Governance Report is due within 30 days from the end of each quarter**, as required under **Regulation 27(2) of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015**. A **newly listed entity** must begin filing from the **quarter ending immediately after its listing date**. The document also reminds companies of the governance disclosure principles in **Regulation 4**—filings to stock exchanges and investors must be **adequate, timely, accurate, explicit, and in simple language**, and periodic or event-based filings must contain **relevant information**.

The FAQs clarify when corporate governance compliance applies to **SME-listed entities**: under **Regulation 280 of the SEBI (ICDR) Regulations, 2018**, as amended on **March 8, 2025**, if a listed SME’s **post-issue paid-up capital exceeds ₹25 crore**, it must comply with the corporate governance provisions of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, including the **Integrated Filing – Governance Report**. They also state that once governance provisions under **Regulation 15** become applicable to a listed entity—covering **Regulations 17 to 27**, specified clauses of **Regulation 46(2)**, and **Paragraphs C, D, and E of Schedule V**—those obligations continue until the entity’s **equity share capital and net worth** fall below the relevant threshold and remain below it for **three consecutive financial years**.

For entities moving into the governance regime because of market-cap ranking, the FAQs say that if a listed company enters the **Top 1000/Top 2000 by average market capitalisation for the first time**, corporate governance provisions become effective **after three months from December 31 (i.e., April 1) or from the beginning of the immediately next financial year, whichever is later**. The included illustration shows that, depending on the quarter-end, the applicability date can fall on **April 1, July 1, October 1, or April 1** based on when the ranking threshold is first crossed. This means companies should monitor their average market capitalisation at year-end and be prepared for a delayed but automatic compliance trigger.

The FAQs also begin detailed data-entry instructions for the governance filing, including what to do if a director does **not have a DIN**: the company must enter the dummy DIN **99999999** and provide the **reason in the remarks column**. The document content provided cuts off before the remaining FAQs, but the visible material makes clear that listed entities should use the XBRL-based quarterly governance filing, follow the specified deadlines, and determine applicability based on listing status, SME paid-up capital, market-cap ranking, and continuing applicability under Regulation 15.

rows.title:
Pre-Packaged Insolvency Resolution Process under Section 54L of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy 
Code, 2016.
rows.desc: National Stock Exchange of India Circular Department: Listing Circular Ref. No.: NSE/CML/2026/15 Date: June 01, 2026 To All Listed Companies, Sub: Pre-Packaged Insolvency Resolution Process under Section 54L of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016. Attention is invited to the provisions relating to Pre-Packaged Insolvency Resolution Process (“PPIRP”) under Chapter III-A of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 (“IBC”). In this regard, as advised by SEBI, it is clarified that, the exemptions available under various SEBI Regulations in respect of a Resolution Plan approved under Section 31 of the IBC are not available in case of a Resolution Plan approved under Section 54L of the IBC under the PPIRP framework. Accordingly, listed entities undergoing PPIRP shall be required to comply with all applicable procedural and regulatory requirements prescribed under the relevant SEBI Regulations. The listed companies are advised to take note of the above and ensure compliance of the same. For and on behalf of National Stock Exchange of India Limited Yukti Sharma Head - Listing
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India, by Listing Circular Ref. No. NSE/CML/2026/15 dated June 1, 2026, has clarified the compliance treatment for listed companies undergoing a Pre-Packaged Insolvency Resolution Process (PPIRP) under Chapter III-A / Section 54L of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016. The key change is that the regulatory exemptions that are available under various SEBI regulations when a resolution plan is approved under Section 31 of the IBC do **not** apply where a resolution plan is approved under Section 54L in the PPIRP framework. In practical terms, any listed entity that enters PPIRP must not assume any relaxed treatment available for ordinary IBC resolution plans approved under Section 31; instead, it must comply with **all applicable procedural and regulatory requirements** under the relevant SEBI regulations.

For compliance teams, this means listed companies in PPIRP should review the specific SEBI rules that would otherwise grant exemptions in a standard IBC resolution and ensure they are fully observed throughout the PPIRP process and upon approval of the resolution plan. The circular does not introduce a new deadline, monetary threshold, or specific filing form, but it does impose an immediate compliance expectation from the date of the circular onward for all listed entities affected by PPIRP. The NSE’s instruction is effectively a notice to listed companies to take note and ensure compliance without relying on Section 31-based exemption relief in the PPIRP context.

rows.title: Filing of disclosures in XBRL format under Regulation 7(2) and Regulation 7(3) of SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015
rows.desc: National Stock Exchange of India Circular Department: Listing Circular Ref. No.: NSE/CML/2026/12 Date: May 04, 2026 To, The Company Secretary, All Listed Entities Subject: Filing of disclosures in XBRL format under Regulation 7(2) and Regulation 7(3) of SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 Dear Sir/Madam, This is to inform you that disclosures under Regulation 7(2) and Regulation 7(3) of SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 were previously being filed through the following path: NEAPS  Compliance  Disclosures  Insider Trading The above-mentioned filing path has now been discontinued, and a new XBRL based utility has been introduced for submission of such disclosures. Accordingly, all listed companies, REITs and InvITs are required to submit the aforesaid disclosure only in XBRL format through the revised process as detailed below: To download XBRL utility: NEAPS  Compliance  Download XBRL Utilities For Submission of disclosures: NEAPS  Compliance  Common XBRL Upload  Prohibition of Insider Trading Please note that previously filed disclosures shall continue to be available at the following link: https://www.nseindia.com/companies-listing/corporate-filings-insider-trading-archive-data Further, with reference to Exchange Circular No. NSE/CML/2026/11 dated May 04, 2026, the said utility will also be available for Single Filing system through API-based integration. You are requested to take note of the above and ensure compliance. Yours faithfully, For National Stock Exchange of India Limited Harshad Dharod Chief Manager-Listing Compliance
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India has changed the filing process for disclosures required under Regulation 7(2) and Regulation 7(3) of the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015. The earlier NEAPS filing path — **NEAPS → Compliance → Disclosures → Insider Trading** — has been **discontinued** and replaced with a **new XBRL-based utility** for submission of these disclosures.

This requirement applies to **all listed companies, REITs, and InvITs**, which must now file the relevant insider-trading disclosures **only in XBRL format** through the revised NEAPS workflow. For downloading the utility, entities must use **NEAPS → Compliance → Download XBRL Utilities**; for submission, they must use **NEAPS → Compliance → Common XBRL Upload → Prohibition of Insider Trading**. The circular does not specify a new filing deadline or change the underlying statutory reporting timelines, but it does impose a new mandatory filing method.

Previously filed disclosures will continue to be accessible at the NSE archive link provided in the circular: **https://www.nseindia.com/companies-listing/corporate-filings-insider-trading-archive-data**. The circular also notes that, in reference to **NSE Circular No. NSE/CML/2026/11 dated May 04, 2026**, the same utility will be available for **Single Filing system through API-based integration**, which is relevant for entities using automated filing processes. Compliance teams should update internal filing procedures immediately to ensure all future Regulation 7(2) and 7(3) disclosures are submitted through the new XBRL process and not through the discontinued path.

rows.summary:
This circular updates the **single filing system through API-based integration between stock exchanges** under the framework introduced by **Exchange Circular NSE/CML/2024/28 dated September 30, 2024**. The main change is that the system is being **extended to cover additional XBRL and non-confidential filings**, so listed entities can submit the relevant disclosure once and have it routed through the integrated exchange mechanism. The circular is addressed to **all listed entities** and is issued by NSE on **May 04, 2026**.

For **XBRL filings**, the single filing/API-based utility is now available for the following disclosures, with the stated effective dates: **Outcome of Board Meeting for dividend, buyback, bonus, and voluntary delisting events** under **Regulation 30 / Schedule III para A part A sub-para 4** effective **April 25, 2026**; **Annual Report – XBRL** under **Regulation 34** effective **April 20, 2026**; **Initiation of forensic audit** under **Regulation 30 / Schedule III para A part A sub-para 17** effective **May 05, 2026**; and **Prohibition of Insider Trading disclosures** under **Regulation 7(2) and 7(3) of the SEBI PIT Regulations, 2015** effective **May 05, 2026**. The XBRL table indicates applicability for **only equity**, **equity + debt**, and, for the PIT disclosure, also **REITs and INVITs**; the table uses check marks to show which entity types are covered, so compliance teams should verify whether their listed entity falls within the applicable columns before relying on the API route.

For **non-confidential filings**, the circular states that the utility now covers a broader set of regulatory disclosures for **only equity** and **equity + debt** listed entities, including: **acquisition/amalgamation/merger/demerger/sale/disposal/other restructuring** under **Regulation 30 / Schedule III para A part A sub-para 1**; **changes in directors, KMPs, senior management, auditor, compliance officer, registrar and share transfer agent** under **Regulation 30 / Schedule III sub-para 7 and 8**; **resignations of statutory auditors** under **sub-para 7A**; **resignation of independent directors, directors, KMPs, SMPs, and compliance officers** under **sub-para 7B and 7C**; **Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report** under **Regulation 34(2)(f)** effective **March 31, 2026**; **prior intimation for board meeting** under **Regulation 29** effective **March 07, 2026**; **closure of trading window** under the **SEBI PIT Regulations**; **fraud/default/arrest** under **Regulation 30 / Schedule III sub-para 6** effective **February 21, 2026**; **corporate debt restructuring** under **Regulation 30 / Schedule III sub-para 9 and 10**; **resolution plans/restructuring relating to bank/FI loans and borrowings and one-time settlement (OTS)**; and **Issue Summary Document (ISD) for buyback via open and tender route** under the SEBI circular on ISD and issue advertisements. The utility also covers **Integrated Filing – Financials** under **Regulation 23(9), Regulation 30 read with Section V-B of the Master Circular, Regulation 32(1), and Regulation 33(3)** effective **January 03, 2026**, **Annual Secretarial Compliance Report** under **Regulation 24A(2)** effective **September 15, 2025**, and **Integrated Filing (Governance)** under **Regulations 13(3), 27(2), and 30** effective **March 01, 2025**; the circular notes that for some of these integrated filing items the applicability for **exclusively debt** entities and **REITs/INVITs** will be **communicated later**.

A specific procedural clarification is included for resignation-related filings: the utility **provides an option to submit the resignation details and the resignation letter(s)** as required under **sub-paras 7A, 7B and 7C of Schedule III, Part A, Para A**, so companies should ensure those supporting documents are attached when using the single-filing route. The circular does not change the underlying disclosure obligations under SEBI regulations; instead, it changes the **filing method** by expanding the set of events that can be submitted through the API-based single filing system. Compliance teams should therefore update filing workflows, confirm the entity-type applicability for each event, and use the new single-filing route from the relevant effective dates onward.

rows.title: XBRL based filing for Violations related to Code of Conduct (CoC) under SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015
rows.desc: National Stock Exchange of India Circular Department: Listing Circular Ref. No.: NSE/CML/2026/13 Date: May 04, 2026 To, The Company Secretary, All Listed Entities/Intermediaries/Fiduciaries Subject: XBRL based filing for Violations related to Code of Conduct (CoC) under SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 SEBI vide Circular No. SEBI/HO/ISD/ISD/CIR/P/2020/135 dated July 23, 2020, prescribed the format for reporting violations of the Code of Conduct under SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015. To enhance accuracy and efficiency in disclosures, the Exchange has introduced an XBRL utility for reporting such violations through NEAPS with effect from May 05, 2026. All Listed Companies/Intermediaries/Fiduciaries shall submit the reporting through the following paths: To download XBRL utility: NEAPS  Compliance  Download XBRL Utilities For Submissions: NEAPS  Compliance  Common XBRL Upload  Violation of Code of Conduct under SEBI (PIT) Regulations, 2015 It may be noted that reporting by listed entities shall be made only in XBRL mode without submission of any PDF. Further, any unlisted entity reporting in the capacity of Intermediary or Fiduciary shall continue to submit the disclosures through email at pit_coc@nse.co.in, as per Exchange Circular No. NSE/CML/2020/44 dated August 26, 2020. The disclosure pertaining to violations of the Code of Conduct shall not be disseminated on the Exchange website. All listed entities are advised to mandatorily submit the reporting through NEAPS only. Submission through any other mode shall not be taken on record and shall be considered invalid. Listed entities, Intermediaries and Fiduciaries are advised to take note of the above and comply accordingly. Yours faithfully, For National Stock Exchange of India Limited Harshad Dharod Chief Manager-Listing Compliance
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) has introduced a new **XBRL-based filing process** for reporting **violations of the Code of Conduct (CoC)** under the **SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015**, replacing the prior non-XBRL reporting approach for listed entities. This change is intended to improve the accuracy and efficiency of disclosures and becomes **effective from May 5, 2026**.

For **all listed companies, intermediaries, and fiduciaries**, the filing must be handled through **NEAPS**. The circular specifies the workflow: users should download the XBRL utility via **NEAPS → Compliance → Download XBRL Utilities**, and submit filings via **NEAPS → Compliance → Common XBRL Upload → Violation of Code of Conduct under SEBI (PIT) Regulations, 2015**. For **listed entities**, reporting must be made **only in XBRL mode** and **no PDF submission is permitted**; any submission through another mode will **not be taken on record and will be treated as invalid**.

The circular also preserves the existing treatment for **unlisted entities acting as intermediaries or fiduciaries**: they must continue to submit disclosures **by email to pit_coc@nse.co.in**, in line with **NSE Circular No. NSE/CML/2020/44 dated August 26, 2020**. In addition, the disclosure relating to CoC violations **will not be disseminated on the Exchange website**. Compliance teams should ensure that listed entities switch to the NEAPS XBRL-only process immediately from the effective date and that any non-listed intermediary/fiduciary reporting remains on the email route.

No.: NSE/CML/2026/07 Date: April 10, 2026 Department: LISTING To, All Listed Entities Subject: Ease of doing business - mechanism for lock-in of pledged shares under SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018 Dear Sir/Ma’am, This is with reference to the SEBI Circular No. HO/49/(17)2026-CFD-POD2/I/8965/2026 dated April 08, 2026, issued by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) titled “Ease of doing business - mechanism for lock-in of pledged shares under SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018”. A copy of SEBI Circular dated April 08, 2026, is enclosed for your reference and for necessary action at your end. The copy of the circular is also available on the NSE website (www.nseindia.com). This is for your information please. For and on behalf of National Stock Exchange of India Limited Snehal Mariappa Manager Encl: SEBI Circular
rows.summary:
This NSE circular dated April 10, 2026 is a forwarding notice to all listed entities referencing a SEBI circular dated April 08, 2026 on an “ease of doing business” measure concerning the **mechanism for lock-in of pledged shares under the SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018**. The NSE communication itself does **not** set out the detailed procedure or compliance mechanics; it states that the SEBI circular is enclosed and available on the NSE website, and that listed entities should take “necessary action” as applicable.  

For compliance purposes, the key point is that this is a **share-lock-in/pledge-related regulatory change** affecting listed entities and potentially promoters or other holders whose shares are subject to lock-in requirements and pledge arrangements under the ICDR Regulations. The document does not specify any numeric thresholds, timelines, or filing deadlines in the text provided, so those would need to be taken from the underlying SEBI circular attached to this notice.  

Operationally, a compliance team should treat this as a prompt to review the SEBI circular and assess whether the company has any outstanding pledged shares that are subject to lock-in, whether the depository/registrar and share transfer processes need to be updated, and whether disclosures or confirmations are required to ensure pledges do not conflict with lock-in obligations. The notice also indicates that the circular is effective as of its issuance date at SEBI, **April 08, 2026**, with the NSE forwarding it on **April 10, 2026**.

rows.title: Relaxation from the applicability of SEBI Master Circular for compliance with the provisions of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 on non-compliance with the Minimum Public Shareholding (MPS) requirements.

No.: NSE/CML/2026/06 Date: April 7, 2026 To, All Listed Entities Subject: Relaxation from the applicability of SEBI Master Circular for compliance with the provisions of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 on non-compliance with the Minimum Public Shareholding (MPS) requirements Dear Sir / Madam, This is with reference to the SEBI Circular No. HO/49/14/14(13)2026-CFD-POD2/ I/8772/2026 dated April 07, 2026, issued by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) titled “Relaxation from the applicability of SEBI Master Circular for compliance with the provisions of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 on non- compliance with the Minimum Public Shareholding (MPS) requirements”. A copy of SEBI Circular dated April 07, 2026, is enclosed for your reference and for necessary action at your end. The copy of the circular is also available on the NSE website (www.nseindia.com). This is for your information please. For and on behalf of National Stock Exchange of India Limited Mandar Desai Manager Encl: SEBI Circular
rows.summary:
This circular is an NSE transmission of a SEBI relaxation measure dated April 7, 2026, addressed to all listed entities and linked to compliance with the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 in cases of non-compliance with Minimum Public Shareholding (MPS) requirements. The NSE states that SEBI has issued Circular No. HO/49/14/14(13)2026-CFD-POD2/I/8772/2026 on April 7, 2026, titled “Relaxation from the applicability of SEBI Master Circular for compliance with the provisions of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 on non-compliance with the Minimum Public Shareholding (MPS) requirements,” and the NSE is forwarding that circular for information and necessary action.

From a compliance perspective, the document itself does not set out the substantive relief terms, deadlines, or numeric MPS thresholds; it confirms that SEBI has granted a relaxation from the applicability of the SEBI Master Circular in the context of listed entities that are not meeting the MPS requirement. The affected parties are all listed entities that have an MPS shortfall or are otherwise subject to MPS compliance under the LODR framework. The only explicit date in this NSE communication is April 7, 2026, which is the date of the underlying SEBI circular and the NSE circular reference date (NSE/CML/2026/06). The circular also states that the SEBI circular is enclosed and available on the NSE website, indicating that compliance teams should review the underlying SEBI text directly to determine the exact relaxation conditions and any action items.

rows.summary:
NSE has updated its “single filing system” through API-based integration between stock exchanges, originally introduced under Circular NSE/CML/2024/28 dated September 30, 2024. Effective March 07, 2026, the single-filing mechanism is expanded to cover additional XBRL filings for specified disclosures, but only to the extent expressly listed in the circular and only for the listed entity categories shown in the table.

For **equity-listed entities** and **equity + debt listed entities**, the new single-filing coverage now includes XBRL submissions for: prior intimation of board meeting under Regulation 29 of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015; closure of trading window under the SEBI PIT Regulations; fraud/default/arrest disclosures under Regulation 30 of SEBI LODR and sub-para 6 of Part A of Schedule III; corporate debt restructuring disclosures under Regulation 30 and sub-para 9 and 10 of Part A of Schedule III; resolution plans/restructuring related to bank/financial institution borrowings, inter-creditors agreements, and one-time settlement (OTS); issue summary document (ISD) for buyback via open and tender route; integrated filing–financials under Regulations 23(9), 30 read with Section V-B of the Master Circular, and Regulations 32(1) and 33(3) (effective January 03, 2026); annual secretarial compliance report under Regulation 24A(2) (effective September 15, 2025); integrated filing–governance under Regulations 13(3), 27(2), and 30 (effective March 01, 2025); meetings of shareholders and voting results under Regulation 44(3) (effective December 28, 2024); reconciliation of share capital audit report under Regulation 76 (effective November 15, 2024); corporate governance report under Regulation 27(2) (effective October 26, 2024), which has been merged into Integrated Filing–Governance pursuant to the SEBI circular dated December 31, 2024; and investor grievance report under Regulation 13(3) (effective October 01, 2024).  

The circular makes an important limitation clear: **for Regulation 29, Regulation 30 of SEBI LODR, and trading window disclosures, listed entities must continue filing PDF submissions at both exchanges and these are not yet covered by single filing except for the XBRL events specifically listed in the table**. Likewise, for all other Regulation 29 and Regulation 30 events not included in the table, entities must continue to make submissions separately on all exchanges, in PDF and XBRL where applicable. NSE also instructs listed entities to avoid duplicate filings of the same disclosure on both exchanges, because the objective is to move toward a true single-filing process. If an exchange later asks for clarification after submission, the listed entity must respond only to the exchange that requested it.  

In practical compliance terms, affected listed entities should update their disclosure workflows from March 07, 2026 to route the newly covered XBRL filings through the single-filing/API process for the exact events identified above, while continuing legacy dual filing where the circular expressly says single filing does not yet apply. Questions are to be directed through NEAPS at **NEAPS > Help > Contact Us > Listing Compliance** or by email to **takeover@nse.co.in**.

rows.title: Seeking of comments / feedback on the XBRL being introduced for filing Qualified Institutional Placements (“QIP”)  applications with the Exchange.
rows.desc: National Stock Exchange of India Circular Department: LISTING Circular Ref. No.: NSE/CML/2026/02 Date: February 03, 2026 To, The Company Secretary, All Listed Entities Subject: Seeking of comments / feedback on the XBRL being introduced for filing Qualified Institutional Placements (“QIP”) applications with the Exchange. 1. OBJECTIVE: The objective of this document is to seek comments / feedback on the proposed transition to an XBRL- based framework for filing QIP applications, in lieu of the existing filings which are made through an application-based system, wherein companies manually input the required information and upload documents in PDF format. 2. BACKGROUND: Listed entities are required to seek approval from the Stock Exchange(s) for issuance of securities through “QIP” as laid down in SEBI LODR Regulations, 2015 and SEBI ICDR Regulation 2018 and various applicable relevant provisions, circulars, guidance note, etc. as amended from time to time. . Accordingly, companies are required to submit applications for in-principle approval, post-allotment approval, and trading approval to the Stock Exchange(s). Over a period of time, Stock Exchanges, in a phased manner, have undertaken initiatives to migrate filings made under the SEBI Act, Regulations and circulars from document-based formats to XBRL- based reporting, with an objective to standardize securities market data and enhance regulatory efficiency. It has been deliberated that implementation of an XBRL-based filing mechanism for QIP applications covering “In-Principle approval and Post-Allotment Listing Approval” which would enable submission of standardised, consistent, and homogeneous compliance data to ease the filing process for listed entities as well as facilitate efficient data analysis and monitoring by the Stock Exchange. Accordingly, in this regard, filing of QIP-related information would require listed entities to file the aforesaid applications in XBRL exclusively, formats of which are made available as Annexure A. 3. ISSUES AND DELIBERATIONS: Please note that the details required are typically descriptive in nature and based on the SEBI Regulation or any other disclosure w.r.t. compliance of any SEBI Act, Regulation, Circular or provision. Accordingly, listed entities can provide their comments/ feedback/suggestions/observations pertaining to any additions/modifications in the fields of the attached format. Continuation Sheet 4. COMMENTS FROM LISTED ENTITIES: Considering the implications of the XBRL filing by listed entities, comments in respect of the subject are solicited. Comments may be sent by email to DL-FI@nse.co.in in the following format latest by February 11, 2026. rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India Limited is seeking comments on a proposed move to **XBRL-only filing** for certain **Qualified Institutional Placement (QIP)** applications, replacing the current **application-based process** where companies manually enter data and upload PDFs. The change is aimed at standardizing securities-market data and improving regulatory efficiency, and it would apply to listed entities seeking **QIP approvals** under the SEBI LODR Regulations, 2015 and SEBI ICDR Regulations, 2018, specifically for **in-principle approval** and **post-allotment listing approval** (the circular also references trading approval in the background, though the proposed XBRL framework described is for in-principle and post-allotment filings).

The circular does not immediately impose a final compliance obligation; rather, it **invites listed entities to comment, suggest additions, or propose modifications** to the draft XBRL fields and format. Comments must be emailed to **DL-FI@nse.co.in** **no later than February 11, 2026**, and the email subject must read **“Comments / Feedback on the XBRL being introduced QIP applications with the Exchange.”** The reply format requested by NSE includes the **name of entity/person, contact number and email address, event name (“XBRL filing for QIP”), the field/heading, comments/suggestions, and detailed rationale**.

The draft Annexure A shows the substantive data points that would have to be captured in XBRL for **Qualified Institutions Placement XBRL for Regulation 28(1) – In Principle Approval (Pre Allotment)**. For the issue details, the filing would require disclosure of the **symbol/BSE code/MSEI symbol**, the **exchange(s) where the issuer is listed** (NSE/BSE/MSEI/others, with the specific exchange required if “others” is chosen), the **board resolution date approving the specified securities issue**, the **date of notice to shareholders**, the **date of shareholders’ approval for QIBs**, the **type of security** (dropdown options: **Equity, Non-Convertible Debt and Warrants, Convertible Securities, Units**), the **number of securities and/or amount in INR crores**, the **lead manager**, and the **objects of the issue**. The draft specifies that **either the number of securities or the issue amount must be mandatory**, and the number-of-securities field changes based on the security type selected: for **Equity**, one row for “No. of Equity Securities”; for **Non-Convertible Debt and Warrants**, separate rows for “No. of Non-Convertible Debt Securities” and “No. of Warrants”; for **Convertible Securities**, one row for “No. of Convertible Securities”; and for **Units**, one row for “No. of Units.”

The draft objects-of-issue table indicates the system will require categorization of proceeds by stated purposes such as **capital expenditure, repayment of loan, conversion of loan, working capital requirement, acquisition of the entity, unidentified acquisition, investment in subsidiary/associates/others, and augmentation of capital base of the company**. Overall, the compliance impact for listed entities is that QIP-related approvals would move from narrative/PDF-based submissions to a **structured electronic XBRL data submission**, with the expectation of standardized field-level disclosure once the framework is implemented after this consultation.

rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India has updated its “single filing system” for API-based integration between stock exchanges by extending the system to **Integrated Filing (Financials)** under **Regulation 33 of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015**, effective **January 03, 2026**. This means listed entities covered by the framework will be able to submit the specified disclosures once through the integrated API-based process rather than making duplicate filings on both exchanges, with the explicit intent of reducing multiple submissions of the same information.

The circular confirms the following disclosure categories and their rollout status: **Integrated Filing (Financials)** applies from **January 03, 2026** for **equity-only** and **equity+debt** listed companies, while the applicability for **exclusively debt** listed companies and for **REITs/InvITs** will be **communicated later**. It also notes that **Annual Secretarial Compliance Report** under **Regulation 24A(2)** has an effective date of **September 15, 2025** for equity-only and equity+debt entities, with the debt-only and REIT/InvIT applicability still pending. **Integrated Filing (Governance)** under **Regulations 13(3), 27(2), and 30** became effective **March 01, 2025** for equity-only and equity+debt entities; **Meetings of shareholders and Voting Results** under **Regulation 44(3)** became effective **December 28, 2024** for equity-only and equity+debt entities; and **Reconciliation of Share Capital Audit Report** under **Regulation 76** became effective **November 15, 2024** for equity-only and equity+debt entities. The **Corporate Governance Report** under **Regulation 27(2)** had an effective date of **October 26, 2024**, but the circular states it has been **merged with Integrated Filing (Governance) pursuant to the SEBI circular dated December 31, 2024**. The **Investor Grievance Report** under **Regulation 13(3)** became effective **October 1, 2024**, with applicability shown for equity-only entities and debt/reit/invIT categories still to be communicated later.

For compliance purposes, the key procedural requirement is that listed entities should **not file the same disclosure multiple times on both exchanges** once the single filing system applies. If one exchange seeks clarification after a submission, the entity must respond **to the exchange that raised the clarification**, rather than routing responses elsewhere. The NSE directs listed entities to comply accordingly and provides support contacts through **NEAPS > Help > Contact Us > Listing Compliance**, or by email to **takeover@nse.co.in**; queries specifically relating to **Integrated Filing (Financials)** should be sent to **listingfr@nse.co.in**.

rows.title: Filing of Financial Results by REITs & InvITs in XBRL Mode
rows.desc: National Stock Exchange of India Circular Department: Listing Circular Ref. No.: NSE/CML/2025/38 Date: October 09, 2025 To, All Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) All Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) Subject: Filing of Financial Results by REITs & InvITs in XBRL Mode This is in reference to the SEBI Master circular SEBI/HO/DDHS-PoD-2/P/CIR/2025/99 dated July 11, 2025, for REITs & SEBI Master circular SEBI/HO/DDHS-PoD-2/P/CIR/2025/102 dated July 11, 2025, for InvITs, regarding Chapter 4 - Continuous Disclosures and Compliances by REITs & InvITs wherein the format for submission of financial results by REITs & InvITs has been revised as per the aforesaid Master circulars. In this regard, we wish to inform you that the excel utility for submission of Financial Results-REITs & InvITs as per the revised format has been made available on NEAPS portal on the below path: Compliance > Common XBRL Upload > Invit/Reit- Financial Results The REITs & InvITs are required to submit the financial results in XBRL mode within 24 hours of submission of the financial results in PDF mode using the excel utility “Financial Results_Invits_Reits” In case of any queries concerning the captioned subject, you may contact the respective team members on the contact details available in the NEAPS platform at path NEAPS > Help > Contact Us > Listing Compliance or send an email to listingfr@nse.co.in Yours faithfully, For National Stock Exchange of India Limited Mandar Walavalkar Vice President-Listing
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) has issued a listing circular dated October 9, 2025 (Ref. No. NSE/CML/2025/38) addressed to all REITs and InvITs, informing them of a revised filing requirement for financial results under the SEBI Master Circulars dated July 11, 2025: SEBI/HO/DDHS-PoD-2/P/CIR/2025/99 for REITs and SEBI/HO/DDHS-PoD-2/P/CIR/2025/102 for InvITs. The circular states that, pursuant to Chapter 4 on Continuous Disclosures and Compliances, the format for submission of financial results by REITs and InvITs has been revised, and NSE has now made available an updated Excel utility on the NEAPS portal for XBRL submission.

Operationally, REITs and InvITs must continue submitting financial results in PDF mode and then file the same financial results in XBRL mode within 24 hours of the PDF submission. The specified utility to be used is “Financial Results_Invits_Reits,” and it can be accessed through NEAPS at: Compliance > Common XBRL Upload > Invit/Reit- Financial Results. This means the compliance obligation is not just to file financial results, but to ensure the XBRL filing is completed on a tight 24-hour follow-on timeline using the prescribed utility and revised format.

For questions, entities are directed to the relevant NEAPS support contacts under NEAPS > Help > Contact Us > Listing Compliance, or by email to listingfr@nse.co.in.
