rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) has expanded its “single filing system” via API-based integration between stock exchanges to cover the **Annual Secretarial Compliance Report** required under **Regulation 24A(2) of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015**, with an **effective date of September 15, 2025**. This means that, for entities covered by the feature, the report can now be filed once through the integrated system rather than separately on both exchanges, as part of NSE’s broader move toward consolidated filing across exchanges.

The circular reiterates that the single-filing mechanism is intended to prevent **multiple filings of the same disclosure on both exchanges**. If one exchange seeks clarification after submission, the listed entity must respond to **that specific exchange** that raised the query, rather than duplicating the response elsewhere. Compliance teams should therefore ensure their internal filing procedures are aligned so that the same document is not resubmitted redundantly on both venues unless specifically required.

As set out in the circular’s table, the single filing system already applies or is being rolled out for several other disclosures: **Investor Grievance Report under Regulation 13(3)** (effective **October 1, 2024**, and later **merged with Integrated Filing (Governance)** pursuant to the SEBI circular dated **December 31, 2024**); **Corporate Governance Report under Regulation 27(2)** (effective **October 26, 2024**, with availability for some entity categories noted as “shall be communicated later”); **Reconciliation of Share Capital Audit Report under Regulation 76** (effective **November 15, 2024**); **Meetings of shareholders and Voting Results under Regulation 44(3)** (effective **December 28, 2024**); and **Integrated Filing (Governance) under Regulations 13(3), 27(2), and 30** (effective **March 1, 2025**). For the **Annual Secretarial Compliance Report**, the table indicates applicability to **equity-listed companies** and **equity + debt listed companies** from **September 15, 2025**, while applicability to **exclusively debt-listed entities** and **REITs/InvITs** is listed as **“shall be communicated later.”**

In practical terms, any listed entity that falls within the categories already enabled for the system should review its filing workflow, confirm use of the API-integrated process, and ensure the report is filed only once through the appropriate exchange interface. The circular does not create a new substantive reporting standard for the Annual Secretarial Compliance Report itself; rather, it changes the **filing mechanism** and the expectations around duplicate submissions and clarification handling. For assistance, NSE directs listed entities to the **NEAPS platform** under **NEAPS > Help > Contact Us > Listing Compliance** or to email **takeover@nse.co.in**.

rows.title: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) on Applicability of the Industry Standards on “Minimum information to be provided for Review of the Audit Committee and Shareholders for Approval of Related Party Transaction (RPT)”
rows.desc: National Stock Exchange of India Circular Department: Listing Circular Ref. No.: NSE/CML/2025/36 Date: September 04, 2025 To, All Listed Entities Subject: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) on Applicability of the Industry Standards on “Minimum information to be provided for Review of the Audit Committee and Shareholders for Approval of Related Party Transaction (RPT)” Dear Sir / Madam, This has reference to SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-2/P/CIR/2025/93 dated June 26, 2025, with respect to the Industry Standards on Minimum information to be provided for review of the audit committee and shareholders for approval of a related party transaction. In this connection, Frequently Asked Questions (FAQS) on the Industry Standards on “Minimum information to be provided for Review of the Audit Committee and Shareholders for Approval of Related Party Transaction (RPT)”, are enclosed for your reference and necessary action. The copy of the circular is also available on the NSE website (www.nseindia.com) Yours Faithfully For National Stock Exchange of India Ltd. Saba Curtay Chief Manager- Listing Compliance Encl: 1. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) on the Industry Standards on “Minimum information to be provided for Review of the Audit Committee and Shareholders for Approval of Related Party Transaction (RPT)”. Frequently Asked Questions on the RPT Industry Standards 1. Does the RPT Industry Standards replace all previous RPT disclosure formats as prescribed under Section III-B of Master Circular for compliance with the provisions of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 by listed entities dated 11 th November, 2024 (“Master Circular”)? Yes. It substitutes the disclosure requirement as specified in the Section III-B of the Master Circular from the specified date. If a particular part of the RPT Industry Standards is inconsistent with subsequent amendments in the LODR Regulations and/or SEBI Circular(s), the provisions of the LODR Regulations and/ or the SEBI Circular(s) shall prevail. 2. What is the scope of ‘minimum information’ and can the management provide additional information beyond what is prescribed? Yes. The RPT Industry Standards specify the minimum information to be disclosed. The management, in the interest of the public shareholders may provide any additional information to the Audit Committee and/or shareholders. As also provided in Para 3(3) of the RPT Industry Standards, Audit Committee may seek any additional information from the management, as it deems necessary and reasonable, to evaluate the proposed RPT. Applicability of the RPT Industry Standards 3. What is the effective date for the applicability of the RPT Industry Standards as per SEBI Circular dated June 26, 2025? The effective date for the applicability of the RPT Industry Standards is 1 st September, 2025, as per SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-2/P/CIR/2025/93 dated 26 th June, 2025. 4. Are RPT Industry Standards applicable to transactions between foreign subsidiaries of Indian listed companies? Yes, in case such RPTs require approval of the Audit Committee and/or shareholders of the listed holding company, as may be applicable in terms of the LODR Regulations. 5. Whether the RPT Industry Standards is applicable to transactions undertaken by subsidiaries of a listed entity where the listed entity is not a party? Yes, (In respect of RPTs requiring approval of the Audit Committee and/or shareholders of the listed holding company, as may be applicable in terms of the LODR Regulations). 6. If the listed entity is having related party transactions with its fellow subsidiaries, can the holding company provide duly certified summary of financial information as required to be placed before the Audit Committee or shareholders under the RPT Industry Standards for all such fellow subsidiaries of the listed company with which the listed entity proposes to enter into the transactions for every year. Yes, the holding company consolidates the financial statements of its subsidiaries and therefore, the holding company may provide duly certified summary of financial information as required to be placed before the Audit Committee or shareholders under the RPT Industry Standards for all such subsidiaries with a cavet that these particulars are provided based on the information obtained for preparation of consolidated financial statements of the listed entity. 7. If a transaction is not covered under Part B and Part C, does it still need to comply with the RPT Industry Standards? As stated in Para 4 of the Executive Summary of the RPT Industry Standards itself, Part A of Para 4 of the RPT Industry Standards applies to all related party transactions unless exempt under Para 1(3) of the RPT Industry Standards. 8. A listed entity enters into three related party transactions during the financial year, each amounting to ₹30 lakh. It then proposes a fourth transaction of ₹11 lakh w
rows.summary:
This NSE circular dated September 4, 2025 forwards FAQs on the SEBI-mandated Industry Standards for the minimum information to be placed before the Audit Committee and shareholders for approval of related party transactions (“RPTs”). The circular makes clear that these Industry Standards **replace** the earlier RPT disclosure formats in **Section III-B of the NSE Master Circular dated November 11, 2024**, from the **specified effective date**, but if any part of the Industry Standards conflicts with later amendments to the LODR Regulations or subsequent SEBI circulars, the **LODR Regulations/SEBI circulars prevail**.

For compliance purposes, the Industry Standards are described as setting only the **minimum** information to be disclosed; listed entities may provide **additional information** to the Audit Committee and/or shareholders if management believes it is in the interest of public shareholders, and the Audit Committee may itself seek further information where it considers that necessary and reasonable to assess the proposed RPT. The FAQs confirm the **effective date is 1 September 2025** under SEBI Circular No. **SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-2/P/CIR/2025/93 dated June 26, 2025**.

The applicability is broad: the Standards apply not only to direct RPTs of the listed entity, but also to RPTs involving **foreign subsidiaries of Indian listed companies** and to transactions undertaken by **subsidiaries where the listed entity itself is not a party**, so long as those transactions require Audit Committee and/or shareholder approval of the listed holding company under the LODR Regulations. The FAQs also state that where the listed entity has RPTs with **fellow subsidiaries**, the holding company may provide a **duly certified summary of financial information** for the relevant subsidiaries to support Audit Committee/shareholder review, but this is subject to a caveat that the information is based on data collected for preparation of the listed entity’s **consolidated financial statements**.

The FAQs further clarify that the Standards are not limited to the specific transaction types covered in Part B and Part C; **Part A of Para 4 applies to all related party transactions unless exempt under Para 1(3)**. The document begins to address a threshold aggregation example involving three RPTs of **₹30 lakh each** and a fourth proposed transaction of **₹11 lakh**, indicating that numerical aggregation/threshold treatment is a compliance issue under the Standards, but the provided text cuts off before the answer is completed.

rows.summary:
This NSE circular announces a new **system-driven disclosure mechanism** for both **credit rating disclosures under Regulation 30(6) read with sub-para 3 of Para A of Part A of Schedule III of SEBI LODR** and for **ESG rating disclosures**, effective **August 02, 2025**. It is issued in light of SEBI’s December 31, 2024 circular on ease-of-doing-business measures for listed entities and SEBI’s April 29, 2025 circular on clarificatory/procedural changes for ESG Rating Providers (ERPs). Under the new arrangement, **stock exchanges will consume rating data directly from CRAs and ERPs and automatically disseminate it on the exchange website**, rather than relying on separate manual/public disclosure processes, and NSE has created dedicated web paths for these disclosures: one for credit rating disclosures and one for ESG rating disclosures.

The circular applies to **all listed entities**, **all SEBI-registered Credit Rating Agencies (CRAs)**, and **all SEBI-registered ESG Rating Providers (ERPs)**. For **credit ratings**, the system covers **“new rating(s) or revision in ratings”** required to be disclosed under the cited LODR provision. For **ESG ratings**, the exchange will prominently display ESG ratings on the listed company’s page for **issuer/entity-level ESG ratings** and on the listed security’s page for **debt-security ESG ratings**, consistent with the April 29, 2025 SEBI circular.

CRAs and ERPs are instructed to use the **NEAPS** portal on a **daily basis** to upload the required rating data. The prescribed workflow is: log in to **https://neaps.nseindia.com/NEWLISTINGCORP/**, then CRAs must select **“SDD- Creating Rating- Reg. 30”** while ERPs must select **“SSD- Credit Rating- ESG- Equity”** for equity-listed entities or **“ESG Rating- Debt”** for debt-listed entities. They must download the Excel template, fill in the required details, and upload it back through the system; the circular notes that the **name and symbol of the listed entity are auto-captured from the ISIN entered**, so the ISIN is the key input for identifying the issuer/security. NSE also points users to its public ISIN reference pages for equity-listed entities and debt private placements so the correct identifiers can be used.

Once uploaded, the information will be **auto-disseminated on the NSE website** at the specified rating disclosure pages. NSE has stated that **login credentials are being provided to all SEBI-registered CRAs and ERPs**, and any operational questions should be raised through **NEAPS > Help > Contact Us > Listing Compliance** or by emailing **takeover@nse.co.in**.

rows.title: Trading Window closure period under Clause 4 of Schedule B read with Regulation 9 of Securities and Exchange Board of India (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 - Extension of automated implementation of trading window closure to Immediate Relatives of Designated Persons, on account of declaration of financial results
rows.summary:
This document appears to be a SEBI insider-trading compliance communication concerning the trading window closure period under Clause 4 of Schedule B read with Regulation 9 of the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015, and it is specifically about financial-results announcements. The key change indicated by the title is an extension of the **automated implementation of trading-window closure** so that it applies not only to **Designated Persons** but also to their **Immediate Relatives** when the company is in the period of closure due to the **declaration of financial results**. In practical terms, this means compliance controls that block or restrict trading must be expanded to cover the trading activity of immediate relatives as well, so they are also prevented from executing trades during the relevant closure window.

For a compliance team, the document signals that the trading-window closure requirement around financial results is being operationalized more broadly and should now be treated as affecting both the insider population and their immediate family members covered by the regulation. The purpose is to prevent trades during the sensitive pre-results/post-results period when unpublished price-sensitive information may exist. Because no substantive text is provided, the summary cannot identify any specific start/end dates, blackout duration, or implementation mechanics beyond the title’s statement that the closure is tied to the declaration of financial results and that the change is an **extension of automated implementation** to Immediate Relatives.  

Given the title alone, the document should be read as a compliance reminder to verify that trading-window controls, surveillance, and any broker/DP block mechanisms are configured to apply to Immediate Relatives of Designated Persons during financial-results blackout periods, consistent with SEBI insider-trading rules.

rows.desc: National Stock Exchange of India Circular Department: Listing Circular Ref. No.: NSE/CML/2025/20 Date: April 02, 2025 To, The Company Secretaries, All Listed Entities Subject: Updates on the Implementation of recommendations of the Expert Committee for facilitating ease of doing business for listed entities- Disclosure of Integrated Filing- Financial This has reference to the SEBI circular SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-2/CIR/P/2024/185 dated December 31, 2024 (‘SEBI Circular’) and read with Exchange’s circular Ref No: NSE/CML/2025/02 dated January 02, 2025, regarding implementation of recommendations of the Expert Committee for facilitating ease of doing business for listed entities. In this connection, this is to inform you that the XBRL utility for Integrated Filing - Financial has been made available on NEAPS portal on the below path: Compliance > Common XBRL Upload > Integrated Filing > Integrated Filing- Financial Listed entities are required to submit financial results in XBRL mode using “Integrated Filing-Financial” utility only. Note: 1. Outcome of the Board Meeting in PDF mode for Financial Results to be submitted within the prescribed timelines of 30 mins or 3 hours as may be applicable, on the below path only: Compliance > Announcements/Corporate actions > Create announcement/ corporate actions > Intimation type: Announcement > Regulation 30 – Para A > Subject – Outcome of board meeting > Type – Financial results 2. Further, the listed entities shall submit Integrated Filing - Financial in XBRL on same date of submission of the financial results (in PDF form), on the below path only: Compliance > Common XBRL Upload > Integrated Filing > Integrated Filing - Financial Please note that the following shall be discontinued w.e.f. April 01, 2025: 1. Financial results submitted in PDF form under NEAPS - Quick Results tab 2. PDF filing of ‘Integrated Filing - Financial’ in the Corporate Announcement under following path: NEAPS > Compliance > Announcements > Announcements/Corporate Actions > Create Announcement. 3. Existing XBRL utilities for filing Financial Results, Related Party Transactions Disclosure, Statement of Deviations and Impact of Audit Qualifications. 4. Submission of Statement of Deviation(s) / variation(s) in PDF format. Continuation Sheet INTERNAL In case of any queries concerning the captioned subject, please reach out to the respective team members on the contact details available in the NEAPS platform at path NEAPS > Help > Contact Us > Listing Compliance or send an email to listingfr@nse.co.in Yours faithfully, For National Stock Exchange of India Limited Yukti Sharma Head -Listing
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India’s circular dated April 2, 2025 (Ref. No. NSE/CML/2025/20) updates listed entities on implementation of the Expert Committee recommendations on “ease of doing business” and specifically the disclosure process for **Integrated Filing – Financial**. The circular refers to SEBI Circular **SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-2/CIR/P/2024/185 dated December 31, 2024** and NSE circular **NSE/CML/2025/02 dated January 2, 2025**, and confirms that the **XBRL utility for Integrated Filing – Financial is now available on the NEAPS portal** at **Compliance > Common XBRL Upload > Integrated Filing > Integrated Filing- Financial**.

For **all listed entities**, financial results must now be filed in **XBRL mode only through the “Integrated Filing-Financial” utility**. In addition, the **Board Meeting outcome for financial results** must still be filed in **PDF format** within the applicable statutory timeline of **30 minutes or 3 hours** (depending on the applicable disclosure timeline), and that PDF filing must be made only through **Compliance > Announcements/Corporate actions > Create announcement/corporate actions > Intimation type: Announcement > Regulation 30 – Para A > Subject – Outcome of board meeting > Type – Financial results**. The circular also requires that the **Integrated Filing – Financial XBRL submission be made on the same date as the PDF submission of the financial results** and only through **Compliance > Common XBRL Upload > Integrated Filing > Integrated Filing - Financial**.

A key compliance change is that, **effective April 1, 2025**, several older filing routes are discontinued. These include: (1) filing **financial results in PDF** under the **NEAPS Quick Results tab**; (2) filing **“Integrated Filing - Financial” in PDF** under the Corporate Announcement path (**NEAPS > Compliance > Announcements > Announcements/Corporate Actions > Create Announcement**); (3) the **existing XBRL utilities** for **Financial Results**, **Related Party Transactions Disclosure**, **Statement of Deviations**, and **Impact of Audit Qualifications**; and (4) submission of **Statement of Deviation(s) / variation(s)** in **PDF format**. Compliance teams should therefore ensure they are using the new Integrated Filing-Financial XBRL workflow and that legacy upload methods are no longer used after the April 1, 2025 cutoff.

For operational support, NSE directs listed entities to use the contact details available on NEAPS under **NEAPS > Help > Contact Us > Listing Compliance** or email **listingfr@nse.co.in**.

rows.desc: National Stock Exchange of India Circular Department: Listing Circular Ref. No.: NSE/CML/2025/17 Date: April 01, 2025 To, The Company Secretaries, All Listed Entities Subject: SEBI Circular on Measures to facilitate ease of doing business with respect to framework for assurance or assessment, ESG disclosures for value chain, and introduction of voluntary disclosure on green credits. This has reference to the SEBI circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-1/P/CIR/2025/42 dated March 28, 2025 (“SEBI Circular”) regarding implementation of recommendations of the Expert Committee for facilitating ease of doing business for listed entities respect to framework for assurance or assessment, ESG disclosures for value chain, and introduction of voluntary disclosure on green credits. A copy of SEBI Circular dated March 28, 2025, is enclosed for reference and necessary action at your end. The copy of the circular is also available on the NSE website (www.nseindia.com). This is for your information please. Yours faithfully, For National Stock Exchange of India Limited Apeksha Raichura Manager – Listing Compliance Encl: 1. SEBI Circular Page 1 of 4 CIRCULAR SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-1/P/CIR/2025/42 March 28, 2025 To, All listed entities All the recognized Stock Exchanges Dear Sir/Madam, Sub: Measures to facilitate ease of doing business with respect to framework for assurance or assessment, ESG disclosures for value chain, and introduction of voluntary disclosure on green credits. 1. Based on the recommendations of the Expert Committee for Facilitating Ease of Doing Business and pursuant to public consultation, the Board, on December 18, 2024, decided to revise various provisions regarding ESG disclosures for value chain, provide an option to undertake ‘assessment’ or ‘assurance’ for BRSR Core and ESG disclosures for value chain, and introduce disclosure on green credits. 2. Accordingly, the provisions of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (“LODR Regulations”) in this regard, have been amended vide Gazette ID CG-MH-E-28032025-262027 dated March 28, 2025. 3. Further, the following partial modifications are being carried out in the Master Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/PoD2/CIR/P/0155 captioned, “Master circular for compliance with the provisions of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 by listed entities”, dated November 11, 2024: Green Credits 3.1. In Principle 6 of BRSR, provided under Annexure 16 of the aforementioned master circular, an additional leadership indicator (i.e. an eighth leadership indicator) shall be included seeking disclosures on green credits in the following format - “8. How many Green Credits have been generated or procured: a. By the listed entity b. By the top ten (in terms of value of purchases and sales, respectively) value chain partners” Page 2 of 4 3.2. Applicability: The provisions under this Section shall be applicable for BRSR disclosures for FY 2024-25 and onwards. Assessment or Assurance 3.3. In order to facilitate ease of doing business, decrease cost and effort for listed entities and their value chain partners for verifications of sustainability reporting, as well as make the process profession agnostic, the following is mandated, and accordingly the relevant provisions on BRSR Core and ESG disclosures for value chain, as prescribed in Section IV-B of Chapter IV of the aforementioned master circular, stand revised as under. 3.4. Para 2.1 of the aforementioned master circular shall read as: “The BRSR Core is a sub-set of the BRSR, consisting of a set of Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) / metrics under 9 ESG attributes. Keeping in view the relevance to the Indian /Emerging market context, few new KPIs have been identified for assessment or assurance such as job creation in small towns, open-ness of business, gross wages paid to women etc. Further, for better global comparability intensity ratios based on revenue adjusted for Purchasing Power Parity (PPP) have been included. The format of BRSR Core for assessment or assurance is placed at Annexure 17A. Further, it is specified that “assessment” refers to third-party assessment undertaken as per the standards developed by the Industry Standards Forum (ISF) in consultation with SEBI.” 3.5. Further, Para 2.2 of the aforementioned master circular shall read as: “In order to facilitate the verification process, the BRSR Core specifies the data and approach for reporting and assessment or assurance. It is clarified that the approach specified is only a base methodology. Any changes or industry specific adjustments / estimations shall be disclosed.” 3.6. Further, Para 2.4.2 of the aforementioned master circular shall read as: “Listed entities shall mandatorily undertake assessment or assurance of the BRSR Core, as per the glide path specified in the following table:” Financial Year Applicability of BRSR Core to top listed entities (by market capitalizatio
rows.summary:
This SEBI circular, dated March 28, 2025 and circulated by NSE on April 1, 2025, revises the ESG/BRSR framework to make assurance/assessment processes easier and adds new disclosure requirements. SEBI says these changes follow Expert Committee recommendations and public consultation, and they have already been implemented through amendments to the LODR Regulations via Gazette ID CG-MH-E-28032025-262027 dated March 28, 2025. The circular also partially modifies the November 11, 2024 Master Circular on LODR compliance, so listed entities need to update their ESG reporting and verification processes accordingly.

For BRSR, SEBI has added a new eighth leadership indicator under Principle 6 in Annexure 16 requiring disclosure of how many Green Credits have been generated or procured, separately for (a) the listed entity and (b) the top ten value chain partners, ranked by value of purchases and sales respectively. This new green credits disclosure applies to BRSR filings for FY 2024–25 onward.

For BRSR Core and ESG disclosures for the value chain, SEBI has changed the framework so listed entities may use either “assessment” or “assurance,” and the process is intended to be profession-agnostic. The circular clarifies that “assessment” means a third-party assessment carried out under standards developed by the Industry Standards Forum (ISF) in consultation with SEBI. It also states that the methodology in BRSR Core is only a base methodology, and any changes or industry-specific adjustments/estimations must be disclosed, so companies cannot silently modify the approach. The revised BRSR Core is described as a sub-set of BRSR containing KPIs/metrics across 9 ESG attributes, with some new metrics tailored to the Indian/emerging-market context such as job creation in small towns, openness of business, and gross wages paid to women, and it also includes intensity ratios based on revenue adjusted for Purchasing Power Parity (PPP).

The circular further states that listed entities must mandatorily undertake assessment or assurance of BRSR Core according to a glide path, with the detailed applicability table to be used for phased compliance. Because the document excerpt provided cuts off before the full glide path table, compliance teams should review the full SEBI circular and updated master circular annexures to confirm exactly when their company falls into the mandatory assessment/assurance regime and which reporting year applies. In practice, the main action items are to update ESG reporting templates for the new green credits disclosure, align internal controls and vendor/value-chain data collection for BRSR Core, and ensure the chosen verification route and methodology disclosures conform to the revised SEBI/ISF standards.

rows.desc: National Stock Exchange of India Circular Department: Listing Circular Ref. No.: NSE/CML/2025/16 Date: April 01, 2025 To, The Company Secretaries, All Listed Entities Subject: Submission of Integrated Filing- Governance This has reference to the SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-2/CIR/P/2024/185 dated December 31, 2024 (‘SEBI Circular’) read with various Exchange Circulars bearing Circular Ref No: NSE/CML/2025/02 dated January 02, 2025, Circular Ref No: NSE/CML/2025/03 dated January 13, 2025 and Circular Ref. No.: NSE/CML/2025/07 dated February 28, 2025 regarding implementation of recommendations of the Expert Committee for facilitating ease of doing business for listed entities in relation to the filing of Integrated Filing-Governance. In this connection, this is to inform you that: 1. The timeline for submission of XBRL for Integrated Filing-Governance from the quarter ended March 31, 2025 onwards, is 30 days from the end of quarter. 2. The listed entities shall submit only Integrated Filing-Governance (XBRL form) within 30 days from the end of the quarter. 3. From quarter ended March 31, 2025 onwards, the listed entities are not required to submit the existing XBRL of Corporate Governance and Investor Grievance Report as per the current process. In case of any queries concerning the captioned subject, please reach out to the respective team members on the contact details available in the NEAPS platform at path NEAPS > Help > Contact Us > Listing Compliance or send an email to takeover@nse.co.in/nsexbrl@nse.co.in. Yours faithfully, For National Stock Exchange of India Limited Yukti Sharma Head -Listing
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India has updated the filing process for listed entities’ governance disclosures under the SEBI circular dated December 31, 2024 and earlier NSE circulars implementing the Expert Committee recommendations on ease of doing business. Starting with the quarter ended **March 31, 2025**, the deadline for submitting **Integrated Filing – Governance in XBRL format** is **30 days from the end of the quarter**.  

For compliance purposes, listed entities are now required to file **only the Integrated Filing – Governance (XBRL)** within that 30-day window. The circular explicitly states that, from the **March 31, 2025 quarter onward**, entities **do not need to file the separate existing XBRL versions of the Corporate Governance Report and the Investor Grievance Report** under the old process.  

The change applies to **all listed entities**. If questions arise, the NSE directs filers to the contact details available on the **NEAPS** platform under **NEAPS > Help > Contact Us > Listing Compliance**, or to email **takeover@nse.co.in** or **nsexbrl@nse.co.in**.

rows.title: Circular on the Faster Rights Issue with a flexibility of allotment to specific investor(s)

The copy of the circular is also available on the NSE website http://www.nseindia.com/ This is for your information please. For and on behalf of National Stock Exchange of India Limited Srishti Soni Manager Encl: 1. Page 2 of 6 5. In view of the new framework of Rights Issue, the following partial modification in the Master Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/PoD-1/P/CIR/2024/0154 on SEBI ICDR Regulations, dated November 11, 2024 shall be carried out: 8.1. Para 1.3.1 of Chapter 2 of Master Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/PoD- 1/P/CIR/2024/0154 shall read as under – “In the letter of offer the issuer shall disclose the process of credit of REs in the demat account and renunciation thereof.” 8.2. Para 1 of Annexure IIIA of Chapter 4 of Master Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/PoD-1/P/CIR/2024/0154 shall read as under- “The draft offer document filed with the Board for public issue (hereinafter “draft offer document”) of securities shall be scrutinized based on the broad guidelines specified as under and accordingly, the draft offer document
rows.summary:
SEBI’s March 11, 2025 circular introduces a new framework for rights issues under the amended SEBI ICDR Regulations, 2018, and the NSE circular dated March 12, 2025 simply forwards it to listed entities and registered merchant bankers for necessary action. The key change is that a rights issue must now be completed within **23 working days from the date the issuer’s Board of Directors approves the rights issue**; SEBI also says that where the rights issue is for **convertible debt instruments** and shareholder approval is required, the timetable must be adjusted to account for that approval step. Correspondingly, the rights issue subscription window must remain open for **at least 7 days and no more than 30 days**.

SEBI has also revised the operational workflow: **stock exchanges and depositories, together with the registrar to the issue, must validate subscription bids and finalize the basis of allotment**, and the exchanges and depositories must develop an **automated investor application validation system within 6 months from the circular’s applicable date**. This is a material process requirement for the market infrastructure institutions involved in rights issues, and issuers and intermediaries should expect the new validation and allotment process to be integrated into the shortened timeline.

The circular also makes several consequential updates to the SEBI master circular for ICDR matters. Issuers must disclose in the **letter of offer** the process for **credit of rights entitlements (REs) to demat accounts and their renunciation**. For application mechanics, SEBI states that applicants may use the **application form available on the registrar’s website or printed forms sourced from the issuer or registrar**. A further procedural change requires that **correction of bid data collated by the self-certified syndicate bank (SCSB) after issue closure must be completed on the issue closure date itself**.

Finally, for filing and fee payment, rights issue issuers must **file the letter of offer with SEBI by email at cfddil@sebi.gov.in** and pay the filing fee **online through the SEBI website payment link under the “Filing Fees” category**. The circular also references partial modifications to the master circular’s public-issue review provisions, indicating that the SEBI filing framework is being aligned with the new faster rights issue process. Overall, the document primarily affects **listed entities planning rights issues, merchant bankers, stock exchanges, depositories, registrars, bankers to an issue, SCSBs, and NPCI**, with the substantive compliance impact centered on tighter timelines, revised bid-validation responsibilities, and updated filing/disclosure procedures.

rows.title: Clarification on fixing the record date under Regulation 42 of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015
rows.desc: Department: LISTING Circular Ref. No: NSE/CML/2025/04 Date: February 07, 2025 To All Listed Entities, Subject: Clarification on fixing the record date under Regulation 42 of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 This is with reference to the recent amendment made by the Securities and Exchange Board of India to regulation 42 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements), Regulations, 2015 vide notification dated December 12, 2024. It is clarified that listed entities shall ensure a minimum gap of at least three working days between the date of board/shareholders’ approval, as applicable to the specific corporate action mentioned in Regulation 42 (1), and the Record Date fixed for such purpose. The minimum gap shall be exclusive of the date of board/shareholder's approval and the actual record date. Further, as per latest amendment, sub-regulation 5 of Regulation 42 of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements), Regulations, 2015 has been omitted. Hence the listed entities are not required to announce dates of closure of their transfer books for any purpose. All Listed entities are requested to take note of the same and comply accordingly. For and on behalf of National Stock Exchange of India Limited Senior Manager Harshad Dharod
rows.summary:
This circular clarifies how listed entities must fix the **record date** under **Regulation 42 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015** following SEBI’s amendment notified on **December 12, 2024**. From this clarification, a listed entity must ensure a **minimum gap of at least three working days** between the **date of board approval or shareholders’ approval** (depending on what is applicable for the relevant corporate action under Regulation 42(1)) and the **record date** set for that corporate action. The three-working-day gap must be calculated **excluding both the approval date and the actual record date**, so the intervening working days are what matter.

The circular also notes a separate compliance change: **Regulation 42(5) has been omitted**. As a result, listed entities are **no longer required to announce closure dates of transfer books for any purpose**. This applies to **all listed entities** and to any corporate action covered by **Regulation 42(1)**. The circular is dated **February 07, 2025**, and the exchange instructs listed entities to take note and **comply accordingly**.

rows.desc: Non-Confidential Circular Department: Listing Circular Ref No: NSE/CML/2025/02 Date: January 02, 2025 To, The Company Secretaries, All Listed Entities Subject: Implementation of recommendations of the Expert Committee for facilitating ease of doing business for listed entities This has reference to the amendments to the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (“SEBI LODR”) which have been published in the Gazette of India on December 13, 2024 and to give effect to certain recommendations of the Expert Committee and carry out consequential changes to the provisions of SEBI Master Circular dated November 11, 2024, on compliance with the SEBI LODR by listed entities, SEBI has issued a circular SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-2/CIR/P/2024/185 dated December 31, 2024 (‘SEBI Circular’). In this regard a copy of SEBI Circular dated December 31, 2024, is enclosed for your reference and for necessary action at your end. The copy of the circular will also be made available on the NSE website at https://www.nseindia.com/companies- listing/circular-for-listed-companies-equity-market Based on the above, the Integrated Filing shall be applicable for the filings to be done for the quarter ending December 31, 2024, and thereafter. The timelines for Integrated Filing shall be as follows: a. Integrated Filing (Governance): within 30 days from the end of the quarter; b. Integrated Filing (Financial): within 45 days from the end of the quarter, other than the last quarter, and 60 days from the end of the last quarter and the financial year In this regard, the first quarterly Integrated Filing i.e. Integrated Filing (Governance) and Integrated Filing (Financial) which is applicable for the quarter ending December 31, 2024, may be filed within a period of 45 days from the end of the quarter. However, for subsequent quarterly filings, the companies shall follow the timelines as mentioned under point a & b above. Note: Basis the above the listed entities shall submit the Integrated filing in PDF as per the format available in the aforementioned SEBI Circular. Further, in order to comply with the aforesaid timelines for the Integrated Filing in PDF, the Exchange has added the Subject titled ‘Integrated Filing- Governance’ and ‘Integrated Filing- Financial’ which will be available under Type Of Disclosure: ‘Others’ and Subject Category: ‘Integrated Filing’ under the Announcement module which can be accessed at the path NEAPS > Compliance > Announcements > Announcements/Corporate Action> Create Announcement. The listed entities shall use the above-mentioned subject and path for submission of the PDF format of the Integrated Filing. Entities are also requested to ensure that while submitting the disclosures under Integrated Filing in PDF, PAN details must be masked. Non-Confidential In addition to the above, the listed entities shall also continue to file the existing XBRL’s/PDF filing as the case may be for each of the compliance provided in this Integrated Filing until further communication is issued by the Exchange. (‘OBM’) PDF for Regulation 30 events as per the current process for: - Outcome of BM for Financial (Quick Results and OBM- as per new timelines i.e. 30mins or 3hrs as may be applicable) - Quarterly disclosure of outstanding default on loans/debt securities as appliable XBRL for Financials (existing utility as per current process and timeline) XBRL for Impact of Audit Qualification (for annual in existing utility as per current process and timeline) XBRL for SOD (existing utility as per current process and timeline) XBRL for RPT (for half year- on the same day of filing of financials results in existing utility) The listed entities are requested to take note of the above and comply accordingly. In case any queries concerning the captioned subject, please reach out to the respective team members on the contact details available in the NEAPS platform at path NEAPS > Help > Contact Us > Listing Compliance or send an email to takeover@nse.co.in Yours faithfully, For National Stock Exchange of India Limited Yukti Sharma Head -Listing Page 1 of 44 CIRCULAR SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-2/CIR/P/2024/185 December 31, 2024 To, All listed entities that have listed their specified securities All Recognized Stock Exchanges All Depositories The Insti
rows.summary:
This circular from the National Stock Exchange implements SEBI’s December 31, 2024 circular and the related amendments to the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, which were published in the Gazette of India on December 13, 2024. Its main effect is to introduce “Integrated Filing” for listed entities, with separate PDF submissions for governance and financial disclosures using the SEBI-prescribed format, while the existing XBRL/PDF filings for the underlying compliances must continue until further notice. The new regime applies to filings for the quarter ending December 31, 2024 and thereafter.

For timing, the first quarterly Integrated Filing for the December 31, 2024 quarter may be submitted within 45 days from quarter-end, but after that the deadlines split: Integrated Filing (Governance) is due within 30 days from the end of each quarter, while Integrated Filing (Financial) is due within 45 days from the end of each quarter other than the last quarter, and within 60 days from the end of the last quarter of the financial year. The circular also clarifies that, for the December 2024 quarter, the “governance” and “financial” integrated filings are both covered by that one-time 45-day filing window. The listed entity must submit the integrated filing in PDF on the NSE platform using the new announcement subjects “Integrated Filing- Governance” and “Integrated Filing- Financial,” located under Type of Disclosure: “Others” and Subject Category: “Integrated Filing” at NEAPS > Compliance > Announcements > Announcements/Corporate Action > Create Announcement.

rows.title: Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR) - FAQs and General Observations / Guidelines for filing of BRSR
rows.summary:
This circular from NSE (Ref. No. NSE/CML/2024/11 dated May 10, 2024) is a guidance note for listed companies on filing the Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR) and BRSR Core, and it reiterates that the controlling requirements are the SEBI LODR Regulations, 2015 and SEBI Circular dated July 12, 2023 (SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-SEC-2/P/CIR/2023/122). The main filing obligation remains that the **top 1,000 listed companies by market capitalization** must submit BRSR in the **updated SEBI-prescribed format**; for example, if a company is in the top 1,000 as of **March 31, 2024**, BRSR applies for **FY 2023–24**. NSE also clarifies that if a company was previously within the top 1,000 on **March 31, 2023 or March 31, 2022**, the obligation continues even if it later falls below the threshold, because Regulation 3(2) preserves applicability once triggered by market-cap criteria. Companies outside the top 1,000 may still file BRSR **voluntarily**, including companies listed on the **SME Exchange**.

For exchange filing, NSE states that if a company is in the top 1,000 on **any one exchange** (NSE or BSE), it must file BRSR with **both exchanges**, not just the exchange where it appears in the top-1,000 list. The circular also addresses BRSR Core assurance requirements: the **top 150 listed companies by market capitalization as of March 31, 2024** must mandatorily obtain **Reasonable Assurance** on BRSR Core. If a company indicates in the BRSR utility that it has undertaken reasonable assurance, it must complete the assurance-provider details at **Point 15** and the **type of assurance** at **Point 16**; if “All / Partial” is selected for Point 16, the company must further specify whether the assurance is **Reasonable Assurance** or **Limited Assurance**. A **copy of the Reasonable Assurance Certificate** must be attached when submitting the BRSR PDF and annual report to the exchanges.

NSE also notes a practical filing rule: the **BRSR XBRL utility from either NSE or BSE can be used interchangeably** for uploading at either exchange, so companies are not restricted to the utility of the same exchange where they file. The annexed FAQs/guidelines are expressly described as **guidance only** and do not override the underlying law, SEBI regulations, or exchange circulars; companies must continue to comply with all applicable listing and other regulatory requirements as amended from time to time.

rows.title: SCORES 2.0 New Technology to strengthen SEBI Complaint Redressal System for Investors
rows.summary:
This circular informs listed companies, municipal debt securities issuers, and registrars and share transfer agents that SEBI’s upgraded complaint-handling platform, SCORES 2.0, has been launched effective April 1, 2024, and that the SEBI complaint redress framework must now be followed on that system. SEBI will send the SCORES user ID and password to the e-mail address of each entity’s designated contact person, so firms should ensure the correct contact details are on record and monitored.

For any complaint received through SCORES, the listed company / municipal debt securities entity / RTA must resolve the matter within 21 calendar days and upload the Action Taken Report (ATR) in SCORES; the ATR is then automatically forwarded to the complainant. If the complainant is dissatisfied, the complaint is escalated to the Exchange for first-level review, and the Exchange must address that escalated complaint within 10 calendar days. If the investor remains dissatisfied after the Exchange’s review, the complaint may be escalated to SEBI for a second review.

The circular also makes clear that failure by the listed company / municipal debt securities entity / RTA, or by the Designated Body as applicable, to meet the prescribed timelines will cause the complaint to be auto-escalated to the next level. In addition, at any stage the investor may choose to refer the complaint to ODR (Online Dispute Resolution); once referred to ODR, the complaint is treated as disposed of in SCORES 2.0. Listed companies are specifically directed to note Schedule VI of SEBI circular SEBI/HO/OIAE/IGRD/CIR/P/2023/156 dated September 20, 2023, together with SEBI circular SEBI/HO/OIAE/IGRD/CIR/P/2023/183 dated December 1, 2023, for the complaint-handling timelines and the consequences for non-compliance.

rows.title: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) – Trading Window closure period under Clause 4 of Schedule B read with Regulation 9 of SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 (“PIT Regulations”) – Extending framework for restricting trading by Designated Persons (“DPs”) by freezing PAN at security level to all listed companies in a phased manner
rows.summary:
This NSE circular dated March 28, 2024 issues FAQs on the SEBI trading-window/PAN-freeze framework under Clause 4 of Schedule B read with Regulation 9 of the PIT Regulations, and says the FAQs are for guidance only while listed companies must continue complying with the PIT Regulations and any amendments. It extends the system-based restriction on trading by Designated Persons (DPs) through freezing PANs at the security level to all listed companies in a phased rollout: as of this FAQ set, the system is already available for NIFTY 50 / SENSEX 30 companies and the top 2000 companies by BSE market capitalization for the quarter ended December 2023, with the remaining listed companies to be covered from 1 April 2024. The issuer does not need to re-enter DP/member data for this purpose if it was already uploaded for System Driven Disclosure (SDD), because that data will auto-populate into the trading-window module.

Operationally, issuers can enter trading-window closure start and end dates only up to T-2 days of the relevant dates, and if the board meeting date is not known on day one of the quarter they may enter a notional end date and later modify it, again subject to the T-2 rule. The depository system is intended to record trading-window closure from the first day of the month following quarter-end for SDD monitoring, so if a company’s actual closure period begins earlier than that, the company must maintain that earlier date internally even though the portal records the first-day-of-next-month date. The PAN freeze works on a PAN–ISIN basis and, where a DP has multiple accounts across both depositories, the freeze will apply across both depositories based on the PAN data uploaded in SDD for the DP, using only the designated depository; DPs do not need to be updated on both depositories.

The FAQs also clarify that pledge invocation is not permitted during the PAN-freeze period unless the pledge was marked before the trading-window closure began. If a DP ceases during a closure period and is deleted from the list, that deletion does not automatically remove the PAN freeze from the trading-window record; the issuer must either grant an exemption period for that DP or the freeze will lift only when the trading-window closure ends. New DPs can be added during the closure period, but the freeze date for the addition will be accepted only on a T-2 basis from the date of addition. The document begins to address ESOP-related trading approval, but the provided text cuts off before the answer is completed, so no further rule can be reliably summarized from the excerpt.

rows.title: Corporate Grouping of Listed Companies
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) has reiterated and tightened the process for reporting changes in a listed company’s corporate group. Under the earlier circular referenced in the notice, any change in a listed company’s corporate group arising from events such as corporate restructuring, takeover, merger, demerger, acquisition, or delisting must be intimated to the Exchange within **two working days of the effective date** of the change.

The key update in this March 27, 2024 circular is procedural: **from now on, companies must submit this intimation only through NSE’s online NEAPS module**, rather than by any other method. NSE says it has introduced an online filing module in the NEAPS application for this purpose, and the annexure provides the path to the function: **NEAPS login > Compliance > Disclosures > Corporate Grouping FPI**. If the menu item is not visible, users must go to **“Customize Menu”** at the top right of the NEAPS home page and tick the checkbox for **“Corporate Grouping FPI.”** The annexure also notes that the change request is initiated by clicking **“Modify.”**

NSE further clarifies that this corporate group repository exists **only to support compliance with SEBI Circular No. SEBI/ HO/ AFD/ AFD –PoD –2/ CIR/ P/ 2023/148 dated August 24, 2023**, and it is **not** a legal definition or interpretation of terms such as “group,” “related party,” or “associate companies” under any other SEBI regulation, circular, or act. For compliance teams, the practical obligation is to carefully determine whether a corporate event has changed the company’s group classification, and if so, ensure the NEAPS filing is made within the two-working-day deadline after the effective date, using the new online workflow only.

rows.title: Repeal of circular(s) outlining procedure to deal with cases where securities are issued prior to April 01, 2014, involving offer / allotment of securities to more 49 but up to 200 investors in a financial year
rows.summary:
The NSE circular dated March 14, 2024 (Ref. No. NSE/CML/2024/06) is a notice to all listed entities informing them that SEBI has issued Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/PoD-1/P/CIR/2024/016 dated March 13, 2024, which repeals earlier circular(s) that had set out a procedure for handling cases where securities were issued before April 1, 2014 and the issuer had offered/allotted securities to more than 49 but up to 200 investors in a financial year. In practical terms, this means the prior special procedure for addressing those legacy pre-April 1, 2014 issuance situations is withdrawn, and listed entities should no longer rely on or follow the repealed circular(s) for such cases. The notice does not introduce a new substantive filing process, deadline, threshold, or numerical change beyond referencing the affected investor range of more than 49 up to 200 investors and the relevant cutoff date of April 1, 2014.

For compliance purposes, the key action is simply to take note of the repeal and ensure alignment with the updated SEBI position, with the NSE directing listed entities to review the SEBI circular available on its website and comply accordingly. The document itself does not specify any new reporting obligation, transition timeline, or enforcement mechanism; it is an informational circular confirming the repeal and advising entities to ensure compliance with the changed regulatory framework.

rows.title: Revised Pricing Methodology for Institutional Placements of Privately Placed Infrastructure Investment Trust (InvIT)
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India issued Circular NSE/CML/2024/05 on February 9, 2024, addressed to all Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) and all parties to InvITs, directing them to note and comply with SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHS-PoD/P/CIR/2024/10 dated February 8, 2024, titled “Revised Pricing Methodology for Institutional Placements of Privately Placed Infrastructure Investment Trust (InvIT).” The NSE circular itself does not restate the detailed pricing mechanics; it serves as a forwarding/compliance notice pointing recipients to the SEBI circular for the substantive requirements.  

For compliance purposes, the key point is that the pricing methodology for institutional placements of privately placed InvITs has been revised, and affected InvITs and all related transaction parties are expected to follow the revised SEBI framework immediately upon the SEBI circular’s issuance on February 8, 2024, unless the underlying SEBI text specifies a different implementation date. No thresholds, formulas, or numerical pricing parameters are provided in the NSE notice itself, so the operative compliance obligations, any amended pricing floor or benchmark, and any transaction-process changes must be taken from the referenced SEBI circular. The NSE also indicates that the SEBI circular is available on its website for reference, signaling that regulated entities should review the full text and ensure their placement procedures, documentation, and internal approvals are aligned with the revised requirements.

rows.title: Guidelines for returning of draft offer document and its resubmission
rows.summary: The National Stock Exchange of India circulated SEBI’s February 6, 2024 circular on “Guidelines for returning of draft offer document and its resubmission,” and directed all listed entities and all issuers proposing to list specified securities to take note and ensure compliance. The NSE notice itself does not set out the substantive return/resubmission rules, thresholds, timelines, or procedural changes; instead, it serves as a forwarding communication pointing recipients to the SEBI circular for the actual requirements. The only date information in the NSE communication is that the NSE circular was issued on February 7, 2024, and it references SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/PoD-1/P/CIR/2024/009 dated February 6, 2024. Compliance teams should therefore treat this as a notification that the SEBI guidance on draft offer document returns and resubmissions applies to relevant issuers and listed entities, and should review the attached SEBI circular directly to determine any filing, correction, or resubmission obligations.

rows.title: Trading Window closure period under Clause 4 of Schedule B read with Regulation 9 of SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 (“PIT Regulations”) – Extending framework for restricting trading by Designated Persons (“DPs”) by freezing PAN at security level to all listed companies in a phased manner
rows.summary:
The document is an NSE circular dated 30 January 2024 that expands the existing “trading window closure” / anti-insider-trading controls under Clause 4 of Schedule B of the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015. Its key change is the phased extension of a mechanism that restricts trading by Designated Persons by “freezing” their PAN at the security level, so that the restriction is no longer limited to select companies but is rolled out to all listed companies over time.

For compliance purposes, the circular means listed entities must align their insider-trading controls with this PAN-based security-level freeze framework, which is intended to prevent Designated Persons from trading in company securities during trading window closure periods even through accounts or relationships outside the immediate company system. The circular is specifically tied to the trading-window closure obligations already required under Clause 4 of Schedule B and Regulation 9 of the PIT Regulations, so it does not create a completely new statutory concept, but it does require implementation of a more technical enforcement method. The affected parties are all listed companies, though the rollout is phased rather than immediate for everyone, so compliance teams need to determine when their company falls into the phase applicable under NSE’s implementation schedule and ensure systems/processes are updated accordingly.

The practical compliance obligation is to ensure PAN-linked restrictions are activated at the security level for Designated Persons, which implies coordination with depositories, intermediaries, and internal compliance systems so trades are blocked during trading window closure periods. Companies should expect that this requires accurate PAN capture and maintenance for all Designated Persons, monitoring of trading windows, and procedures to respond to any system-blocked transactions or exception handling in line with insider trading policy. The document’s substance is therefore an implementation extension: it broadens the freeze-based trading restriction model to all listed companies and requires listed entities to prepare for system-level enforcement rather than relying only on manual controls.

rows.title: Framework for Offer for Sale (OFS) of Shares to Employees through Stock Exchange Mechanism
rows.summary:
SEBI issued a new circular dated January 23, 2024, titled **“Framework for Offer for Sale (OFS) of Shares to Employees through Stock Exchange Mechanism,”** and the National Stock Exchange of India circulated it to **all listed entities** on January 30, 2024 for reference and necessary action. The document does not itself set out the substantive mechanics of the employee OFS framework; instead, it directs listed companies to the updated SEBI circular and makes clear that the new framework is applicable through the **stock exchange mechanism** for **OFS of shares to employees**.

For compliance purposes, the key point is that listed entities need to review SEBI’s updated circular on the NSE website and assess whether any employee share sale arrangements they implement must now follow the revised OFS framework. The notice does not specify any thresholds, pricing rules, deadlines, exemptions, or procedural steps in the text provided, but it does indicate that action may be required by listed entities in connection with employee-directed share sales under the exchange mechanism.

rows.title: Extension of timeline for verification of market rumours by listed entities
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India (NSE), through Circular Ref. No. **NSE/CML/2024/01 dated January 29, 2024**, is notifying **all listed entities** of a SEBI circular issued on **January 25, 2024** concerning the **extension of the timeline for verification of market rumours by listed entities**. The NSE circular itself does not set out the detailed compliance change, but it makes clear that SEBI has issued a regulatory update requiring listed companies to follow the revised timing for how quickly they must verify and respond to market rumours, and that the SEBI circular is enclosed for necessary action.

For compliance purposes, the key point is that this is a **listed-entity obligation** under SEBI’s disclosure framework, so any entity listed on the NSE should review the enclosed SEBI circular and align internal investor-relations, legal, and disclosure escalation processes with the **extended verification timeline**. The NSE states that the SEBI circular is also available on its website and provides this notice for information and action. Because the NSE notice does not reproduce the actual deadline extension, specific verification period, or operative procedural steps, a compliance team should treat the **January 25, 2024 SEBI circular** as the controlling source for the exact revised requirements and implementation date.

rows.title: Revision to the Framework on Social Stock Exchange
rows.summary: The National Stock Exchange of India’s circular dated December 29, 2023, informs all Social Enterprises and all listed companies that SEBI has revised the Social Stock Exchange (SSE) framework through Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/PoD-1/P/CIR/2023/196 dated December 28, 2023. This NSE communication does not itself set out the substantive rule changes; rather, it states that SEBI has made “certain modifications/additions” to the earlier SSE framework originally issued by SEBI on September 19, 2022 and published by NSE on September 22, 2023. The circular’s operative requirement is that recipients should note the attached SEBI circular and carry out any compliance actions required under the revised framework. No specific effective date, deadlines, thresholds, rates, or procedural details are provided in the NSE circular text itself beyond the December 28, 2023 SEBI amendment date and the December 29, 2023 NSE dissemination date.

rows.title: Extension of timelines for providing ''choice of nomination’ in eligible demat accounts and mutual fund folios
rows.summary: The National Stock Exchange of India’s circular dated December 28, 2023 simply informs all listed companies that SEBI has issued Circular No. SEBI/HO/MIRSD/POD-1/P/CIR/2023/193 dated December 27, 2023, titled “Extension of timelines for providing ‘choice of nomination’ in eligible demat accounts and mutual fund folios.” The NSE circular itself does not set out the substantive requirements; it forwards the SEBI circular and says copies are enclosed and available on the NSE website, and that listed companies should take necessary action if applicable. Since the circular is directed to all listed companies for information, compliance teams should review the referenced SEBI circular directly to determine the revised timelines and any obligations that may flow through to issuer-side processes or investor-facing disclosures.

rows.title: Amendment to Circular dated July 31, 2023 on Online Resolution of Disputes in the Indian Securities Market
rows.summary:
The document is an NSE listing circular addressed to all listed companies, but it does not itself introduce new substantive compliance rules; rather, it informs issuers that SEBI has issued a separate amendment circular dated December 20, 2023, amending the SEBI circular of July 31, 2023 on “Online Resolution of Disputes in the Indian Securities Market.” The NSE letter, numbered **NSE/CML/2023/86** and dated **December 20, 2023**, states that a copy of the SEBI circular is enclosed for reference and “necessary action,” and that it is also available on the NSE website. 

For a compliance team, the key point from this document alone is that it applies to **all listed companies** and serves as a formal notice that the underlying SEBI framework for online dispute resolution has been amended. However, the NSE communication does **not** specify the amendment’s operational details, implementation steps, deadlines, thresholds, or penalties; those would have to be reviewed in the referenced SEBI circular itself. Accordingly, the immediate obligation here is to retrieve and assess the enclosed SEBI amendment circular and determine whether the company’s dispute-handling, investor grievance, arbitration, or online resolution processes need to be updated in response to the amended SEBI requirements.

rows.title: Filing of Announcements pertaining to Loss of Share Certificate/Issue of Duplicate Share Certificate/Closure of Trading Window and Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (''CIRP’) in XBRL format on NSE Electronic Application Processing System (NEAPS) platform
rows.summary:
This NSE Listing circular, dated **December 8, 2023** and addressed to the **Company Secretary/Compliance Officer of all listed companies**, announces that certain **Regulation 30** disclosures under the **SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015** must now be filed in **XBRL format** on the **NEAPS** platform for three specific announcement types: **loss of share certificate/issue of duplicate share certificate**, **closure of trading window**, and **Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP)**. The new XBRL filing facility becomes available from **December 9, 2023**; from that date, companies should use the XBRL utility in NEAPS for these subjects, accessible via **COMPLIANCE → Common XBRL Upload → Equity Announcement-XBRL**, after selecting the relevant “Subject of Announcement.”

The circular also imposes a **dual-filing requirement during the initial stage**: the **PDF filing will be treated by NSE as compliance under Regulation 30**, but the listed entity must **also submit the same disclosure in XBRL mode within 24 hours of the PDF submission**. NSE states that this is only an interim arrangement and that, at a **later date to be separately notified**, the Exchange will move to **XBRL-only submission** for these events. Listed entities must therefore ensure both the initial PDF filing and the follow-on XBRL upload are completed on time until the transition date is announced.

Operationally, the process requires the user to log in to the **NEAPS portal** at the listed URL, navigate to the XBRL upload module, choose the applicable announcement subject, **download the offline Excel utility**, complete it, and **generate an XML file** for upload. After XML generation, the filer must enter the required details on the portal and click **“Upload XBRL File”** to finish submission. NSE also notes that these three events will be available in **iXBRL format**, and the report can be accessed in NEAPS under **Report → Announcement XBRL Report iXBRL or Inline XBRL**; the circular provides a general explanation that iXBRL combines human-readable HTML with machine-readable tags.

For support or clarification, listed entities are directed to contact the **Announcements team at takeover@nse.co.in** or use the contact details shown on the NEAPS platform. The circular is issued by **National Stock Exchange of India Limited**, signed by **Ajit Mahadik, Manager – Listing Compliance**.

rows.title: Revised framework for computation of Net Distributable Cash Flow (NDCF) by Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs).
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India circular dated December 7, 2023 is addressed to all Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) and serves as a notice that SEBI issued a new circular on December 6, 2023 revising the framework for computation of Net Distributable Cash Flow (NDCF) for REITs. The NSE circular itself does not set out the revised calculation rules; rather, it directs REITs to the SEBI circular, enclosed with the notice and also posted on the NSE website, for the substantive requirements and any necessary action. From a compliance perspective, the affected entities are all REITs subject to Indian securities regulation, and the change concerns how NDCF must be computed for distribution purposes under the revised SEBI framework.

No separate effective date, transition period, or numerical thresholds are stated in the NSE notice itself. The only immediate obligation conveyed by the NSE is that REITs should review the December 6, 2023 SEBI circular and take whatever action is required to align their NDCF computation and related distribution/compliance processes with the revised framework.

rows.title: Revised framework for computation of Net Distributable Cash Flow (NDCF) by Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs).
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India’s circular dated December 7, 2023 is addressed to all Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) and transmits SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHS-PoD/P/CIR/2023/184 dated December 6, 2023, which introduces a revised framework for computing Net Distributable Cash Flow (NDCF) for InvITs. The NSE circular itself does not restate the mechanics of the new NDCF calculation, but it makes clear that the SEBI circular is the operative document and that InvITs should take necessary action in line with the revised framework.

For compliance purposes, the key point is that the computation methodology for NDCF applicable to InvITs has been formally revised by SEBI and is intended for immediate reference and implementation by all InvITs covered by the framework. No specific numerical thresholds, rates, transition periods, or filing deadlines are provided in the NSE cover circular itself, and it does not create any separate obligations beyond forwarding the SEBI requirement and indicating that the full text is available on the NSE website. Compliance teams should therefore review the SEBI circular dated December 6, 2023 directly to determine the exact revised calculation, reporting, distribution, and governance requirements that apply to their trust.

rows.title: Extension of timeline for implementation of provisions of circular SEBI/HO/OIAE/IGRD/CIR/P/2023/156 dated September 20, 2023 on Redressal of investor grievances through the SEBI Complaint Redressal (SCORES) Platform and linking it to Online Dispute Resolution platform.

The earlier SEBI framework relates to **redressal of investor grievances through the SEBI Complaint Redressal (SCORES) platform** and **linking SCORES to the Online Dispute Resolution (ODR) platform**; the new document does **not** create new substantive obligations itself, but tells listed entities that the compliance date for those earlier provisions has been extended.

For compliance purposes, the key point is that any obligations imposed by the September 20, 2023 SEBI circular should be reviewed against the **revised implementation timeline** announced in SEBI’s **December 1, 2023** extension circular, rather than the original date. The NSE circular does not restate the detailed procedural requirements, thresholds, or technical steps from the SEBI framework; it simply advises listed companies that the updated SEBI circular is enclosed and should be acted upon as necessary. No numerical thresholds, rates, or monetary amounts are introduced in this NSE communication.

The affected entities are **all listed companies** on the NSE. The action expected of compliance teams is to **read the enclosed SEBI circular**, update internal grievance-handling and dispute-resolution procedures to align with the extended implementation schedule, and ensure readiness for SCORES-based grievance redressal and the linkage to the ODR platform once the revised deadline becomes applicable. The NSE also notes that the SEBI circular is available on the NSE website for reference.
