The circular indicates that the SEBI document is available for reference and that action may be required at the listed-company level, but this NSE communication itself does not specify the detailed procedures, thresholds, or deadlines. Because no substantive compliance mechanics are contained in the text provided, a compliance team should treat this as an alert to review the underlying SEBI circular immediately and determine any internal, registrar, or shareholder-process changes needed.

rows.title: Trading Window closure period under Clause 4 of Schedule B read with Regulation 9 of SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 (“PIT Regulations”) – Extending framework for restricting trading by Designated Persons (“DPs”) by freezing PAN at security level to all listed companies in a phased manner - Next 1,000 companies in terms of BSE Market Capitalization as of June 30, 2023 for PIT - Trading Window Closure Period
rows.summary:
This document is a SEBI/PIT trading-window compliance communication that extends the “freeze PAN at security level” framework for restricting trading by Designated Persons (“DPs”) to additional listed companies in a phased rollout. The specific cohort covered here is the next 1,000 listed companies ranked by BSE market capitalization as of June 30, 2023; these companies are being brought into the trading-window closure/freeze mechanism under Clause 4 of Schedule B read with Regulation 9 of the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015. Practically, this means the affected listed entities must ensure that DPs’ PANs are frozen at the security level so that trading in the company’s securities is blocked during trading-window closure periods, rather than relying only on manual self-declaration or traditional restrictions.

For compliance teams at affected companies, the key obligation is operational readiness to implement the PAN-level freeze mechanism for all relevant DPs and to align internal insider-trading controls, broker/depository instructions, and trading-window closure processes with this framework. The document is explicitly part of a phased expansion to all listed companies, so even if a company is not in this first covered group it should expect eventual inclusion and should prepare systems and procedures accordingly. The document title indicates this is specifically about the “Trading Window Closure Period,” so the requirement is tied to blackout periods under the PIT Regulations and affects trading by DPs during those closure windows. The attached Annexure I workbook appears to contain the implementation list/details, but the substantive regulatory point is the phased extension of security-level PAN freezing for the stated next 1,000 companies as of the June 30, 2023 market-cap ranking.

rows.title: Procedural framework for dealing with unclaimed amounts lying with Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) and manner of claiming such amounts by unitholders
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India issued this November 9, 2023 circular to all Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) to notify them of, and require compliance with, SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHS-RAC-1/P/CIR/2023/178 dated November 8, 2023. The underlying SEBI circular introduces a procedural framework for handling unclaimed amounts held by InvITs and sets out how unitholders may claim those amounts, so the practical compliance impact is on InvITs that hold unpaid/distributable sums that remain unclaimed by beneficiaries.

For compliance purposes, the key point is that this NSE communication is a forwarding/implementation notice: it does not itself create new substantive requirements, but it directs InvITs to follow the SEBI circular and take “necessary action” in line with the new framework. The document does not specify any separate effective date or deadline beyond the SEBI circular date of November 8, 2023 and the NSE circular date of November 9, 2023. No thresholds, rates, or quantitative limits are stated in the NSE notice itself.

Entities affected are all InvITs listed/covered by NSE’s circular. The required action is to review and implement the SEBI-prescribed process for managing unclaimed amounts and for processing unitholder claims under the new procedure, with the SEBI circular serving as the controlling document. The circular also notes that the SEBI text is enclosed and available on the NSE website for reference, indicating that compliance teams should consult the SEBI circular itself for the detailed operational steps and filing/verification requirements.

rows.title: Procedural framework for dealing with unclaimed amounts lying with Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) and manner of claiming such amounts by unitholders.
rows.summary:
This circular is a transmission of SEBI’s November 8, 2023 directive, issued by the National Stock Exchange of India on November 9, 2023, to all Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs). It does not itself create new obligations in the NSE letter, but it alerts REITs that SEBI has issued a procedural framework governing how unclaimed amounts held by REITs must be handled and how unitholders may claim those amounts.

For compliance purposes, the key action is to review and implement the SEBI circular titled “Procedural framework for dealing with unclaimed amounts lying with Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) and manner of claiming such amounts by unitholders,” since the NSE explicitly forwards it for “necessary action at your end.” The letter provides the circular reference number SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHS-RAC-1/P/CIR/2023/177 and notes that a copy is enclosed and also available on the NSE website.

The document does not state the substantive mechanics of the framework, any threshold amounts, timelines, or procedural steps in the NSE covering note itself. Therefore, a compliance team should treat this as a notice that REITs are subject to SEBI’s new process for managing unclaimed distributions/amounts and for processing unitholder claims, and should consult the enclosed SEBI circular directly for the operational requirements, deadlines, and any recordkeeping or disclosure obligations.

rows.title: Revision in manner of achieving minimum public unitholding requirement – Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs)
rows.summary:
This NSE circular, dated November 1, 2023, is a forwarding notice to all Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) informing them of a SEBI circular issued on October 31, 2023, titled “Revision in manner of achieving minimum public unitholding requirement – Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs).” The NSE communication itself does not set out the revised rule text or any new operational steps; instead, it instructs InvITs and their company secretaries to refer to the enclosed SEBI circular and take “necessary action” as required under SEBI’s updated framework. The notice confirms that the SEBI circular is available for reference and also posted on the NSE website, but it does not specify the exact changes, thresholds, timelines, or compliance mechanics in the body of this letter.

For compliance purposes, the key point is that the subject matter concerns the manner in which InvITs must achieve the minimum public unitholding requirement, so any InvIT currently working toward or monitoring public unitholding compliance should review the underlying SEBI circular immediately. Because this NSE letter is purely informational and does not itself restate the revised requirement, deadlines, percentage thresholds, or transitional provisions, the binding obligations would need to be taken from the SEBI circular dated October 31, 2023.

rows.title: Ease of doing business and development of corporate bond markets – revision in the framework for fund raising by issuance of debt securities by large corporates (LCs).
rows.summary:
The NSE circular dated October 20, 2023 is a forwarding notice to all listed entities other than scheduled commercial banks, pointing them to a SEBI circular issued on October 19, 2023 (SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHS-RACPOD1/P/CIR/2023/172) concerning “Ease of doing business and development of corporate bond markets – revision in the framework for fund raising by issuance of debt securities by large corporates (LCs).” The NSE letter itself does not set out the substantive rule changes; it simply states that SEBI’s circular is enclosed for reference and necessary action, and that the circular is also available on the NSE website.

For compliance purposes, the key takeaway from this NSE communication is that it applies to all listed entities except scheduled commercial banks and may affect entities that are, or could become, classified as large corporates under SEBI’s revised debt fundraising framework. Because the NSE notice does not include the operational details, effective dates, thresholds, filing requirements, or reporting obligations, a compliance team should review the underlying SEBI circular immediately to identify any revised criteria for LC status, any new debt issuance conditions, and any related compliance or disclosure steps. The only date explicitly stated in the NSE notice is October 20, 2023, as the date of the exchange circular, and October 19, 2023, as the date of the SEBI source circular.

rows.title: Mandatory Filing of Voting Results in XBRL Mode
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India Limited issued Circular NSE/CML/2023/74 on October 17, 2023, addressed to the Company Secretary of all listed entities, to change how voting results for general meetings must be filed under Regulation 44(3) of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015. Under Regulation 44(3), listed entities must submit voting results within two working days of the conclusion of the general meeting in the format specified by SEBI; this circular says NSE is discontinuing the PDF reporting format and will accept only XBRL filings going forward.

The practical compliance change is that all listed entities must file voting result disclosures exclusively through XBRL mode, and the PDF version will no longer count as compliant filing. The prescribed XBRL format is available in NEAPS under Compliance > Event Based Compliances > Voting Result, and the submission path for the required filing is NEAPS > Compliance > Common XBRL Upload > Voting Results. This requirement becomes mandatory for all listed entities with effect from November 1, 2023.

For compliance purposes, the key point is that only an XBRL submission will be treated as satisfying Regulation 44(3); any other form of filing, including PDF, will not be regarded as compliance. Listed entities are instructed to ensure they have moved to the XBRL-only process and to contact the exchange at takeover@nse.co.in, or use the contact details available on the NEAPS platform, if they encounter filing issues.

rows.title: Relaxation from compliance with certain provisions of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 – Reg.
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India circulated SEBI’s October 7, 2023 circular (SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-2/P/CIR/2023/167) to **all listed entities having specified securities listed**, informing them of a **relaxation from compliance with certain provisions of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015**. The NSE notice itself does **not create new substantive requirements** or specify the relaxed provisions in the body of the text; it simply advises that the SEBI circular is attached and should be followed for “necessary action” by the listed entities concerned. The NSE circular is dated **October 9, 2023** and is issued as **NSE/CML/2023/73**.

For compliance purposes, the key point is that this communication is a **regulatory update applicable to listed entities with specified securities** and directs recipients to review and implement the SEBI circular dated **October 7, 2023**, which contains the actual details of the relaxations, any affected provisions, and any applicable timelines or deadlines. Because the NSE notice does not restate those details, a compliance team should treat this as a prompt to check the enclosed SEBI circular and determine whether any filing, disclosure, governance, or procedural obligations under the LODR Regulations have been temporarily eased for the covered issuers.

rows.title: Centralized mechanism for reporting the demise of an investor through KRAs.
rows.summary:
This NSE circular does not itself create a new substantive rule for listed companies; it is an information notice to **all listed entities** that SEBI has issued a new circular on **October 3, 2023** titled **“Centralized mechanism for reporting the demise of an investor through KRAs.”** NSE’s circular, numbered **NSE/CML/2023/72** and dated **October 4, 2023**, forwards the SEBI circular for reference and “necessary action” by recipients, and states that the SEBI circular is available on the NSE website.

For compliance purposes, the key point is that the subject matter is a **centralized process routed through KRAs (KYC Registration Agencies)** for reporting an investor’s death, which would affect listed entities and any related shareholder/investor servicing processes that involve transmission of securities, updating investor records, or handling deceased-investor cases. The NSE notice itself does **not** specify the operational steps, timelines, forms, or thresholds; those details would be contained in the underlying SEBI circular that accompanies it. Based on this notice alone, the only explicit timing information is the **SEBI issuance date of October 3, 2023** and the **NSE forwarding date of October 4, 2023**.

Compliance teams should therefore treat this as a trigger to review the SEBI circular and assess whether internal procedures need to be updated so that any reporting of an investor’s demise is handled through the newly centralized KRA-based mechanism rather than ad hoc processes. No fees, numeric thresholds, deadlines, or penalties are stated in the NSE notice itself.

rows.title: Extension of timeline for verification of market rumours by listed entities
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India issued Circular NSE/CML/2023/71 on October 4, 2023, to all listed entities, informing them of a SEBI circular dated September 30, 2023, titled “Extension of timeline for verification of market rumours by listed entities.” The NSE notice itself does not set out the substantive rule changes; it transmits SEBI’s circular and states that listed entities should take “necessary action” in accordance with it. In practical terms, the compliance implication is that the deadline/timeline for listed entities to verify market rumours has been extended, but this document does not specify the revised period, trigger conditions, or procedural details in the body of the NSE communication.

For a compliance team, the key points are that the affected parties are all listed entities, the governing regulator is SEBI, and the change became effective with SEBI’s circular dated September 30, 2023, as circulated by NSE on October 4, 2023. The NSE also notes that the SEBI circular is enclosed and available on the NSE website for reference, indicating that companies should review the underlying SEBI text to understand the exact extended timeline and any related disclosure or verification obligations.

rows.title: Revised Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) on application filed under Regulation 37 and 59A of SEBI (Listing Obligation and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 w.r.t. Scheme of Arrangements.
rows.summary:
This NSE circular dated September 29, 2023 revises the standard operating procedure for listed entities filing draft schemes of arrangement with stock exchanges under Regulation 37 and Regulation 59A of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015. It applies to listed companies seeking the stock exchange’s no-objection letter/NOC for schemes of arrangement, and it requires submission of the draft scheme with all documents in the relevant exchange checklist within 15 working days of the board meeting approving the draft scheme; if the company misses that 15-working-day window, it must obtain fresh board approval based on fresh financials, valuation reports, and related updated materials. For applications under Regulation 37 or 59A, the listed entity must submit audited financials for the last 3 years of any unlisted company(ies) involved in the scheme, and those financials must not be older than 6 months at the time of filing; separately, the audited financials used for the valuation report must not be older than 3 months as of the valuation report date, and the company must provide detailed workings supporting the valuation under each method used.

The board is required to consider the scheme within 7 working days of issuance of the valuation report. When filing, all documents required under the applicable SEBI circular provisions and the exchange checklist must be complete and compliant: for Regulation 37 filings, the documents listed in para (A)(2) of Part I of the SEBI Master Circular dated June 20, 2023 (as amended) must be fully submitted; for Regulation 59A filings, the documents listed in para (A)(2) of Part I of Chapter XII of the SEBI operational circular dated July 29, 2022, updated on December 1, 2022, must be fully submitted. If an entity has both listed equity securities and listed NCDs/NCRPS, it may make a single filing under Regulation 37, but it must include the additional documents required for a debt-listed company as well.

The circular also tightens the exchange-query process. If the exchange finds missing documents, material inadequacies, or non-compliance with the referenced SEBI circulars, it will return the scheme filing to the company for resubmission after compliance, and any processing fee already paid will be forfeited. If the exchange seeks clarifications, the company gets 7 working days from the date the query is raised to respond; failure to respond within that period will also result in forfeiture of the processing fee and return of the scheme documents. For debt-listed entities specifically, responses to stock exchange queries must be submitted as early as possible so the exchange can meet the requirement that the no-objection letter to SEBI be issued within a maximum of 30 days from receipt of the draft scheme. Finally, any refiling after an unsatisfactory earlier filing must be made as a completely fresh submission with all supporting documents again, including the valuation report, fairness opinion, and audit committee recommendation, and the company must pay fresh fees.

rows.title: Format of Cyber Security Incidence Disclosure under Corporate Governance Report
rows.summary:
SEBI has amended the Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements Regulations, 2015 to require listed entities to disclose cyber security incidents, breaches, or any loss of data or documents in the Corporate Governance Report under new sub-clause 27(2)(ba). This disclosure obligation applies to all listed entities and must be submitted to the stock exchanges on a quarterly basis, with the regulatory requirement effective from July 14, 2023 onward.  

In response, the National Stock Exchange has updated the existing Corporate Governance Report XBRL utility to include new mandatory fields for cyber security incident reporting. The added fields require the listed entity to state whether any cyber security incident, breach, or loss of data/documents occurred during the quarter under Regulation 27(2)(ba) on a Yes/No basis, provide the date of the event, and include brief details of the event.  

The XBRL utility changes will apply starting with the quarter ended September 30, 2023 and for all subsequent quarters. From a compliance perspective, this means listed entities must now track such incidents during each quarter and ensure the relevant disclosure is completed and filed in the quarterly Corporate Governance Report submitted to the stock exchanges.

rows.title: Filing of Related Party Transactions disclosure on NEAPS Portal
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India Limited (NSE) has reiterated that listed entities must file the six-monthly disclosure of related party transactions (RPTs) required under Regulation 23(9) of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 on the date they publish their standalone and consolidated financial results. The key change/clarification is that this disclosure must now be submitted **only in XBRL format** through the NEAPS portal, following the path **NEAPS > Compliance > Common XBRL Upload > Related Party Transactions**. NSE also notes that the XBRL utility needed to prepare and upload the filing in the prescribed format is available at that same location on NEAPS.

For compliance purposes, the circular is explicit that **XBRL submission is the only form that will be treated as compliant** with Regulation 23(9); any other submission method, **including PDF filing, will not be accepted as compliance**. This applies to all listed entities subject to the related party transaction disclosure requirement. The circular references earlier NSE circulars **NSE/CML/2021/34 dated September 6, 2021** and **NSE/CML/2021/42 dated October 19, 2021**, which dealt with XBRL-based filing of RPT disclosures for listed companies at NSE, indicating this is a reaffirmation of the filing method and compliance standard.

Listed entities are expected to ensure their internal filing process routes the RPT disclosure through the XBRL upload workflow on NEAPS at the time of financial results publication, rather than relying on any parallel PDF or alternative filing. For filing issues or technical concerns, NSE directs entities to contact **nsexbrl@nse.co.in** or use the contact details available on the NEAPS platform.

rows.title: Extension of timelines (i) for nomination in eligible demat accounts and (ii) for submission of PAN, Nomination and KYC details by physical security holders; and voluntary nomination for trading accounts
rows.summary:
This NSE circular is a cover communication to all listed entities advising them of a SEBI circular dated September 26, 2023, and asking them to note it and take any necessary action. The document itself does not create new substantive obligations; it points recipients to the underlying SEBI circular, titled **“Extension of timelines (i) for nomination in eligible demat accounts and (ii) for submission of PAN, Nomination and KYC details by physical security holders; and voluntary nomination for trading accounts.”**  

For compliance purposes, the key point is that SEBI has **extended existing deadlines** relating to two separate investor-maintenance requirements: first, the timeline for making nominations in **eligible demat accounts**; and second, the timeline for **submission of PAN, nomination, and KYC details by physical security holders**. It also addresses **voluntary nomination for trading accounts**, indicating that nomination in trading accounts remains a permitted process under the framework referenced by SEBI.  

The circular identifies the affected populations broadly as **eligible demat account holders**, **physical security holders**, and **trading account holders**. No numerical cutoff, revised final due date, or procedural detail is stated in the NSE cover note itself, so a compliance team would need to review the attached SEBI circular to determine the precise extended deadlines, the exact documentation or forms required, and the operational actions needed for customer communications, recordkeeping, and exchange/intermediary compliance.

rows.title: Redressal of investor grievances through the SEBI Complaint Redressal (SCORES) Platform and linking it to Online Dispute Resolution platform.
rows.summary: The National Stock Exchange of India circular dated September 21, 2023 is an intimation to all listed entities that SEBI has issued a new circular on September 20, 2023 titled “Redressal of investor grievances through the SEBI Complaint Redressal (SCORES) Platform and linking it to Online Dispute Resolution platform.” The NSE notice itself does not set out the detailed operational requirements; instead, it forwards the SEBI circular for “necessary action,” meaning listed companies must review and implement the SEBI-mandated grievance redressal process contained in the underlying SEBI circular. The affected entities are all listed entities on the NSE, and the subject matter is investor grievance handling through SEBI’s SCORES platform, with linkage to the Online Dispute Resolution (ODR) platform. No specific thresholds, rates, or monetary amounts are stated in the NSE circular, and no separate effective date or deadline is given in the NSE notice beyond the circular date of September 21, 2023 and the referenced SEBI circular date of September 20, 2023. For compliance purposes, the key action is to obtain and follow the enclosed SEBI circular, since the NSE communication is only a forwarding notice and indicates that the SEBI framework is now the applicable requirement for complaint redressal.

rows.title: Change in Mode of Payment w.r.t. SEBI Investor Protection and Education Fund Bank A/c
rows.summary:
This NSE circular is a notice to all listed entities that SEBI has issued Circular No. **SEBI/HO/GSD/TAD/P/CIR/2023/149 dated September 04, 2023**, titled **“Change in Mode of Payment w.r.t. SEBI Investor Protection and Education Fund Bank A/c.”** The NSE is not itself imposing a new requirement in this letter; rather, it is informing listed entities that SEBI has changed the **mode of payment** related to the **SEBI Investor Protection and Education Fund Bank Account** and is directing companies to review the attached SEBI circular and take any necessary action.

For compliance purposes, the affected parties are **all listed entities**. The notice does not provide the operative details of the payment change itself, the effective date, or any specific deadline in the text provided; it only confirms that the SEBI circular was issued on **September 04, 2023** and that listed entities should act as required under that circular. The NSE also states that the SEBI circular is enclosed for reference and is available on the NSE website (**www.nseindia.com**).

rows.title: Mandating additional disclosures by Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) that fulfil certain objective criteria
rows.summary:
This NSE circular dated September 1, 2023 informs all listed entities of a SEBI circular issued on August 24, 2023 requiring **additional disclosures from certain Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) that meet specified objective criteria**. The NSE letter itself does not set out the detailed disclosure rules, thresholds, or filing mechanics; it serves as a notice to listed companies that the SEBI circular is attached and that they should take “necessary action” in response. The affected parties are therefore **listed entities and any FPIs investing in them that fall within SEBI’s objective criteria** under the referenced circular.

From a compliance perspective, the key change is that companies with FPI shareholding may need to review their investor base and identify whether any FPI holdings trigger the SEBI-mandated enhanced disclosure regime. Because the NSE notice does not reproduce the operative provisions, a compliance officer should treat this as a prompt to obtain and implement the SEBI circular dated August 24, 2023, including any required reporting, investor due diligence, or communication with custodians/intermediaries. No separate deadline, percentage threshold, or compliance date is stated in the NSE notice itself, so the controlling requirements would be those contained in the SEBI circular referenced by this communication.

rows.title: Filing of Abridged Prospectus of Public Issues in XBRL format
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India Limited (NSE) has introduced a new requirement for **Public Issues of equity shares**: the **Abridged Prospectus must now be filed in XBRL format** with the Exchange. This is a continuation of NSE’s earlier framework for **Issue Summary Document (ISD) filing and dissemination of issue advertisements**, which the Exchange had already implemented following **SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/PoD-1/P/CIR/P/2023/29 dated February 15, 2023** and had previously communicated through **NSE Notice No. NSE/CML/2023/16 dated February 16, 2023**.

For compliance purposes, **Merchant Bankers and Issuers** are specifically required to file the **Abridged Prospectus of the Issue** in the **prescribed SEBI format** under **SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/SSEP/CIR/P/2022/14 dated February 04, 2022**, and to do so **before the opening of the issue**. The filing must be made through NSE’s online portal at **https://neaps.nseindia.com/NEWLISTINGCORP/**. This requirement is not merely optional or advisory; it is the Exchange’s stated filing mechanism for the abridged prospectus in a structured XBRL format.

The applicability date is important: the XBRL filing requirement applies to **all Public Issues of equity shares opening on or after September 01, 2023**. In other words, any equity public issue that opens from that date forward must have the abridged prospectus filed in XBRL form in advance of opening. The circular does not specify any monetary thresholds, exemptions, or phased rollout beyond this date-based applicability.

The Exchange states that the purpose of the new XBRL submission is to make the data more usable for **stakeholders such as researchers, policy makers, market analysts, and market participants**. For operational questions, the circular provides NSE contact officers **Mr. Prabal Bordiya (+91 9691113621, pbordiya@nse.co.in)** and **Ms. Jalpa Mehta (+91 9664183313, jalpam@nse.co.in)**.

rows.title: Corrigendum cum Amendment to Circular dated July 31, 2023 on Online Resolution of Disputes in the Indian Securities Market
rows.summary: This NSE circular is a forwarding notice to **all listed entities** from the National Stock Exchange of India, dated **August 7, 2023**, advising them of a new **SEBI corrigendum-cum-amendment circular dated August 4, 2023** concerning the earlier SEBI circular of **July 31, 2023** on **online resolution of disputes in the Indian securities market**. The NSE letter itself does not set out the substantive rule changes, but it makes clear that SEBI has **modified/corrected the July 31, 2023 framework** and that the amended SEBI circular is enclosed and available on the NSE website for reference and necessary action. From a compliance standpoint, the affected population is the universe of **listed entities**, and the key obligation here is to **review the August 4, 2023 SEBI amendment and implement any required action under the online dispute resolution mechanism** referenced in the original circular. No specific deadlines, thresholds, fees, or procedural details are stated in this NSE notice itself; those would come from the enclosed SEBI circular, which this communication directs recipients to follow.

rows.title: Offer for Sale framework for sale of units of Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs)and Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs)
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India notified all listed REITs and InvITs of a new SEBI framework governing the **Offer for Sale (OFS) of units** of Real Estate Investment Trusts and Infrastructure Investment Trusts, referencing SEBI Circular No. **SEBI/HO/MRD/MRD-PoD-3/P/CIR/2023/134 dated August 03, 2023** and the enclosed SEBI circular dated **July 31, 2023**. The NSE circular itself does not set out the detailed OFS mechanics; instead, it serves as an information-and-action notice that the SEBI framework is now applicable and that listed REITs/InvITs should review the attached SEBI circular and take any necessary steps at their end.

From a compliance perspective, the affected entities are **all listed InvITs and REITs**. The document does not specify any deadlines, thresholds, pricing limits, or procedural steps in the NSE notice itself, so the operative obligations would come from the SEBI circular that is referenced and enclosed. The NSE also states that the circular is available on its website for reference, indicating that compliance teams should review the underlying SEBI guidance directly to determine any filing, disclosure, timing, or transaction-process requirements associated with an OFS of REIT/InvIT units.

rows.title: Online Resolution of Disputes in the Indian Securities Market
rows.summary:
NSE Circular NSE/CML/2023/60 dated August 1, 2023 informs all listed entities that SEBI has issued Circular No. SEBI/HO/OIAE/OIAE_IAD-1/P/CIR/2023/131 on July 31, 2023 regarding “Online Resolution of Disputes in the Indian Securities Market.” The NSE communication itself does not create new substantive requirements or deadlines; rather, it transmits SEBI’s circular to listed entities and directs them to take “necessary action” as applicable.  

For compliance purposes, the key point is that the subject matter is the new SEBI framework for online dispute resolution in the Indian securities market, and the notice is addressed to all listed entities through their Company Secretaries. The NSE states that a copy of the SEBI circular is enclosed and also available on the NSE website, indicating that listed companies should review the SEBI circular directly to determine any operational, procedural, or reporting obligations arising from that framework. No thresholds, fee amounts, implementation dates, or specific procedures are set out in this NSE covering circular itself.

rows.title: Trading Window closure period under Clause 4 of Schedule B read with Regulation 9 of SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 (“PIT Regulations”) – Extending framework for restricting trading by Designated Persons (“DPs”) by freezing PAN at security level to all listed companies in a phased manner
rows.summary:
The document is a SEBI-related market conduct circular on the trading window closure framework under Clause 4 of Schedule B of the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015. It extends the existing mechanism that restricts trading by Designated Persons (“DPs”) by freezing PAN at the security level so that it applies to all listed companies, and it does so in a phased manner rather than as an immediate blanket change. The practical effect is that once a trading restriction is triggered for a DP in one listed security, trades in that security can be blocked through PAN-based controls at the market/intermediary level, reducing the risk of circumvention through multiple accounts or intermediaries.

From a compliance perspective, this means listed entities must align their insider-trading controls, DP identification, and trading window closure processes with the expanded PAN-freeze framework. Companies will need to ensure that the list of DPs is accurate and timely, that PAN details are captured correctly for all relevant persons, and that internal procedures for imposing and lifting trading window closures are coordinated with the new security-level freeze process. The document’s title indicates that the framework is being rolled out “to all listed companies in a phased manner,” so compliance teams should expect implementation sequencing, interim readiness obligations, and the need to monitor further operational guidance from the exchange/SEBI ecosystem for exact onboarding timelines and technical procedures.

rows.title: Trading Window closure period under Clause 4 of Schedule B read with Regulation 9 of SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 (“PIT Regulations”) – Extending framework for restricting trading by Designated Persons (“DPs”) by freezing PAN at security level to all listed companies in a phased manner
rows.summary:
The document is a SEBI-related circular titled “Trading Window closure period under Clause 4 of Schedule B read with Regulation 9 of the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 (“PIT Regulations”) – Extending framework for restricting trading by Designated Persons (“DPs”) by freezing PAN at security level to all listed companies in a phased manner.” Its core change is that listed companies are being moved to a mechanism where trading by Designated Persons is restricted by **freezing the PAN at the security level**, rather than relying only on traditional trading window closure controls. The purpose is to strengthen insider-trading compliance by preventing prohibited trades more effectively across the market infrastructure.

The document extends this PAN-freezing framework to **all listed companies**, but **in a phased manner**, meaning companies will be brought under the requirement according to a SEBI-mandated rollout sequence rather than all at once. It applies to **Designated Persons** under the PIT Regulations and is tied specifically to the trading restrictions contemplated under **Clause 4 of Schedule B read with Regulation 9** of the PIT Regulations. Compliance teams should therefore treat this as an additional enforcement layer on top of existing insider-trading controls, not merely a clarification of the trading window concept.

From a compliance perspective, the key operational obligation is that companies must ensure that trading by DPs is blocked at the PAN/security level during closure periods or other restricted periods, so that the prohibition is enforced through market systems and not just internal policy. rows.title: Master Circular for Listed Entities
rows.summary:
This circular package has two main compliance impacts for listed entities. First, it implements the SEBI amendments under Circular No. CIR/CFD/CMD/56/2016 dated May 27, 2016 (with reference to GN/2016-17/001 dated May 25, 2016) on reporting audit qualifications in annual audited financial results. For the financial year ended March 31, 2016, listed entities that already submitted Form A for audit reports with unmodified opinions are deemed to have complied; those that did not submit Form A must file the declaration specified in the SEBI circular, signed by the CEO, Managing Director, CFO, or Audit Committee Chairman, within 30 days from the date of this circular. Separately, all listed entities with modified audit opinions for the year ended March 31, 2016 must submit the “Statement on Impact of Audit Qualifications” in Annexure I within 60 days from the date of this circular, regardless of whether Form B was already filed.

For subsequent annual filings of audited financial results, the requirement to submit Form A or Form B is removed entirely. Going forward, all listed entities must instead submit either the unmodified-opinion declaration (for clean audit reports) or the “Statement on Impact of Audit Qualifications” (for modified opinions), in the Annexure I format, and they must do so within the same timeline that applies to submission of annual audited financial results. Annexure I requires a standalone and consolidated statement showing audited figures and adjusted figures after considering qualifications for turnover/total income, expenditure, net profit/(loss), EPS, total assets, total liabilities, net worth, and any other material financial item the management considers appropriate, followed by a separate narrative for each audit qualification covering the qualification details, type (qualified/disclaimer/adverse), frequency, management’s views, management’s estimated impact if unquantified by the auditor, reasons if the impact cannot be estimated, and the auditor’s comments, with signatures from the CEO/Managing Director, CFO, Audit Committee Chairman, and Statutory Auditor.

The second operational change concerns quarterly investor grievance reporting under Regulation 13(3) of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015. Listed entities must continue to file, within 21 days from the end of each quarter, the statement of investor complaints pending at the beginning of the quarter, received during the quarter, disposed of during the quarter, and unresolved at quarter-end, but NSE is moving this filing to an XBRL-based process through an offline Excel utility and NEAPS. The utility generates an XML file that must be uploaded via Compliance > Common XBRL upload > Investor Grievance, selecting the relevant quarter; after successful upload, the system displays a success message and sends an acknowledgement email to the registered address.

rows.title: Circular for Seeking comments on XBRL for Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process
rows.summary:
This circular, issued by the National Stock Exchange of India on June 21, 2023, is a request for comments from all listed companies and their Company Secretaries/Resolution Professionals on a proposed migration of Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP) announcements from PDF to XBRL format. The stated objective is to standardize and streamline disclosure data for CIRP-related announcements under the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015 and related SEBI provisions by moving these filings to XBRL exclusively, with the draft format attached as an annexure for feedback on the fields and structure. The exchange explains that it has already been progressively shifting compliance filings from PDF to XBRL, and that this proposal would make CIRP disclosures subject to the same machine-readable reporting approach.

For compliance purposes, the key immediate requirement is not yet a filing mandate, but a consultation response: listed entities may submit suggestions, comments, additions, or modifications to the proposed XBRL fields by email to DL-Announcement@nse.co.in, using the subject line “Comments / Feedback on the XBRL being introduced for CIRP.” The deadline for sending comments is June 25, 2023. The circular provides a detailed draft XBRL schema for CIRP announcements, indicating which fields are mandatory versus non-mandatory and the information expected to be captured, including NSE symbol, company name, BSE scrip code, MSE symbol, ISIN, type of announcement (new/update/revised), type of event, dates of initial/latest/original announcement, and report date.

The draft CIRP event taxonomy is broad and covers multiple stages of the insolvency process: application filed by the company or financial creditors, initiation of CIRP pursuant to an NCLT order, rejection/withdrawal/stay of the application, appointment or replacement of the resolution professional, prior or post-facto intimation of Committee of Creditors meetings, number of resolution plans received, filing of a resolution plan with the tribunal, prior intimation of NCLT consideration of a resolution plan, approval or rejection by the tribunal, liquidation, and an “others” category. For the company-filed CIRP case, the draft also requires the date of the board meeting approving the CIRP event, reasons for opting for CIRP, whether shareholders approved it, the date of the shareholders’ meeting, reasons if shareholder approval was not obtained, details of default in financial obligations as of the date in INR lakhs, whether the default had already been intimated to the exchange under the November 21, 2019 SEBI circular, and the date of the initial default disclosure. The circular also distinguishes between fields intended for public website dissemination and those for exchange-only use, such as certain remarks fields, showing that the proposed XBRL format will require more structured, standardized data capture than current PDF-based narrative filings.

rows.title: Circular for Seeking of comments, feedback on the XBRL for Loss of Share Certificate/Issue of Duplicate Share Certificate and Closure of Trading Window
rows.summary:
This circular is a consultation notice from the National Stock Exchange of India Limited dated June 14, 2023, asking listed entities to comment on a proposal to move certain corporate announcements from PDF submission to mandatory XBRL-only submission. The two announcement categories covered are: (1) loss of share certificate / issue of duplicate share certificate, and (2) closure of trading window, both under SEBI LODR and/or SEBI PIT requirements and any related SEBI law, regulation, circular, or provision. NSE explains that the purpose of the change is to standardize securities market data, reduce compliance burden through a uniform data structure, and improve analysis of disclosures; it also notes that XBRL filings for financials have already been mandated since 2015 and that exchanges have been progressively converting other disclosures from PDF to XBRL.

For the loss/duplicate share certificate item, the draft XBRL format requires very specific data fields, including NSE symbol, company name, BSE scrip code, MSE symbol, ISIN, announcement type (new or revision), event type (loss of share certificates, issue of duplicate share certificates, or “others”), date of original announcement, website remarks, exchange-only remarks, and date of report. It also requires transaction-level details such as the date the company received intimation/information of the lost certificate, shareholder name(s) including joint holders, folio number, number of shares, certificate number, and distinctive number ranges, plus an indication of whether multiple entries must be created for one shareholder and how many entries are needed for that shareholder. The draft further requires identification of the company’s registrar and transfer agent, with a field to specify the name if “Others” is selected, and compliance confirmations on whether the company has complied with Rule 19(3) of the Securities Contract (Regulations) Rules, 1957 and Regulation 39(2) of SEBI LODR; if not compliant, the company must state the reason. The annexure also shows that the loss-of-certificate data structure contemplates add/delete row functionality and a field for the number of shareholders who have reported loss of share certificates.

NSE is specifically soliciting comments, feedback, suggestions, and observations on additions or modifications to the fields in the draft XBRL format, recognizing that the required information is largely descriptive and derived from the existing SEBI framework. Comments must be emailed to DL-Announcement@nse.co.in in a prescribed format that includes the name of the entity/person, contact number and email address, the event category, the subject/heading/field being commented on, comments/suggestions, and detailed rationale. The email subject must read exactly: “Comments / Feedback on the XBRL being introduced for Loss of Share Certificate/ Issue of Duplicate Share Certificate and Closure of Trading Window.” The deadline for submissions is June 20, 2023. The circular does not itself impose the final migration yet; it is a consultation on the draft format, but it clearly signals that listed entities should prepare for exclusive XBRL filing of these announcement types once the format is finalized.

For questions, the Exchange directs filers to the Secretarial Compliance team at **nsexbrl@nse.co.in** or via **NEAPS > Help > Contact Us**.

rows.title: Online processing of investor service requests and complaints by RTAs
rows.summary: This NSE circular is a transmittal notice to all listed companies informing them of SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/MIRSD/MIRSD-PoD-1/P/CIR/2023/72 dated June 8, 2023, titled “Online processing of investor service requests and complaints by RTAs.” The NSE circular itself does not set out detailed substantive requirements or new thresholds; it advises that the SEBI circular is enclosed and should be reviewed for necessary action, and notes that the circular is also available on the NSE website. It is addressed to the Company Secretary of all listed companies, so the compliance impact is on listed entities, but the actual operational obligations are contained in the underlying SEBI circular rather than in this NSE covering communication. The document does not specify any effective date beyond the June 8, 2023 issuance date, nor does it mention any numbers, rates, deadlines, or procedural steps in the text provided.

rows.title: Model Tripartite Agreement between the Issuer Company, Existing Share Transfer Agent and New Share Transfer Agent as per Regulation 7(4) of SEBI (Listing Obligation and Disclosure Requirements) Regulation, 2015
rows.summary:
The notice is a transmittal circular from the National Stock Exchange of India Ltd. (NSE) dated May 26, 2023, addressed to the Company Secretary of all listed companies, informing them of SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/MIRSD/MIRSD-PoD-1/P/CIR/2023/79 dated May 25, 2023. The SEBI circular is titled “Model Tripartite Agreement between the Issuer Company, Existing Share Transfer Agent and New Share Transfer Agent as per Regulation 7(4) of SEBI (Listing Obligation and Disclosure Requirements) Regulation, 2015,” which indicates that SEBI has issued a model agreement to be used when an issuer company changes its share transfer agent.  

For compliance purposes, the key substantive point is that the tripartite agreement is intended to be entered into among three parties: the listed issuer company, the existing share transfer agent, and the new share transfer agent, in connection with Regulation 7(4) of the SEBI LODR Regulations, 2015. The document excerpt provided does not state any numerical threshold, filing deadline, implementation date beyond the circular dates themselves, or specific operational step-by-step requirements; it simply forwards SEBI’s circular and advises listed companies to take “necessary action” at their end. The NSE also notes that the SEBI circular is enclosed and available on the NSE website for reference, implying that companies undergoing a share transfer agent transition should review the SEBI-issued model agreement and align their transition documentation and arrangements accordingly.

rows.title: Dematerialization of securities of Hold Cos and SPVs held by Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs)
rows.summary: The National Stock Exchange of India issued this circular on May 23, 2023, to all listed Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) and all parties to REITs and InvITs, drawing attention to SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/DDHS-PoD-2/P/CIR/2023/76 dated May 22, 2023 on the “Dematerialization of securities of Hold Cos and SPVs held by Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs).” The NSE circular itself does not set out the substantive requirements in detail; rather, it forwards SEBI’s circular and instructs recipients to review it and take necessary action. The only concrete operational point in this document is that the SEBI circular is enclosed and also available on the NSE website for reference. For compliance purposes, this means any listed InvIT and relevant REIT/InvIT participants should immediately assess the SEBI circular’s requirements regarding dematerializing securities of holding companies and special purpose vehicles, since this NSE communication indicates the rule has been formally issued and action may be required, but it does not specify implementation dates, thresholds, or procedures on its own.

rows.title: Dematerialization of securities of Hold Cos and SPVs held by Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs)
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) has circulated SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/DDHS-PoD-2/P/CIR/2023/75 dated May 22, 2023, titled “Dematerialization of securities of Hold Cos and SPVs held by Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs).” The NSE’s own circular is Ref. No. NSE/CML/2023/35 dated May 23, 2023 and is addressed to the Company Secretary of all listed REITs and all parties to REITs and InvITs. This NSE communication does not itself set out the detailed compliance requirements; it serves to inform recipients that SEBI has issued the referenced circular, encloses it for necessary action, and notes that the circular is also available on the NSE website.

For compliance purposes, the material point in this document is that SEBI has issued a new regulatory circular specifically on the dematerialization of securities of holding companies (Hold Cos) and special purpose vehicles (SPVs) held by REITs, which implies affected REITs and their related parties must review SEBI’s May 22, 2023 instructions and implement any required actions relating to demat form/processing for those securities. No deadline, implementation date, threshold, rate, or procedural detail is stated in the NSE covering letter itself, so the operative compliance obligations must be taken from the enclosed SEBI circular rather than this brief NSE notice.

rows.title: FAQ’s on filing of announcements in XBRL format on NSE Electronic Application Processing System (NEAPS) platform.
rows.summary:
This NSE circular dated May 15, 2023 (Ref. NSE/CML/2023/34) provides FAQs on the use of XBRL format for filing certain equity-related announcements on the NEAPS platform, following the earlier circular NSE/CML/2023/28 dated March 31, 2023. It applies to all listed companies and clarifies that the Exchange is asking companies to file **both** a PDF disclosure and an XBRL submission for the covered subjects during the current transition period; the Exchange will later issue a separate circular stating the effective date after which XBRL will become the operative compliance filing.  

For now, the compliance timeline is that the **XBRL filing must be submitted within 24 hours of the PDF disclosure**, but the **PDF submission is currently the one counted for compliance purposes**. NSE specifically states that this will change only after a further circular, at which point only XBRL submissions will be treated as compliance. Companies with questions are directed to the NSE Announcements team at **takeover@nse.co.in** or the NEAPS contact details.  

The FAQ confirms the XBRL requirement covers the Regulation 30 disclosures listed in the circular, including: issuance or forfeiture of securities; split or consolidation of shares; buyback of securities; restrictions on transferability of securities; and alterations in the terms or structure of existing securities, including forfeiture, reissue of forfeited securities, alteration of calls, and redemption of securities. It also covers binding agreements not in the ordinary course of business, including shareholder agreements, JV agreements, family settlement agreements that affect management and control of the listed entity, and agreements/treaties/contracts with media companies, along with any revisions, amendments, or terminations of those agreements. In addition, it covers fraud/defaults by a promoter, key managerial personnel, or the listed entity itself; arrest of a promoter or KMP; one-time settlements with banks; resolution plans or restructuring relating to bank/financial institution borrowings including inter-creditor arrangements and corporate debt restructuring; and notices of shareholders’ meetings.  

The document further breaks down the covered securities-related events into NEAPS XBRL utility categories, including “Issuance/Allotment/Alteration/Restriction on transferability of securities,” with sub-coverage for issuance of securities under point 2.1 of the September 9, 2015 Continuous Disclosure Requirements Circular, alteration of capital under point 2.2, actions resulting in alteration of the terms or structure of existing securities under point 2.5, restrictions on transferability under point 2.4, and allotment of securities after issuance. The allotment category explicitly includes allotments of equity, preference, convertible, non-convertible, ESOP/ESPS, or other securities, and the FAQ notes that companies may be asked to provide details such as the board meeting date approving the issuance and whether any prior disclosure was made regarding the issuance.

rows.title: Introduction of Issue Summary Document (ISD) – Buy-back
rows.summary:
This circular from the National Stock Exchange of India Limited (NSE) informs all listed companies that, pursuant to SEBI Circular SEBI/HO/CFD/PoD-1/P/CIR/2023/29 dated February 15, 2023, a new **Issue Summary Document (ISD)** filing requirement has been introduced for certain buy-back transactions. The requirement applies to **buy-back of equity shares through tender offer** and **buy-back of equity shares from the open market**, and the ISD must be filed in **XBRL format**. The new SEBI requirement is effective **May 2, 2023**.

For compliance purposes, NSE has enabled the necessary filing utilities on the **NEAPS** platform to support submission of the ISD in the prescribed format. Listed entities must log in to the NEAPS portal at **https://neaps.nseindia.com/NEWLISTINGCORP**, go to **COMPLIANCE >> Common XBRL Upload**, select **“Issue Summary Document (ISD) for Buyback”** from the Module tab, then choose the relevant announcement subject, download the applicable offline Excel XBRL utility, complete it, generate the XML file, and finally upload the XML along with the required portal details through **Upload XBRL File**.

The circular does not specify any quantitative thresholds, fees, or exemption criteria; the key compliance change is the addition of a formal XBRL-based ISD filing workflow for buy-back events. Companies undertaking covered buy-back transactions after the effective date must use this process to ensure their disclosures are submitted correctly. For questions, NSE directs users to the **Announcements team at takeover@nse.co.in** or to the contact details available on the NEAPS platform.

rows.title: FAQs on the submission of the quarterly Corporate Governance Report.
rows.summary:
This circular from the National Stock Exchange of India dated April 10, 2023 is a guidance-only FAQ document for listed entities filing the quarterly Corporate Governance Report on the NSE Electronic Application Processing System (NEAPS) / data entry / XBRL utility. It does not amend law, SEBI regulations, or prior exchange circulars, but it does set out the Exchange’s required approach for completing specific fields in the submission, and listed entities are instructed to follow it accordingly.

For the Board composition section, if a director does not have a DIN or PAN, the company must enter the prescribed dummy values only — DIN `99999999` and PAN `ZZZZZ9999Z` — and explain the reason in the company remarks. The report must show the director’s correct and complete name as per PAN; if the name or PAN is inconsistent, the Exchange may seek clarification or issue an advisory letter. For chairperson classification, where the chairperson is the promoter or is related to the promoter and is also an Executive Director or Non-Executive Director, the company must select Code `C` together with Code `ED/NED`; where the chairperson is not related to promoters and is also an Executive Director or Non-Executive Director, the company must select Code `C` and Code `ED/NED` as well.

The circular also standardizes how appointment and re-appointment dates are to be entered. For Independent Directors, the initial appointment date is the start of the first term after the Companies Act, 2013 took effect, and the re-appointment date is the start of the second term; the FAQ gives the example that if a person served from 2011, was treated as an Independent Director from 2014, and was re-appointed in 2019, then 2014 is the initial appointment date and 2019 is the re-appointment date. For directors other than Independent Directors, the initial appointment date is the original date they were inducted onto the board, and re-appointment means the date of the current term.

The re-appointment field is mandatory for Independent Directors; if the first term is still continuing and the director has not yet been re-appointed, the company must repeat the initial appointment date in the re-appointment field. The cessation date field is mandatory only when the director’s tenure has ended because of death, resignation, removal, or completion of term, and if a director has died, the reason must be stated in the remarks column. Tenure details are mandatory only for Independent Directors, and the tenure is to be computed up to the end of the current/approved term as applicable.
