rows.title: Filing of announcements in XBRL format on NSE Electronic Application Processing System (NEAPS) platform
rows.summary:
NSE has announced that, effective **January 28, 2023**, listed companies can begin filing certain **SEBI LODR** disclosures in **XBRL format** on the **NEAPS** portal, specifically through **COMPLIANCE >> Common XBRL Upload >> Equity Announcement-XBRL**. The initial announcements covered are: **Regulation 29 prior intimation of a Board meeting**; and under **Regulation 30**, disclosures relating to **changes in directors, key managerial personnel (MD, CEO, CFO, Company Secretary, etc.), auditor, compliance officer, or share transfer agent**; **outcomes of Board meetings for dividend, buyback, bonus issue, or voluntary delisting**; and **acquisition(s), schemes of arrangement (including amalgamation/merger/demerger/restructuring), or sale/disposal of any unit, division, subsidiary, or other restructuring**.

For now, companies must still make the disclosure in **PDF mode** as currently required under Regulation 30, but NSE is adding an additional obligation to file the **same disclosure in XBRL within 24 hours of the PDF submission**. NSE also states that this is an interim arrangement: at a later date, to be communicated separately, the exchange will move to **XBRL-only submission** for these announcements. Compliance teams should therefore treat the PDF filing as the immediate disclosure obligation and the XBRL upload as a mandatory follow-on filing within the 24-hour window.

The filing process requires the user to log in to **https://neaps.nseindia.com/NEWLISTINGCORP**, navigate to the common XBRL upload section, choose the relevant announcement subject, download the applicable **offline Excel XBRL utility**, complete it, generate the **XML file**, and then upload that XML on the portal after entering the required details. Questions are to be directed to NSE’s Announcements team at **takeover@nse.co.in** or via the contact details shown on NEAPS.

rows.title: Standard Operating Process under SEBI(PIT) Regulations, 2015 for ensuring compliance with Structured Digital Database (“SDD”)
rows.summary:
This circular reiterates that all listed entities must maintain a Structured Digital Database (“SDD”) under Regulations 3(5) and 3(6) of the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015, and it is specifically aimed at listed companies that are subject to NSE’s compliance monitoring. It refers to earlier NSE circulars that had already set the timeline for submitting the SDD compliance certificate for the quarters ended September 30, 2022 and December 31, 2022, and another circular dated November 4, 2022 that described the consequences of non-compliance with Regulations 3(5) and 3(6).

The key compliance consequence highlighted here is that if a listed entity is found non-compliant with the SDD requirements, the Exchange will display a non-compliance warning on the company’s “Get Quote” page on the Exchange website starting from the next trading day, and that status will remain visible until the Exchange satisfactorily verifies that the company has fully complied. The circular further clarifies an additional disclosure consequence: the details of the compliance officer will also be displayed on the same “Get Quote” page where this non-compliance information is published.

No new substantive SDD filing deadline or numerical threshold is introduced in this circular itself; rather, it reinforces the existing obligation to maintain SDD records and warns of the Exchange’s public disclosure mechanism for companies that fail to comply. It also states that this circular supersedes NSE circular reference number NSE/CML/2023/09 dated January 25, 2023, and requests all listed companies to take note and comply accordingly.

rows.title: Standard Operating Process under SEBI(PIT) Regulations, 2015 for ensuring compliance with Structured Digital Database (“SDD”)
rows.summary:
This circular requires all listed entities to note and comply with the existing Structured Digital Database (SDD) obligations under Regulations 3(5) and 3(6) of the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015, and it updates how compliance will be evidenced and displayed by the Exchange. For listed entities that are subject to Regulation 24A of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015, the Secretarial Auditor must now specifically confirm SDD compliance in the Annual Secretarial Audit Report; companies should proactively inform their Secretarial Auditor of this requirement so it is explicitly covered in the audit.  

The circular also reiterates the Exchange’s non-compliance consequences under its earlier Circular No. NSE/CML/2022/52 dated November 4, 2022: if a listed company is found non-compliant with Reg. 3(5) and 3(6), the Exchange will display on the company’s “Get Quote” page that the company is non-compliant with SDD, starting from the next trading day and continuing until the Exchange has satisfactorily verified full compliance. In addition to the company-level non-compliance notice, the circular clarifies that the name of the compliance officer will also be displayed on the same “Get Quote” page where this information is published.  

The circular references earlier NSE communications that set timelines for submitting the SDD Compliance Certificate for the quarters ended September 30, 2022 and December 31, 2022, and it is intended as a further compliance advisory on top of those prior directions. No new monetary threshold is introduced, but the operational impact is significant because failure to maintain or demonstrate SDD compliance may now result in public disclosure on the Exchange website linked both to the company and the compliance officer. The circular is effective immediately and applies to all listed companies.

rows.title: Facility of conducting meetings of unit holders of REITs through Video Conferencing or Other Audio-Visual means
rows.summary:
This NSE circular dated 13 January 2023 is a forwarding communication to all listed companies from the National Stock Exchange of India, alerting them to a SEBI circular issued one day earlier, on 12 January 2023, titled “Facility of conducting meetings of unit holders of REITs through Video Conferencing or Other Audio-Visual means.” The NSE letter itself does not impose new substantive obligations; it informs recipients that SEBI has issued the referenced circular and that a copy is enclosed and available on the NSE website for necessary action.

For compliance purposes, the key point is that the underlying SEBI circular concerns Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) and the manner in which meetings of REIT unit holders may be conducted, specifically permitting meetings through video conferencing or other audio-visual means. No implementation deadline, threshold, rate, or procedural detail is stated in the NSE cover note itself, and the document does not specify which listed entities beyond REIT-related stakeholders are directly affected. A compliance officer would need to review the attached SEBI circular dated 12 January 2023 to determine the precise meeting-process requirements, any conditions for using electronic modes, and any timeline for adoption or compliance.

rows.title: Facility of conducting meetings of unit holders of InvITs through Video Conferencing or Other Audio-Visual means
rows.summary: This NSE circular is a transmission notice, not an independent rule change: on 13 January 2023, NSE informed listed companies of SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHS_Div2/P/CIR/2023/14 dated 12 January 2023, titled “Facility of conducting meetings of unit holders of InvITs through Video Conferencing or Other Audio-Visual means.” The NSE communication itself does not set out the substantive requirements, deadlines, thresholds, or procedures; it simply states that a copy of the SEBI circular is enclosed for “necessary action” and is available on the NSE website. For compliance purposes, the relevant affected entities are InvITs and the meetings of their unit holders, with the subject matter being permission/facilitation to conduct such meetings through video conferencing or other audio-visual means. The document should therefore be treated as a notice to review and implement the operative requirements in the underlying SEBI circular, rather than as the source of those requirements itself.

rows.title: Circular for seeking of comments / feedback on the XBRL being introduced for submission of Announcements pertaining to Corporate Debt Restructuring
rows.summary:
This circular, issued by NSE on January 11, 2023, does not itself impose a finalized rule change; it seeks comments and feedback from listed entities on a proposal to migrate corporate announcements relating to Corporate Debt Restructuring (CDR) from PDF submissions to an XBRL-only filing format under SEBI LODR Regulation 30 and the relevant SEBI circulars. The practical change being proposed is that CDR announcements would no longer be filed as free-form PDF disclosures; instead, listed companies would be required to submit the information in a standardized XBRL template so the stock exchange can capture structured, comparable data across issuers.

The circular makes clear that the affected parties are listed entities that make CDR-related announcements, whether the CDR is voluntary or referred by lenders/creditors. It explains that this proposal is part of a broader exchange effort to convert disclosure filings from PDF to XBRL, following the earlier implementation of XBRL-based reporting for financial filings from 2015 onward, with the stated goals of standardizing market data, easing compliance burden, and improving data analysis. No penalty or implementation date for mandatory filing is stated in this document; instead, the current deadline is for feedback on the draft format.

Comments, suggestions, and observations were requested by email to DL-Announcement@nse.co.in no later than January 13, 2023, and the email subject line had to read “Comments / Feedback on the XBRL being introduced for Corporate Debt Restructuring.” The circular also specifies the information the draft XBRL template would require: general identifiers such as NSE symbol, company name, BSE scrip code, MSE symbol, ISIN, disclosure stage (initial or update), disclosure type (new or revision), dates of the initial and latest announcements, and separate remarks fields for website dissemination versus exchange-only use, along with the date of report. For an initial CDR disclosure, the template asks whether the restructuring is voluntary or lender/creditor-referred, the date of the board meeting approving CDR, reasons for opting for CDR, details of the referring lenders/creditors, details of the loan subject to restructuring, and a brief description of the proposal. For update disclosures, it requires the implementation stage of the scheme, execution date of the agreement, parties, principal terms, a summary of the executed agreement, and, where applicable, final RBI/lender-approved package details, lender names, securities involved, interest and repayment schedules, negative/restrictive covenants, any other SEBI compliance disclosures, and any additional information, again with separate website and exchange-only remarks fields.

rows.title: Comprehensive Framework on Offer for Sale (OFS) of Shares through Stock Exchange Mechanism
rows.summary:
This NSE communication is a forwarding notice, not a new rule in itself. It informs all members that SEBI issued Circular No. SEBI/HO/MRD/MRD-PoD-3/P/CIR/2023/10 on January 10, 2023, titled “Comprehensive Framework on Offer for Sale (OFS) of Shares through Stock Exchange Mechanism,” and that the SEBI circular is enclosed and available on the NSE website for reference and necessary action.

For a compliance team, the key point is that any entity using, facilitating, or participating in the stock-exchange mechanism for an OFS must review and implement the SEBI framework referenced in the January 10, 2023 circular. However, this NSE note itself does not describe the substantive OFS requirements, procedural changes, thresholds, deadlines, or affected issuer categories; it only confirms that SEBI has issued the framework and that members should take action as required by that underlying SEBI circular. No separate effective date beyond the SEBI circular date of January 10, 2023 is stated in this notice, and no additional numerical limits or operational instructions appear in the text provided.

rows.title: Circular for seeking comments, feedback from Listed Entities for XBRL being introduce for  submission of Announcements pertaining to all Notices of Shareholders Meeting in phase manner
rows.summary:
NSE Circular No. **NSE/CML/2023/04** dated **January 10, 2023** is a **consultation circular**, not yet a final implementation notice, seeking comments from listed companies on a proposal to move from **PDF to XBRL** for submitting **corporate announcements relating to notices of shareholders’ meetings** under the **SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015** and the SEBI circular dated **September 9, 2015**, as amended. The exchange says the broader policy direction is to standardize market data and reduce compliance burden by using a uniform XBRL filing structure, building on the XBRL-based filing framework already used for financial reporting since 2015 and being expanded in phases to other LODR disclosures.

For the specific item covered in this consultation, the proposed change is that announcements for **all notices of shareholders’ meetings** would be filed **exclusively in XBRL**, initially in **Phase I**, where only the **agenda heading details** are captured; **Phase II**, which would capture **all details forming part of the notice**, is stated to come later in a separate circular. The draft XBRL template attached to the circular shows that the filing would require basic company and event identification fields such as **NSE symbol, company name, BSE scrip code, MSE symbol, ISIN, event type** (AGM, EGM, postal ballot, NCLT/court-convened meeting, or others), **mode of meeting** (physical or VC/OAVM), **meeting date/time/place**, **postal ballot voting end date**, and the **number of agenda/business items**. It also requires disclosure of the **resolution/agenda type** (ordinary resolution, special resolution, others) and a **resolution header/searchable content**, with dropdown-based standardized resolution headings.

The draft annexure indicates that the “ordinary resolution” dropdown/category includes items such as **adoption of financial statements, appointment/re-appointment of directors and auditors, bonus issue, dividend declaration/confirmation, change in authorized capital, donation to charitable trusts, office of profit, promoter re-classification, remuneration/ratification of statutory auditors**, and related governance items; the list continues beyond the excerpt provided. The circular further distinguishes between **“remarks (website dissemination)”** and **“remarks for exchange (not for website dissemination)”**, so companies would need to prepare content with the correct disclosure channel in mind. NSE requests that listed entities send **comments, feedback, suggestions, or observations** on the Phase I draft format by email to **DL-Announcement@nse.co.in**, using the subject line **“Comments / Feedback on the XBRL being introduced for notice of shareholders meeting”**, and the deadline for submission is **January 12, 2023**. The circular is addressed to **all listed companies**, but it is explicitly a request for input on the proposed phased XBRL reporting structure rather than an immediate operative compliance mandate.

rows.title: Filing of SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011 disclosure to Exchange
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India is changing the filing process for disclosures made under the SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011. Effective **January 07, 2023**, such SAST disclosures must be submitted to the Exchange via the dedicated **Takeover email ID: takeover@nse.co.in**, rather than through the earlier filing route referenced in the Exchange’s prior circulars on the new digital portal.

This circular is a continuation of NSE Circular No. **NSE/CML/2022/03 dated January 06, 2022** and Circular Ref. No. **NSE/CML/2022/09 dated February 17, 2022**, which had informed members about the launch of the Exchange’s new digital portal for filings. The document does not change the underlying SEBI SAST disclosure obligations themselves; it changes the **submission channel** for those disclosures to the Exchange. Companies required to make SAST filings should direct all such filings to the takeover email address starting on the effective date.

For compliance purposes, the Exchange also notes that relevant contact details for Exchange officers are available on the **NEAPS portal**, and companies may contact the designated officers for issues and queries related to SEBI (SAST) filings.

rows.title: Relaxation from compliance with certain provisions of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 –Reg.
rows.summary:
This circular from the National Stock Exchange of India Ltd. is a transmission notice to all listed companies informing them of a SEBI circular dated January 5, 2023, titled “Relaxation from compliance with certain provisions of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 – Reg.” The NSE circular itself, dated January 6, 2023, does not introduce new substantive requirements; it forwards SEBI’s January 5, 2023 circular and instructs companies to review it and take necessary action, with the SEBI circular also made available on the NSE website.

For compliance purposes, the key point is that SEBI has granted a relaxation from compliance with certain provisions of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015, but this NSE note does not state the exact provisions relaxed, the scope of the relaxation, or any conditions, deadlines, or thresholds within the body of this letter. Therefore, the compliance team should treat this as a notification affecting all listed companies and should obtain and review the enclosed SEBI circular itself for the precise regulatory relief, effective dates, and any filing or reporting obligations that may apply.

rows.title: Circular for seeking comments, feedback from Listed Entities for XBRL being introduce for issuance of securities, alteration of capital, action which will result in alteration of the terms or structure of any existing securities, any restriction on transferability of securities or forfeiture of securities, alteration, any restriction on transferability of securities.
rows.summary:
This NSE circular (Ref. No. NSE/CML/2023/01 dated January 5, 2023) is a consultation notice to all listed companies seeking comments on a proposal to replace PDF-based corporate announcement filings with XBRL-only submissions for a defined set of Regulation 30/LODR events. The proposed XBRL migration would apply to announcements relating to issuance or forfeiture of securities, split or consolidation of shares, alterations in capital, actions that change the terms or structure of existing securities, restrictions on transferability of securities, reissue of forfeited securities, alterations of calls, redemption of securities, and similar events under the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015 and the relevant SEBI circulars.

For compliance teams, the key change is that these announcements would no longer be filed in PDF format but would need to be submitted exclusively in XBRL, using the standardised data fields being drafted by the exchanges. The circular explains that the purpose is to standardise securities-market data, reduce compliance burden over time, and enable more uniform analysis of listed entities’ disclosures; it also notes that listed entities already file XBRL for financial filings and that exchanges have been moving other SEBI-regulated filings from PDF to XBRL in phases. The draft XBRL template attached to the circular shows that the filing will require structured fields such as NSE symbol, company name, BSE scrip code, MSE symbol, ISIN, event type, and detailed event-specific information.

The consultation specifically asks listed entities to comment on the proposed fields, including any additions, modifications, or other observations, because the data requirements are described as largely based on existing LODR provisions and SEBI circular requirements. Comments must be emailed to DL-Announcement@nse.co.in in the prescribed format identifying the entity/person, contact number and email, the event category, the relevant subject/heading/field, the suggested change, and the detailed rationale. When sending comments, the subject line must read: “Comments / Feedback on the XBRL being introduced for issuance or forfeiture of securities, alteration, any restriction on transferability of securities”.

The deadline for submitting feedback was January 8, 2023. The circular is signed by National Stock Exchange of India Limited and encloses the draft XBRL format for the proposed announcement types; the visible portion of the draft shows, for example, that fund-raising/issuance filings will need event classification such as new issuance versus cancellation/termination, the reasons for cancellation, board meeting date and times, and whether prior intimation of the board meeting was given to the stock exchange.

rows.title: Revised Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) on application filed under Regulation 37 and 59A of SEBI (Listing Obligation and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 w.r.t. Scheme of Arrangements.
rows.summary:
This circular, effective from **December 20, 2022**, issues a **revised standard operating procedure (SOP)** for listed entities seeking a stock exchange **No-Objection Certificate (NOC)** for a **scheme of arrangement** filed under **Regulation 37** and, where applicable, **Regulation 59A** of the **SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015**. A draft scheme must be filed with the exchange **within 15 working days of the board meeting** approving the draft scheme; if that deadline is missed, the company must obtain **fresh board approval** based on **updated financials, valuation report, etc.** The filing must be complete and include all documents required under the relevant exchange checklist and the cited SEBI circulars.

For schemes involving **unlisted company(ies)**, the company must submit the **audited financials of the last 3 years**, and those financials must **not be older than 6 months** at the time of submission; these financials are specifically to be used by the valuer for the **Income Approach**. When the exchange issues its observation letter, it will require an **undertaking** from the listed entity confirming that the unlisted company financials will still be **no more than 6 months old when the scheme papers are filed with NCLT**. For valuation methods **other than the Income Approach**, the audited financials used for valuation must be **no older than 3 months**. In addition, the board must consider the scheme **within 7 working days of the valuation report being issued**.

The SOP also tightens the completeness and submission requirements at the exchange level: under **Regulation 37**, the documents listed in **para (I)(A)(2) of the SEBI Master Circular dated November 23, 2021 (as amended)** must be fully complete; under **Regulation 59A**, the documents in **para (I)(A)(2) of SEBI Circular dated November 17, 2022** must be fully complete. If a listed entity has both **specified securities** and **NCDs/NCRPS** listed, it must make a **single filing under Regulation 37**, and also attach the **additional documents required for debt-listed companies**.

If the exchange finds missing documents, requests clarifications, or identifies material inadequacies or non-compliance, it will return the scheme for rectification and allow the company **7 working days** to cure the defects. If the company does not respond within that period, any **fees paid for processing will be forfeited** and the scheme documents will be returned. For **debt-listed entities**, the company must respond to exchange queries **as early as possible** so that the exchange can meet the requirement that the **NOC to SEBI must be issued within 30 days from receipt of the draft scheme**. If responses are still not provided in time, the company may have to **re-file the scheme as a fresh application**, and the **processing fees will again be forfeited**; any such refiling must include a **fresh valuation report, fairness opinion, audit committee recommendation, and related documents**.

rows.title: Clarifications with respect to SEBI Circular no. SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHSRACPOD1/P/CIR/2022/156 dated November 17, 2022 (“SEBI Circular”), on Scheme(s) of Arrangement by entities who have listed their Non-convertible Debt securities (NCDs)/ Non-convertible Redeemable Preference shares (NCRPS)’
rows.summary:
This NSE circular dated December 19, 2022 provides implementation clarifications for SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHS-RACPOD1/P/CIR/2022/156 dated November 17, 2022, which introduced the procedure for schemes of arrangement involving entities that have listed non-convertible debt securities (NCDs) and/or non-convertible redeemable preference shares (NCRPS) under the amended LODR provisions (Regulations 59A/94A). The clarified requirements apply only to listed entities whose Board meeting approving the scheme of arrangement was held after November 14, 2022, which is the effective date of the relevant amendment to the SEBI LODR Regulations.

For the draft scheme comment process, entities with both specified securities and NCDs/NCRPS listed must submit the report on complaints/comments to the stock exchanges within 7 days after the expiry of the 21-day public posting period for the draft scheme on the websites of the stock exchanges and the listed entity. Entities that have only NCDs/NCRPS listed must submit the complaints/comments report within 7 days after the expiry of a 10-day posting period. This means the public consultation period differs depending on whether the company also has listed specified securities, and the submission deadline runs from the end of that applicable posting period.

On timelines for stock exchange queries, issuers with only NCDs/NCRPS listed must respond to any stock exchange queries within 7 working days of the query being raised; incomplete replies will be treated as non-submission. This is tied to the requirement that the “No-Objection” letter to SEBI must be issued within a maximum of 30 days from receipt of the draft scheme of arrangement. The circular also clarifies that these response timelines apply only to issuers with only NCDs/NCRPS listed, while for entities with specified securities the timelines set out in the joint SOP continue to govern.

For filing mechanics, listed entities with both specified securities and NCDs/NCRPS are required to make a single filing of the draft scheme under Regulation 37, and that filing must also include the additional documents required for an NCD/NCRPS-listed company under Regulation 59A. If, under a scheme of arrangement, the issuer proposes to raise further NCDs without using the Electronic Bidding Platform (EBP), it must separately obtain an exemption from SEBI from the EBP requirement.

The circular also clarifies that where debenture-holder approval is required under Point 12 of the SEBI circular, the valuation/threshold for that approval is to be determined in accordance with Section 230 of the Companies Act, 2013. Finally, if the scheme provides for an exit offer to dissenting holders of NCDs/NCRPS, the Board of Directors must specifically comment on that exit offer when recommending the draft scheme, and any such exit-offer provision must be expressly included in the scheme itself.

rows.title: Circular pertaining to submission of the Aadhar details in the Announcement/Offer Documents submitted to the Exchange.
rows.summary:
This NSE Listing Circular (Ref. No. NSE/CML/2022/60, dated December 19, 2022) requires all listed entities and all issuers proposing to list securities with the Exchange to stop disclosing Aadhaar numbers or any Aadhaar-related information in announcements, offer documents, or any other public document submitted to the Exchange, with immediate effect. The circular is based on Section 29(4) of the Aadhaar Act, 2016 (as amended in 2019), which prohibits public disclosure of Aadhaar numbers, demographic information, or photographs collected under the Act except as specifically permitted, and further requires any Aadhaar information that must be published under other applicable laws to be published only in masked form.

For listed entities, the Exchange specifically observed that some are submitting newspaper clippings that contain Aadhaar numbers or Aadhaar cards along with unrelated news on the same page; the circular directs entities to submit only the clipping relevant to their own announcement and not the full newspaper page. For entities/issuers preparing draft offer documents or offer documents, the circular says Aadhaar numbers or Aadhaar-related information of promoters or others that are required under applicable SEBI regulations (including the SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018 and the SEBI (Issue and Listing of Non-Convertible Securities) Regulations, 2021) must be provided to the Exchange separately, and must not appear in the draft offer document, offer document, or any other public document.

In practical compliance terms, the document imposes an immediate obligation to review all submissions to the Exchange and ensure that any Aadhaar references are removed from public-facing materials or masked where disclosure is legally required, while any required Aadhaar details are routed separately to the Exchange through non-public channels. The circular is directed to Company Secretaries of all listed entities and prospective issuers, and it is a mandatory compliance instruction rather than a discretionary best practice.

rows.title: Circular for filing of Equity announcements and Financial Results to be made available on the NEAPS (NSE Electronic Application Processing System) platform
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India Limited issued this circular to move all **Equity Announcements** and **Financial Results** filings onto the **NEAPS (NSE Electronic Application Processing System) portal only**, consolidating these submissions under a single platform. This change applies to **all listed companies** and becomes effective **December 17, 2022**. The circular states that filings must now be made in the same manner as was available on NEAPS in **February 2022**, and it is a continuation of earlier circulars dated **January 6, 2022 (NSE/CML/2022/03)**, **February 17, 2022 (NSE/CML/2022/09)**, and **July 8, 2022 (NSE/CML/2022/34)** regarding the new digital portal.

The circular then specifies the filing procedure depending on the board meeting agenda. If the board meeting outcome contains **only financial results** as the agenda item, the company must file the **quarterly, half-yearly, or annual financial results in PDF format only under the “Quick Results” module** on NEAPS. If the board meeting outcome includes **multiple agenda items along with financial results**, the company must file the disclosure **both under the “Announcement” module and the “Quick Result” module** on NEAPS. In addition, the **XBRL version of the financial results** must be filed under the **“Full Results” module** on NEAPS.

For operational support, the Exchange notes that the **contact details of the relevant Exchange officers are available on the NEAPS portal**, and companies are expected to use those contacts for issues and queries related to filings on the platform. The compliance implication is that companies should transition any remaining Equity Announcement and Financial Results workflows to NEAPS by the effective date and ensure internal filing procedures distinguish between single-agenda financial results filings, multi-agenda board outcomes, and XBRL submissions so that each is submitted in the correct NEAPS module.

rows.title: FAQ’s - Disclosure of holding of specified securities and Holding of specified securities in dematerialized form
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India issued this circular on December 14, 2022 (Ref. No. NSE/CML/2022/57) to all listed companies, updating its guidance in the form of FAQs on filing the shareholding pattern under Regulation 31 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, specifically on disclosure of holding of specified securities and dematerialized holdings. The circular does not create a new standalone legal regime, but it directs companies to comply with the listing regulations and any other applicable regulations as amended from time to time, and says the FAQs are for guidance only. It is aimed at improving the accuracy and consistency of the quarterly Shareholding Pattern report submitted to the Stock Exchange.

A key clarification is how to report deceased promoters or promoter group individuals: if an individual in the promoter or promoter group has died and the shares have not yet been transmitted to the legal heirs as of quarter-end, the company must continue to show the deceased person’s name in the promoter/promoter group section and add a detailed note explaining the situation. Once transmission is completed, the company may remove the deceased promoter’s name from subsequent shareholding pattern filings and must instead include the legal heir(s)’ name(s), again with a detailed note describing the transmission. If a promoter or promoter group company has been wound up or dissolved after merger/amalgamation, the company must add detailed notes in the shareholding pattern from the forthcoming quarter.

The circular also clarifies that a shareholder already disclosed in Table II, which covers promoter and promoter group shareholding, must not be repeated in Table III, which covers public shareholders; a person or entity that qualifies as promoter/promoter group should appear only in Table II and not again in Table III. Where a shareholder could fit more than one Table III category, the company must classify that holder only once, under the category that appears first in the prescribed shareholding-pattern format; shareholding categories must be unique and not duplicated. If a shareholder category contains multiple sub-categories, the number of shares must be separately reported under each relevant sub-category in column no. (XV) of Table III.

For changes in promoter status, the circular says a promoter’s name cannot be removed from the shareholding pattern merely because the shares were transferred or sold during the quarter; removal is allowed only after the stock exchange approves the reclassification request. Until that approval is granted, the company must continue showing the promoter/promoter group with nil shareholding. For disclosures on significant beneficial owners, if the company has none, it must select “No” in the declaration sheet. For trust or HUF holdings, the company may name the Trust or HUF itself, but if the promoter or promoter group consists of a Trust or HUF, it must also place the trustee’s name or karta’s name, respectively, in brackets.

Finally, the circular permits companies to upload the XML file generated from the BSE utility into NEAPS for shareholding-pattern filing; if there are upload issues, companies are instructed to email the error to nsexbrl@nse.co.in. The exchange’s disclaimer emphasizes that these FAQs are guidance only and do not override the legal requirements contained in the applicable law, SEBI regulations, or exchange circulars.

rows.title: Guidance note on inclusion of "object of the issue" in case of preferential issue and in Qualified institutions placement.
rows.summary:
This NSE guidance note, dated **December 13, 2022** and issued by the **National Stock Exchange of India Limited**, clarifies how listed companies must disclose the **“Object of the issue”** in documents relating to **preferential issues** and **Qualified Institutions Placements (QIPs)** under **Chapter V and Chapter VI of the SEBI (ICDR) Regulations, 2018**. It was issued after the **November 21, 2022** amendment to the SEBI ICDR Regulations, which introduced a requirement to appoint a **SEBI-registered Credit Rating Agency (CRA)** as the **monitoring agency** for tracking utilization of issue proceeds where the issue size of a QIP or preferential issue **exceeds INR 100 crore**. The Exchange states that issuers have been using inconsistent disclosure formats and, especially where there are multiple objects, have not always made the funding requirement for each object clear enough for effective monitoring.

The guidance requires issuers to present the purpose of fund-raising under a separate heading titled **“Object of the issue”** in the **QIP placement document** and the **notice to shareholders for preferential issues**. Each object must be described **clearly and specifically**; vague or open-ended descriptions are not acceptable. The amount proposed to be used for each object must also be stated clearly. If an exact amount cannot be quantified, the issuer may provide a **broad range**, but that range must be a **realistic estimate**, must be supported by an explanation for using a range, and the range spread cannot exceed **plus/minus 10%** of the amount specified for that object.

The note also imposes restrictions on how proceeds are allocated and tracked: the total issue size earmarked for the identified objects must be used **only** for those stated objects and **cannot be shifted to General Corporate Purposes (GCP)**. If any amount is allocated to **GCP**, it cannot exceed **25% of the funds raised** in the relevant preferential issue or QIP. Issuers must additionally disclose the **tentative timeline** for using the proceeds for each object and specify **how unutilized funds will be held** until full deployment. These disclosure requirements are intended to support the CRA monitoring function for issues above the INR 100 crore threshold.

For compliance and processing purposes, the Exchange says it will check adherence to these disclosure requirements when reviewing applications under **Regulation 28(1) of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2018** for **in-principle approval** before allotment of securities. The guidance applies to **all QIP and preferential issues approved by the Board of Directors on or after December 13, 2022**.

rows.title: Circular for Seeking of comments, feedback on the XBRL for Regulation 30- OTS, ICA, Agreements, Fraud and Default
rows.summary:
This circular, issued by NSE Listing Department on November 22, 2022 (Ref. No. NSE/CML/2022/55), seeks feedback from all listed companies on a proposed shift from PDF to XBRL filing for certain Regulation 30 announcements under SEBI LODR. The specific disclosures proposed to become XBRL-only are: (1) one-time settlement (OTS) / inter-creditors agreements (ICA), (2) agreements that are binding but not in the ordinary course of business, including any revisions, amendments, or terminations of such agreements, and (3) frauds/defaults by a promoter, key managerial personnel, or the listed entity itself, including arrest of a promoter or key managerial personnel. The exchange says the objective is to standardize and structure these corporate disclosure data points so they can be filed in a uniform format, reduce compliance burden over time, and improve data analysis by the stock exchange; the proposal is aligned to SEBI LODR and the SEBI circular dated September 9, 2015, as amended.

The circular does not impose an immediate final filing rule in this document itself; rather, it invites comments, suggestions, and observations on the proposed XBRL fields and any additions or modifications needed. Feedback was requested by email to DL-Announcement@nse.co.in in a specified format containing the name of the entity/person, contact number and email address, the event category, the relevant subject/heading/field, the comment or suggestion, and the detailed rationale. The email subject line had to be: “Comments / Feedback on the XBRL being introduced for OTS/ICA, Agreements, Fraud/Defaults,” and comments were due no later than November 28, 2022.

The attached draft XBRL format shows the proposed data capture requirements for OTS/ICA disclosures. For such filings, the issuer would need to report identifiers such as NSE symbol, company name, BSE scrip code, MSE symbol, and ISIN, then specify the event type as either ICA or OTS. If the event is an ICA, the filer must also indicate the stage of disclosure, choosing from: decision to initiate resolution of loans/borrowings; signing of the ICA by lenders; finalization of the resolution plan; implementation of the resolution plan; or salient features of the resolution/restructuring plan decided by lenders, excluding commercial secrets. The draft also requires disclosure of whether the filing is being made for a listed company, the name of the entity for which the disclosure is filed, the relationship with the listed company, the disclosure date, and the meeting in which OTS was considered, if applicable, limited to Board Meeting or Audit Committee Meeting.

rows.title: : Master Circular on issuance of No Objection Certificate (NOC) for release of 1% of Issue Amount
rows.summary:
SEBI has issued a new master circular dated **November 7, 2022** titled **“Master Circular on issuance of No Objection Certificate (NOC) for release of 1% of Issue Amount,”** and the National Stock Exchange of India circulated it to **all companies whose securities are listed on SEBI-recognized stock exchanges** on **November 9, 2022**. The document itself is a transmittal notice from NSE rather than a substantive rule change summary, but it makes clear that the updated SEBI circular is now the operative guidance for obtaining an **NOC for release of 1% of the issue amount**.  

For compliance purposes, the key point is that any listed company subject to the SEBI issue-allotment/issuance framework that seeks release of this **1% of issue amount** must follow the updated procedure and conditions contained in the SEBI master circular. The NSE notice does not restate the underlying conditions, timelines, or documentary requirements, so the compliance team should review the SEBI circular directly to determine the exact application steps, supporting documents, and any preconditions for issuance of the NOC.  

The notice indicates the circular is available on the NSE website and is issued **for reference and necessary action**, meaning affected issuers should ensure their corporate finance, secretarial, and listing compliance teams incorporate the updated SEBI instructions into any pending or future request for release of the 1% amount.

rows.title: Addendum to SEBI Circular on Development of Passive Funds
rows.summary:
This document is not a new substantive rule by itself; it is an exchange communication addressed to all Asset Management Companies (AMCs) that points readers to a SEBI circular dated October 28, 2022, identified as SEBI/HO/IMD/DOF2/P/CIR/2022/145, titled “Addendum to SEBI Circular on Development of Passive Funds.” The only affirmative action stated here is that the referenced SEBI circular is available on the NSE website for reference; the letter itself says “This is for your information please” and does not set out any new compliance requirements, operational changes, deadlines, thresholds, or fees in the text provided.

For a compliance team, the practical takeaway is that the addendum is addressed to AMCs and concerns the development of passive funds, so any obligations, procedures, or timelines would come from the underlying SEBI circular rather than from this covering notice. Since no specific requirements are reproduced in the document content, a compliance officer should retrieve and review the full SEBI circular dated October 28, 2022 to determine whether it imposes any changes to passive fund product development, disclosures, approvals, investor communication, or other AMC obligations.

rows.title: Corrigendum on Standard Operating Process under SEBI (PIT) Regulations, 2015 for ensuring compliance with Structured Digital Database (SDD)
rows.summary:
This NSE circular is a corrigendum/reference update to the Exchange’s earlier circular dated October 28, 2022 (NSE/CML/2022/51) on the Standard Operating Process under SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 relating to compliance with the Structured Digital Database (SDD) requirement. It applies to all listed companies on the NSE, including equity and/or debt listed entities.

The key requirement is that companies must comply with Regulations 3(5) and 3(6) of the SEBI (PIT) Regulations, 2015, which require maintenance of a Structured Digital Database by the company. If a company is found not to have complied with those SDD requirements, the Exchange will take enforcement action by displaying on the listed entity’s “Get Quote” page on the Exchange website that the company is non-compliant with SDD.

This disclosure will begin from the next trading day after the non-compliance is identified and will continue until the Exchange has satisfactorily verified that the company has fully complied with the SDD requirements. The circular does not introduce a new numerical threshold, rate, or deadline date beyond this “next trading day” trigger, but it does create an immediate market-facing consequence for non-compliance. Compliance teams should therefore ensure the company’s SDD is maintained in line with Reg. 3(5) and 3(6), because failure to do so can result in public non-compliance status being shown on the Exchange website until rectified and verified.

rows.title: Standard Operating Process under SEBI (PIT) Regulations, 2015 for ensuring compliance with Structured Digital Database (SDD)
rows.summary:
The provided content does not contain readable regulatory text from the document itself; instead, it appears to be a corrupted/binary DOCX file dump (starting with the ZIP header “PK”) with no extractable language about SEBI PIT, the Structured Digital Database (SDD), dates, thresholds, or procedural requirements. rows.title: Seeking of comments / feedback on the XBRL being introduced for submission of Announcements pertaining to Outcome of Board Meeting (Dividend, Buyback, Bonus shares and Voluntary Delisting)
rows.summary:
The document is a market consultation/call for comments from listed entities on the introduction of a new XBRL-based submission format for “Outcome of Board Meeting” announcements. It specifically proposes that announcements relating to board decisions on **dividend, buyback, bonus shares, and voluntary delisting** be filed in XBRL, rather than only in the existing free-text or standard announcement format. The purpose is to standardize disclosures, improve machine-readability, and support more structured regulatory reporting and analysis.

For compliance teams at listed entities, the practical impact is that whenever the company announces the outcome of a board meeting covering any of these actions, the disclosure may need to be prepared in the prescribed XBRL structure and submitted through the exchange’s filing system in that format. This would require internal processes to capture the relevant decision data in a standardized way at the time of the board meeting outcome, and to ensure finance/legal/company secretarial teams can map the announcement content into the XBRL taxonomy correctly before filing. Entities should also expect that specific fields for the action type and the associated terms/quantities will need to be completed consistently, which may create additional validation and governance requirements compared with unstructured announcements.

The document is a **request for comments/feedback**, not the final operative rule itself, so the immediate compliance obligation is to review the proposed XBRL submission approach and provide feedback if requested by the regulator/exchange. Because the provided text is corrupted and does not show the underlying circular’s issuance date, comment deadline, taxonomy details, or implementation date, those specific dates and thresholds cannot be confirmed from the material supplied and should be checked in the original PDF/circular before implementing any process changes.

rows.title: Amendments to guidelines for preferential issue and institutional placement of units by a listed REIT
rows.summary:
This notice is a forwarding communication from the National Stock Exchange of India Limited to all listed companies, pointing them to SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHS_Div3/P/CIR/2022/130 dated September 28, 2022, which amends the guidelines for preferential issue and institutional placement of units by a listed REIT. The document itself does not set out the amended provisions; it simply states that SEBI has issued the circular and encloses it for reference and “necessary action” by recipients.

For compliance purposes, the key point is that this concerns listed REITs and the processes for preferential issue and institutional placement of their units. No effective date other than the circular date of September 28, 2022 is stated in this covering notice, and no thresholds, rates, procedural steps, or filing deadlines are specified in the text provided. A corporate compliance team should therefore treat this as an alert to review the attached SEBI circular directly and determine whether any group entities involved with a listed REIT must update issuance/placement procedures, approvals, disclosures, or internal controls in line with the amended guidelines.

rows.title: XBRL based filing of Shareholding Pattern Report for Listed Companies at NSE
rows.summary:
This NSE circular, dated September 30, 2022 (Ref. No. NSE/CML/2022/49), informs all listed companies that the Shareholding Pattern Report must now be filed in XBRL format on the NSE’s NEAPS portal, in line with SEBI circular SEBI/HO/CFD/PoD-1/P/CIR/2022/92 dated June 30, 2022 on disclosure of specified securities and dematerialized holdings. The practical change is that NSE has made an Excel utility available for generating the XBRL/XML file for the Shareholding Pattern Report, and this utility will be available from October 1, 2022, under NEAPS > Compliance > Periodic Compliances > Share Holding Pattern > SHP Submission > Download SHP XBRL Utility. Companies must use the utility to generate the XML file and then upload it through NEAPS under NEAPS > Compliance > Common XBRL Upload > select “Shareholding Pattern” from the dropdown > click “Upload XBRL File” > browse and select the XML file; successful submission is confirmed by a “File Uploaded successfully” message.

The circular also points companies back to NSE’s June 30, 2022 circular for FAQs on the new shareholder categories and subcategories introduced by the SEBI requirement, but states those FAQs are for guidance only and not a substitute for compliance with the governing regulations. Listed companies are expressly instructed to ensure compliance with the Listing Regulations and any other applicable regulations as amended from time to time. If companies need clarification or encounter difficulty, NSE directs them to write to nsexbrl@nse.co.in or call the toll-free help line 1800 266 0050 (IVR option 4).

rows.title: Amendments to guidelines for preferential issue and institutional placement of units by a listed InvIT
rows.summary:
SEBI has issued Circular No. SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHS_Div3/P/CIR/2022/129 dated September 28, 2022, titled “Amendments to guidelines for preferential issue and institutional placement of units by a listed InvIT.” The document is essentially an intimation letter from the National Stock Exchange of India Limited to all listed companies, forwarding the SEBI circular for reference and “necessary action,” so the operative changes are contained in that SEBI circular rather than in the NSE cover note itself.

For a compliance team, the key point is that the amendments apply to listed Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) and relate specifically to the regulatory framework governing preferential issuance of units and institutional placement of units. The notice does not itself reproduce the amended requirements, thresholds, timelines, or procedural steps, but it makes clear that the SEBI circular should be reviewed and implemented as applicable by the relevant listed entity. There are no additional deadlines or numeric thresholds stated in the covering communication beyond the circular date of September 28, 2022. The practical action item is to obtain and assess the enclosed SEBI circular and confirm whether any current or planned preferential issue or institutional placement of InvIT units must be adjusted to comply with the amended guidelines.

rows.title: Revised Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) on application filed under Regulation 37 of SEBI (Listing Obligation and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 w.r.t. Scheme of Arrangements
rows.summary:
This NSE circular revises the standard operating procedure for listed companies seeking a stock exchange no-objection certificate under Regulation 37 of SEBI LODR for a draft Scheme of Arrangement. The key filing deadline is that the scheme application, together with all documents required under the exchange checklist, must be submitted within **15 working days of the board meeting approving the draft scheme**; if the company misses that window, it must obtain **fresh board approval** based on updated materials such as **fresh financials and a fresh valuation report**.

For schemes involving **unlisted companies**, the listed entity must submit the **audited financials for the last 3 years**, and those financials must **not be older than 6 months** at the time of submission. These financials are to be used by the valuer for the **Income Approach** valuation. In addition, when the exchange issues its observation letter, it will require an **undertaking** from the listed entity confirming that the unlisted company’s financials will still be **no more than 6 months old when the scheme papers are filed with NCLT**.

For valuation materials **other than the Income Approach**, the period under consideration must **not be older than 3 months**. The listed entity’s board must also consider the scheme **within 7 working days of the valuation report being issued**, so companies need to align board scheduling and report finalization tightly.

The application submitted under Regulation 37 must be **complete in all respects** and include the documents required under **para I(A)(2) of the SEBI circular dated November 23, 2021, as amended**, as well as the relevant exchange checklist items. If the exchange finds the filing incomplete, needs clarification, or identifies **material inadequacies or non-compliance** with the March 10, 2017 SEBI circular / November 23, 2021 Master Circular framework, it will return the scheme for rectification and give the company **7 working days** to cure the defects.

If the company does not respond or complete the required corrections within the allowed time, the application may have to be **re-filed as a fresh application**, and any fees already paid for processing will be **forfeited** by the exchange/regulator. Any such re-filing must include a **fresh valuation report, fairness opinion, audit committee recommendation, and related updated documents**, and the company must pay **fresh fees** again. The circular applies to **all listed companies** filing scheme-of-arrangement applications with the exchange under Regulation 37, and it is dated **September 28, 2022**.

rows.title: Framework on Social Stock Exchange
rows.summary:
This NSE circular does not itself impose new substantive obligations on listed companies or social enterprises; it is an information-only notice dated September 22, 2022 advising recipients that SEBI has issued a detailed framework for the Social Stock Exchange (SSE) by circular dated September 19, 2022. The underlying regulatory change occurred earlier, when SEBI amended the ICDR Regulations, LODR Regulations, and AIF Regulations by notification dated July 25, 2022 to create a broad legal framework for the SSE.

For compliance purposes, the key point is that the SSE framework now exists as part of India’s securities law regime and may affect “social enterprises” and “listed companies” to the extent they seek to raise funds, list, or otherwise interact with the Social Stock Exchange platform. The NSE circular itself does not specify thresholds, rates, filing dates, or implementation steps; it simply encloses the SEBI circular and directs recipients to the new framework for review. A compliance team should therefore treat this as a trigger to assess whether the organization qualifies as or engages with a social enterprise/SSE participant and to review the separate SEBI circular dated September 19, 2022 for the detailed operational, disclosure, or eligibility requirements.

rows.title: Guidance note on use of digital signature certificate for announcements submitted by listed companies
rows.summary:
This NSE guidance note clarifies the exchange’s requirement that **all listed entities on NSE authenticate corporate announcements/filings using a Digital Signature Certificate (DSC)** when submitting them through NSE’s electronic filing systems, and it is issued as a reference note to explain the earlier circular. The underlying requirement comes from **NSE Circular NSE/CML/2022/39 dated August 2, 2022**, which applies to **all listed entities on NSE** and is tied to **Regulation 10 of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015**, under which filings must be made on the electronic platform specified by the stock exchange. The circular states that announcements filed on **NEAPS** or the **Digital Portal** must be digitally authenticated, and it also notes that the exchange provides listed companies with a **unique user ID and password** for access to these portals.

The guidance note makes clear that, as a general rule, **all corporate announcements must be submitted with DSC**, but it carves out limited exceptions: **(i)** an **outcome of a Board meeting that includes only financial results**, **(ii)** disclosures that include **documents issued by third parties** rather than the listed company itself (examples given include **auditor certificates, NCLT/other court orders, credit rating documents, and a director’s resignation letter copy**), **(iii)** **newspaper advertisements**, and **(iv)** any other disclosures that the stock exchanges may specify from time to time. It also explains what is **not acceptable as a signature** for these purposes: **physical signatures, pasted image signatures, “Sd/-” signatures, and copy-pasted signatures** are all treated as non-admissible.  

The note further clarifies that **scanned documents are not a substitute for compliance unless they are machine-readable and searchable**; merely uploading a scanned PDF after affixing DSC is not enough. If a document is scanned, the typed/handwritten/printed text must be converted into **machine-encoded text using OCR**, and the file must be in a **fully searchable format** before filing. In practical terms, the filing must contain a **detectable DSC** and be **machine readable**; the stock exchange will not treat a scanned, non-searchable disclosure as compliant even if a signature image is present.

Finally, the note warns that any disclosure submitted in violation of these requirements will be treated as a **non-compliance**. The listed entity must **re-submit the announcement immediately** in the proper form, and **appropriate action may follow** if the defect is not corrected without delay. The guidance note itself does not create a separate new deadline date beyond this immediate rectification obligation, but the effective compliance expectation flows from the prior NSE circular dated **August 2, 2022**, with this September 7, 2022 note serving only to provide operational clarity.

rows.title: Amendments to guidelines for preferential issue and institutional placement of units by a listed REIT
rows.summary:
SEBI has issued Circular No. SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHS_Div3/P/CIR/2022/0116 dated August 26, 2022, titled “Amendments to guidelines for preferential issue and institutional placement of units by a listed REIT.” The document is a forwarding notice from the National Stock Exchange of India Limited to company secretaries of all listed companies, enclosing the SEBI circular for information and necessary action. The notice itself does not set out the substantive amendment text, but it indicates that the underlying regulatory changes affect the framework governing preferential issues and institutional placements of units by listed REITs.

For compliance purposes, the key point is that listed REITs and any parties involved in issuing or placing their units should review the enclosed SEBI circular and determine whether any internal issuance/placement processes, approvals, disclosure practices, or transaction documentation need to be updated to align with the amended guidelines. No effective date, deadlines, thresholds, or specific procedural changes are stated in this covering communication beyond the SEBI circular’s date of August 26, 2022. If your organization is a listed REIT, sponsor, manager, trustee, lead manager, or otherwise involved in such offerings, the operative requirements would be contained in the attached SEBI circular rather than in this brief NSE forwarding note.

rows.title: Amendments to guidelines for preferential issue and institutional placement of units by a listed InvIT
rows.summary: This communication is an informational forwarding of SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHS_Div3/P/CIR/2022/0115 dated August 26, 2022, titled “Amendments to guidelines for preferential issue and institutional placement of units by a listed InvIT.” The letter itself does not set out the detailed amendments; it simply notifies listed companies that SEBI has issued the circular and that a copy is enclosed for reference and necessary action. The affected entities are listed InvITs and, by extension, listed companies receiving the circular for compliance awareness. No specific numerical thresholds, rates, procedural steps, or implementation deadline are stated in this forwarding notice, so compliance teams would need to review the attached SEBI circular directly to identify the actual substantive changes and any obligations arising from them.

rows.title: Addendum to SEBI Circular on Development of Passive Funds
rows.summary:
This document is not itself a substantive regulatory change; it is a forwarding notice addressed to all Asset Management Companies (AMCs) pointing them back to SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/IMD/DF2/CIR/P/2022/102 dated July 28, 2022, titled “Addendum to SEBI Circular on Development of Passive Funds.” The notice states that a copy of the SEBI circular is available on the NSE website for reference, and it is issued “for your information,” without setting out any new obligations, implementation steps, deadlines, rates, thresholds, or procedures in the text provided. 

For compliance purposes, the key point is simply that AMCs should review the referenced SEBI circular itself, because this addendum notice does not describe the rule changes directly and does not impose any separate compliance action beyond awareness of the underlying SEBI circular. The document is signed by the National Stock Exchange of India Limited through Senior Manager Yogesh Deshmukh.

rows.title: Trading Window closure period under Clause 4 of Schedule B read with Regulation 9 of SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 (“PIT Regulations”) – Framework for restricting trading by Designated Persons (“DPs”) by freezing PAN at security level
rows.summary:
This NSE circular is a forwarding notice dated August 5, 2022, addressed to all listed companies and their Company Secretaries, informing them of a SEBI circular issued the same day on insider trading controls under Clause 4 of Schedule B read with Regulation 9 of the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015. The substantive subject of the referenced SEBI circular is a new framework for restricting trading by Designated Persons (“DPs”) by freezing PAN at the security level during trading window closure periods. In practical terms, compliance teams should note that the underlying regulatory action is directed at preventing DPs from trading in specified securities when the trading window is closed, by implementing PAN-based freezes in the trading system rather than relying only on policy-level prohibitions.

The NSE letter itself does not set out the detailed mechanics, thresholds, or implementation steps; it simply encloses the SEBI circular for “necessary action” and notes that the circular is also available on NSE’s website. The only explicit date in this letter is August 5, 2022, which is both the NSE circular date and the date of the SEBI circular being circulated. For compliance purposes, the affected entities are all listed companies, and the affected persons are their Designated Persons under the PIT Regulations, with the restriction applying at the security level through PAN freezing during the trading window closure period.

rows.title: Circular on use of digital signature certificate for announcements submitted by listed companies
rows.summary:
This NSE circular requires all listed companies to use a **digital signature certificate (DSC)** when submitting **announcements to the Stock Exchange** through the Exchange’s electronic filing systems, specifically **NEAPS** and the **Digital Portal**. The change is based on **Regulation 10 of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015**, which already requires listed companies to file reports, statements, documents, filings, and other information electronically, and it builds on SEBI’s earlier COVID-era circulars that permitted digital signature authentication for filings submitted to stock exchanges.

The key compliance change is that, going forward, **filings/announcements must be authenticated using a DSC as a mandatory requirement**, rather than merely being permitted or optional. This applies to announcements made under the various **SEBI regulations** through the Stock Exchange filing route. The circular specifically notes that listed companies already receive a **unique user ID and password** for accessing the electronic portals, but now the submission itself must also be digitally signed.

There are limited exceptions where the DSC requirement does **not** apply: **(1)** the **outcome of a Board meeting that includes only financial results**, **(2)** disclosures that include **documents issued by parties other than the listed company**—for example, an **auditor’s certificate, NCLT or other court order, credit rating documents, etc.**, **(3)** **newspaper advertisements**, and **(4)** any other disclosures that the Stock Exchanges may later specify as excluded. Compliance teams should therefore verify whether each announcement falls within one of these carve-outs before filing.

The circular is **effective from September 01, 2022**. From that date onward, listed companies should ensure their internal filing workflow, authorized signatories, and DSC availability are in place so that all non-exempt exchange announcements are submitted with digital signature certification and do not miss regulatory filing deadlines.

rows.title: Guidance note on disclosures pertaining to analysts / institutional investors meet and best practices
rows.summary:
This NSE circular dated July 29, 2022 (Ref. No. NSE/CML/2022/38) is addressed to the Company Secretary of all listed companies and serves as a guidance note on disclosures for analysts’ meetings, institutional investor meetings, conference calls, and related interactions under SEBI LODR Regulations, 2015, specifically the disclosure requirement in point 15 of Para A of Part A of Schedule III. It does not create a new mandatory regime on its own, but it reiterates the existing legal requirements and, importantly, sets out recommended best practices that listed entities may use to benchmark their reporting processes. It also follows and supplements NSE’s earlier guidance note issued on June 29, 2021 (NSE/CML/2021/24).

Before a meet/call, listed companies must submit the schedule of analysts’ or institutional investors’ meetings to the Exchange within the timelines required under the LODR Regulations, regardless of whether the interaction is an earnings call or another type of call. The circular notes that as a best practice, many leading listed companies also host the notice of an earnings/open-ended call or meet on their website and submit it to the Exchange well in advance. For such pre-meeting disclosures, the guidance recommends including the meeting/call details, mode of attendance, registration instructions, disclaimers or notes to ease registration/participation, any specific platform requirements, any inclusions or exclusions of participants/audiences, and any other relevant particulars; it also notes that presentations for earnings/open-ended meets/calls are often uploaded to the Exchange and company website in advance. A key regulatory change is highlighted here: SEBI’s amendment dated May 5, 2021 made disclosure of the schedule of group meetings/conference calls conducted physically or through digital means mandatory, while disclosure of one-to-one meetings became voluntary.

During the meet/call, companies must ensure adequate and timely disclosure practices and must not share Unpublished Price Sensitive Information (UPSI) in any analyst/institutional investor interaction, whether the event is organized by the listed company or merely attended by it, and whether the interaction is one-to-one or in a group, physical or virtual. The circular emphasizes that the concern is market fairness and avoidance of information asymmetry between select investors and minority shareholders. If UPSI is nevertheless shared in any such interaction, the company must disclose audio recordings or transcripts of all such information in accordance with the timelines prescribed under the applicable regulations. The note also references the EU/UK Market Abuse Regulation (MAR) as an international benchmark, explaining that selective disclosure of material non-public information at investor meetings is prohibited there as well and would require an immediate announcement if it occurs, even though the act itself would still be a breach.

The document further points to an observed best practice among top listed companies: adding a disclaimer or confirmation in the disclosure that the company will rely on publicly available documents for discussion, which helps reduce the risk of selective disclosure. Overall, the circular instructs listed entities to continue complying with all applicable listing and insider-trading regulations as amended from time to time, and clarifies that the guidance note is meant only for reference and benchmarking of reporting procedures, not as a standalone substitute for the underlying legal obligations.

rows.title: Levy of Goods and Services Tax (GST) on the fees payable to SEBI
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India issued a circular on July 20, 2022 to all listed companies, forwarding SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/GSD/TAD/CIR/P/2022/0097 dated July 18, 2022 on the “Levy of Goods & Services Tax (GST) on the fees payable to SEBI.” The NSE notice itself does not create new requirements, but it alerts listed companies that SEBI has issued updated guidance on GST applicability to fees payable to SEBI and that the attached SEBI circular should be reviewed for necessary action.

For compliance purposes, the material point is that SEBI has formally addressed GST on its fees as of July 18, 2022, and listed companies are expected to align any SEBI fee payments and related accounting/tax treatment with that circular. No specific rates, thresholds, or deadlines are stated in the NSE covering communication, and it does not identify a subset of listed entities or activities beyond generally applying to all listed companies that may be subject to SEBI fees.

rows.title: Extension of time for filing of information required under Regulation 46 and 62 of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 in NEAPS (NSE Electronic Application Processing System).
rows.summary:
This NSE circular extends the deadline for all listed entities to file the information required under Regulations 46 and 62 of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015 through NEAPS (NSE Electronic Application Processing System). It follows NSE circular NSE/CML/2022/35 dated July 11, 2022, which had announced the launch of a new NEAPS module for such filings.

The key compliance change is that, instead of filing immediately under the new module, listed entities were given additional time until **August 31, 2022** to complete the required submissions. The circular says the extension was granted after receiving representations from listed entities and considering the practical difficulties they reported in transitioning to the new filing process.

This notice applies to **all listed entities** whose disclosures/filings fall under **Regulation 46 and Regulation 62** of the LODR Regulations. No substantive change is made to the underlying information required by those regulations; the change is only the filing deadline and the use of the new NEAPS electronic filing process. Compliance teams should ensure the required information is uploaded in NEAPS by the extended deadline and should direct any clarification requests to the NSE contacts named in the circular: **Mr. Aniket Raut** and **Ms. Dhwani Shah**.

rows.title: Release of new module for filing of information required under Regulation 46 and 62 of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 on NEAPS (NSE Electronic Application Processing System)
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India issued a listing circular on July 11, 2022 (Ref. No. NSE/CML/2022/35) informing all listed entities that it has launched a new NEAPS module for compliance with SEBI LODR Regulations, specifically Regulations 46 and 62, which require listed companies to maintain a functional website with prescribed basic company information. Under the new process, every listed entity must submit the URLs for the information required under these regulations through NEAPS: the initial disclosure is to be filed at **NEAPS > Periodic Compliance > Regulation for Functional Website**, and any later updates or changes must be made at **NEAPS > Reports > Regulation for Functional Website**.  

The circular does not change the underlying SEBI website-disclosure obligation itself, but it creates a mandatory exchange filing mechanism to support enforcement of that obligation. All listed entities are instructed to complete the filing of the required Regulation 46 and 62 information by **July 18, 2022**. If clarification is needed, the circular provides contact points at the NSE: **Mr. Aniket Raut (araut@nse.co.in)** and **Ms. Dhwani Shah (cdfr_dshah@nse.co.in)**.

rows.title: Release of New Digital Portal for filing of Information with the Exchange - for Financial results, Related Party Transactions (RPT) and Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR) under SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulation, 2015
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) issued Circular NSE/CML/2022/34 on July 8, 2022, to all listed companies announcing the next phase of its new Digital Portal for Exchange filings. This circular amends the filing process by requiring that, **effective July 11, 2022**, three specific disclosures be filed on the new portal rather than the existing NEAPS system: **Financial Results XBRL submissions** (via Digital Exchange > Compliance > Financial Results > Full Results), **Related Party Transactions XBRL submissions** (via Digital Exchange > Compliance > Financial Results > Related Party Transactions), and **Business Responsibility & Sustainability Report (BRSR) XBRL submissions** (via Digital Exchange > Compliance > Business Responsibility & Sustainability Report (BRSR)). The requirement applies to **all NSE-listed entities**.

The circular makes clear that this is a **phase 2 rollout** and is in continuation of earlier NSE circulars dated **January 6, 2022 (NSE/CML/2022/03)** and **July 8, 2022 (NSE/CML/2022/18)**, which had already introduced the Digital Portal for other filings, including equity-announcement disclosures under SEBI’s takeover regulations. For compliance purposes, companies should note that **only the above three filing types move to the new portal in this phase**; **all other filings will continue to be made through the existing NEAPS portal** for the time being. NSE also stated that it will separately share details of a **demo/training session** explaining how to make these filings through the Digital Portal.

To support the transition, NSE has set up a dedicated help desk for portal-related issues and questions, reachable at **toll-free 1800 266 0050 (IVR option 4)** or by email at **compliancecustomersupport@nse.co.in**.

rows.title: Guidance Note on Regulation 13(3) of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulation, 2015 - Investor Complaints Report
rows.summary:
This NSE guidance note reiterates the existing requirement under Regulation 13(3) of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015: every listed entity must file a quarterly investor complaints statement with the recognized stock exchange(s) within 21 days from the end of each quarter. The statement must report the number of investor complaints pending at the start of the quarter, received during the quarter, disposed of during the quarter, and remaining unresolved at quarter-end.

The key clarification is that, when preparing the quarterly report, the listed company must count **all investor complaints received from every source**, not just complaints coming through the stock exchange or SEBI SCORES. The circular specifically notes complaints may arrive through SEBI SCORES, the exchange, hard copies, emails to grievance-handling officials, letters, and similar channels, and all of these must be included in the totals reported.

NSE issued this note because it observed mismatches between companies’ reported complaint numbers and the complaints actually forwarded through the exchange and SEBI SCORES. The circular gives an example where a company received 5 complaints via SCORES, 5 via the exchange, and 5 directly by email/letter; if all 15 were resolved or pending as described, the quarterly disclosure must reflect the full 15 received, 10 disposed of, and 5 pending, even if the company’s prior submission did not do so. Companies are warned that if discrepancies are found, action may be initiated against the company.

For compliance purposes, listed companies should reconcile internal grievance logs with complaints received through all external channels before filing the quarterly investor complaints report, and ensure the disclosure is consistent with both the listing regulations and any other applicable regulations, as amended from time to time.
