rows.title: Advisory under Regulation 46 and 62 of SEBI (Listing Obligation and Disclosure Requirements) Regulation, 2015
rows.summary:
This NSE listing circular, dated **July 4, 2022** (Ref. No. **NSE/CML/2022/32**), is an **advisory to all listed entities** under **SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015**, specifically referencing **Regulation 46** and **Regulation 62**. It reiterates that listed entities must maintain a **functional company website** with basic company information and directs them to place the required disclosures from **Regulation 46(2)** for all listed entities and **Regulation 62(1)** for equity and debt listed entities in a **separate, clearly labeled website section**. The NSE noted that although many entities are already making the required disclosures, they are often **difficult to find because they are not centralized or properly indexed**, which is the main compliance concern being addressed.

The circular requires listed entities to organize the disclosures exactly under the following website paths: **Home > Investors > Disclosures under Regulation 46 of the LODR** for the Regulation 46(2) disclosures, and **Home > Investors > Disclosures under Regulation 62 of the LODR** for the Regulation 62(1) disclosures. In addition, entities must ensure that any policy uploaded on the website shows its **effective date or last amended date**; the NSE specifically observed that this is often missing and expects it to be added. No new monetary thresholds, filing deadlines, or rate changes are introduced in this circular, but it does create an operational compliance expectation that the website disclosures be **centralized, properly indexed, and date-stamped** so they can be easily located and verified.

For compliance purposes, the practical effect is that listed entities should review their investor-relations or compliance webpages to confirm that all required LODR disclosures are consolidated under the specified sections and that policy documents clearly display the most recent amendment/effective date. The circular concludes by advising all listed entities to take the necessary steps to comply with these website-disclosure requirements.

rows.title: FAQ's - Disclosure of holding of specified securities and Holding of specified securities in dematerialized form
rows.summary:
The NSE’s June 30, 2022 circular (NSE/CML/2022/31) forwards SEBI Circular SEBI/HO/CFD/PoD-1/P/CIR/2022/92 dated June 30, 2022 on disclosure of holding of specified securities and holding of specified securities in dematerialized form, and attaches FAQs to guide listed companies on the revised shareholder classification and reporting requirements. The circular is addressed to the Company Secretary of all listed companies and makes clear that companies must comply with the listing regulations and any other applicable regulations as amended from time to time; the FAQs are guidance only, not a substitute for the underlying regulatory requirements.

For shareholding pattern disclosures, the document clarifies that a shareholder already reported in Table II as part of the Promoter/Promoter Group must not be repeated in Table III as a public shareholder, even if that shareholder also fits a public-category label; promoter and promoter group holdings are excluded from Table III entirely. If a shareholder fits more than one public-shareholder category in Table III, the entity must be classified only once, in the category that appears first in the prescribed order of the format, so holdings are not duplicated across categories. Where a category itself contains multiple sub-categories, column XV of Table III requires the number of shares to be reported separately for each sub-category.

The FAQ also defines several new shareholder categories for reporting purposes. “Asset Reconstruction companies” means an Asset Reconstruction Company under section 2(1)(ba) of the SARFAESI Act, 2002. “Sovereign Wealth Funds” includes state-owned investment funds such as domestic NIIF and foreign funds such as GIC Private Limited, Singapore. “Foreign Direct Investment” is to be understood as FDI under rule 2(r) of the Foreign Exchange Management (Non-debt Instruments) Rules, 2019. “Foreign Portfolio Investors Category I” and “Category II” refer to FPIs registered under regulation 5 of the SEBI (Foreign Portfolio Investors) Regulations, 2019 in the corresponding FPI category.

The document further specifies how to classify government-related and government-owned holdings: shares held by the Central Government or the President of India go under “Central Government / President of India,” shares held by a State Government or Governor go under “State Government / Governor,” and shares held by companies or body corporates where the Central or State Government is a promoter must be reported in the corresponding category indicated in the format. Overall, the practical compliance impact is that listed companies must update their shareholding-pattern reporting logic to align with the new shareholder categories/sub-categories, avoid duplicate reporting across Tables II and III, and ensure any dematerialized/specifed-securities disclosures reflect these revised classifications from the date of the circular onward.

rows.title: Disclosure of holding of specified securities and Holding of specified securities in dematerialized form
rows.summary: This NSE circular does not itself introduce a new substantive rule; it forwards and draws attention to SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/PoD-1/P/CIR/2022/92 dated June 30, 2022, entitled “Disclosure of holding of specified securities and Holding of specified securities in dematerialized form.” It is addressed to the Company Secretary of all listed companies and states that the SEBI circular is enclosed and available on the NSE website for reference and necessary action, indicating that listed entities must review and implement whatever disclosure and dematerialization-related requirements are contained in the underlying SEBI circular. The only date given in this notice is June 30, 2022, which is the issuance date of both the SEBI circular and this NSE forwarding circular. No thresholds, percentages, filing deadlines, or procedural details are set out in the NSE text itself; compliance personnel would need to consult the attached SEBI circular to determine the specific disclosure obligations, affected securities/holdings, and any required reporting format or timing.

rows.title: Reduction of timelines for listing of units of privately placed Infrastructure Investment Trust (InvIT)
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India circulated SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHS_Div3/P/CIR/2022/087 dated June 24, 2022, titled “Reduction of timelines for listing of units of privately placed Infrastructure Investment Trust (InvIT).” The NSE letter itself is primarily an intimation to all listed companies and does not set out additional operational details; it states that the SEBI circular is enclosed “for your reference and for necessary action” and is “for your information.”  

For compliance purposes, the material point is that SEBI has changed the timeline for listing units of privately placed InvITs, meaning entities involved in the private placement and listing process for InvIT units must follow the reduced listing period introduced by the June 24, 2022 SEBI circular. The NSE communication does not reproduce the exact revised deadline or procedural steps in the text provided, so the specific new timeline, effective date mechanics, and any filing/listing requirements would need to be confirmed from the enclosed SEBI circular itself.

rows.title: Filing of Report to SEBI in respect of any acquisition made in reliance upon exemption provided for in regulation 10 of SEBI (SAST) Regulations, 2011
rows.summary:
This circular instructs that any report filed with SEBI under Regulation 10(7) of the SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011, for an acquisition made in reliance on an exemption under Regulation 10, must now be submitted to SEBI **only by email** to the dedicated address **sastexemptionapplication@sebi.gov.in**. The email submission must include the **details of the fees paid**.  

The notice is addressed to **all listed companies** and also expressly references **acquirers and listed entities**, so compliance teams should ensure that any exempt acquisition reporting process uses this prescribed email route and includes fee-payment details. The circular does not state a new substantive exemption rule or change any threshold, rate, or deadline; rather, it changes/clarifies the **filing method** for these Regulation 10(7) reports. Listed companies are requested to **take note and comply accordingly** effective from the circular date, **June 22, 2022**.

rows.title: Guidance note for filing intimations w.r.t. Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC) / Inter-Creditors Agreement (ICA)
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) circular dated June 7, 2022 requires all listed entities and resolution professionals to use the Exchange’s **new digital portal** for insolvency- and restructuring-related disclosures, and to file them under the **specific designated subject/category paths** rather than through other routes. For **Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP)** disclosures, the circular specifies separate submission paths for: **(i) commencement/admission of CIRP**, **(ii) approval of a resolution plan by the Hon’ble NCLT**, and **(iii) withdrawal/revocation/rejection of CIRP**; it also says that **all other CIRP intimations required under Schedule III, Part A of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015 must likewise be filed under the “Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process” category** on the digital portal. The portal paths are explicitly given as: for commencement, **Compliance > Equity > New Announcement > Category: Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process > Subject Type: CIRP – Commencement**; for approval of resolution plan, **… Subject Type: CIRP – Approval of Resolution Plan**; and for withdrawal, **… Subject Type: CIRP – Revocation / Rejection**.

The circular also creates a filing expectation for **resolution plans/restructuring of loans or borrowings from banks/financial institutions**, including situations where lenders sign an **Inter-Creditor Agreement (ICA)**. In those cases, listed entities must **promptly intimate the Exchange** with the broad details required under **Para A of Schedule III of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015**, and the filing must be made through **Compliance > Equity > New Announcement > Category: Miscellaneous Disclosure (Event/Periodic) > Subject Type: General Updates**, with the description **“Inter-Creditor Agreements.”** The June 7, 2022 circular is expressly issued in continuation of earlier NSE circulars on this topic, and the Exchange asks listed entities to take note and ensure compliance.

The earlier NSE circular referenced and reproduced in the document, **NSE/CML/2019/20 dated September 24, 2019**, explains the policy background for **disclosure of default / ICA**. It cites the RBI’s **June 7, 2019** stressed-assets framework, under which lenders must conduct a **prima facie review of a defaulting borrower within 30 days of default** (the “Review Period”) and decide on a resolution strategy, which may include either implementing a resolution plan or initiating proceedings under the **Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC)**. Where a resolution plan is to be implemented, **all lenders must enter into an ICA during the Review Period** to set the ground rules for finalizing and implementing the resolution plan for borrowers that have credit facilities from more than one lender.

For compliance purposes, the practical obligation is that affected listed entities, IRPs/RPs, and other relevant filers must ensure the right event is mapped to the **correct NSE portal category and subject type**, because the Exchange is directing filings away from general routes and into the specific insolvency/restructuring submission screens. The document does not create a new substantive insolvency law standard, but it does tighten the **filing process**, requiring prompt and correctly categorized disclosure of CIRP milestones and ICA-related restructuring events on the Exchange’s digital portal.

rows.title: Extension of facility for conducting annual meeting and other meetings of unitholders of REITs and InvITs through Video Conferencing (VC) or through Other Audio-Visual means (OAVM)
rows.summary:
This NSE circular does not itself create new substantive requirements; it informs all listed InvITs, listed REITs, and parties to REITs/InvITs that SEBI has issued Circular No. SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHS_Div2/P/CIR/2022/079 dated June 3, 2022, extending the facility for holding annual meetings and other unitholder meetings through Video Conferencing (VC) or Other Audio-Visual Means (OAVM). The practical effect is that these entities may continue to conduct unitholder meetings electronically under the extended SEBI framework, rather than being limited to physical meetings, for the period specified in the underlying SEBI circular.

The NSE notice is dated June 7, 2022 and is addressed to company secretaries, all listed Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs), all listed Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs), and other parties to REITs and InvITs. It states that the SEBI circular is enclosed for reference and necessary action, and that the circular is also available on the NSE website. Because the NSE communication is only a forwarding/notification circular, any compliance obligation, procedure, or deadline would come from the SEBI circular it references, not from this NSE note itself.

rows.title: Circular on Development of Passive Funds
rows.summary:
This document is an informational forwarding circular from the National Stock Exchange of India Limited to **all Asset Management Companies (AMCs)** regarding **SEBI Notification No. SEBI/HO/IMD/DOF2/P/CIR/2022/69 dated May 23, 2022**, titled **“Circular on Development of Passive Funds.”** The text does **not itself introduce new requirements, obligations, thresholds, procedures, or deadlines**; it simply advises AMCs that SEBI has issued the referenced circular and notes that a copy is available on the NSE website for reference.

For compliance purposes, the key takeaway is that the underlying SEBI circular on passive funds is the relevant document to review for any substantive changes or compliance actions. This NSE communication contains no implementation date beyond the SEBI circular date of **May 23, 2022**, and it does not specify any affected products, operational steps, reporting requirements, or quantitative limits in its own text.

rows.title: Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) for dispute resolution under the Stock Exchange arbitration mechanism for disputes between a Listed Company and/or Registrars to an Issue and Share Transfer Agents (RTAs) and its Shareholder(s)/Investor(s)
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) issued this circular on May 31, 2022 to all listed companies, forwarding SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/MIRSD/MIRSD_RTAMB/P/CIR/2022/76 dated May 30, 2022. The subject is the “Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) for dispute resolution under the Stock Exchange arbitration mechanism” for disputes between a listed company and/or its registrar and share transfer agents (RTAs) and its shareholders/investors.

For compliance purposes, the only action explicitly required by the NSE notice itself is that listed companies review the enclosed SEBI circular and take “necessary action” at their end; the NSE does not restate the SOP content in this notice, but directs recipients to the SEBI circular for the operative requirements. The circular applies to disputes involving listed companies and/or RTAs on one side and shareholders/investors on the other, specifically in the context of stock exchange arbitration as the dispute-resolution mechanism. No separate deadline, threshold, rate, or transition date is set out in the NSE notice itself; the effective regulatory reference is the SEBI circular dated May 30, 2022, which is the source document for the detailed SOP.

The notice also states that the SEBI circular is enclosed for reference and is available on the NSE website (www.nseindia.com). From a compliance team perspective, this means the company secretary and relevant investor grievance/secretarial teams should obtain and implement the SEBI SOP directly, since this NSE communication is only a forwarding advisory and not a substantive restatement of the arbitration procedures.

rows.title: Simplification of procedure and standardization of formats of documents for issuance of duplicate securities certificates
rows.summary:
The notice is a forwarding circular from the National Stock Exchange of India Ltd. to the Company Secretaries of all listed companies, dated May 25, 2022, advising them of SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/MIRSD/MIRSD_RTAMB/P/CIR/2022/70 of the same date. The NSE circular itself does not set out the detailed rule changes, but it clearly states that SEBI has issued a new framework titled **“Simplification of procedure and standardization of formats of documents for issuance of duplicate securities certificates”** and that the enclosed SEBI circular requires **necessary action** by listed companies.  

For compliance purposes, the key point from this document is that listed companies are being directed to align their processes for **issuance of duplicate securities certificates** with the SEBI-prescribed simplified procedure and standardized document formats. No separate effective date, transitional deadline, numerical threshold, or fee/rate is stated in the NSE forwarding letter itself; the operative requirements would be in the referenced SEBI circular attached to the notice. The NSE also notes that the circular is available on its website, and the communication is informational in form but action-oriented in substance because it instructs recipients to review the SEBI circular and implement whatever procedural changes it requires for duplicate certificate issuance.

rows.title: Streamlining the Process of Rights Issue
rows.summary: This circular is an informational listing notice from the National Stock Exchange of India Limited, dated May 20, 2022, addressed to all listed companies and forwarding SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/SSEP/CIR/P/2022/66 dated May 19, 2022 on “Streamlining the Process of Rights Issue.” The NSE notice itself does not create separate substantive requirements; instead, it alerts listed issuers that SEBI has issued updated rights-issue procedural instructions and that the enclosed SEBI circular should be reviewed for necessary action. From a compliance perspective, this means any listed company planning or executing a rights issue should check the SEBI circular’s revised framework and ensure its offer/issuance process is aligned with the streamlined procedure effective from the SEBI circular date, May 19, 2022. The notice does not specify any thresholds, ratios, deadlines, filing periods, or numerical compliance requirements on its face, so the operative obligations would be found in the attached SEBI circular rather than in this NSE covering letter.

rows.title: Simplification of procedure and standardization of formats of documents for transmission of securities
rows.summary: This NSE circular is a transmission notice to all listed companies, informing them of SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/MIRSD/MIRSD_RTAMB/P/CIR/2022/65 dated May 18, 2022, which introduces a simplified procedure and standardized document formats for the transmission of securities. The NSE circular itself does not set out the detailed operational changes; instead, it forwards SEBI’s circular and indicates that listed companies must review it and take necessary action, as the underlying requirements arise from amendments to the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015. The affected entities are all listed companies and, by implication, their company secretaries and investor servicing/registrar processes that handle transmission requests (for example, transfers arising on death or other transmission events, rather than ordinary market transfers). The effective date is the SEBI circular’s issue date, May 18, 2022, with the NSE circular issued the next day, May 19, 2022; no separate implementation deadline, numerical threshold, or fee/rate is stated in the NSE text provided. Compliance teams should therefore obtain and implement the SEBI circular’s standardized forms and process changes in their securities transmission procedures, and ensure internal and RTA-related workflows align with the revised requirements.

rows.title: Relaxation from compliance with certain provisions of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015
rows.summary: This NSE circular is a forwarding notice to all listed companies, informing them that SEBI issued Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/CMD2/CIR/P/2022/62 on May 13, 2022, titled “Relaxation from compliance with certain provisions of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015.” The NSE letter itself does not set out the substantive relaxations, deadlines, or modified requirements; instead, it directs companies to the SEBI circular for the actual compliance relief and any related action items. In other words, the operative regulatory change is the SEBI-issued relaxation referenced in the attached circular, and listed entities should review that SEBI document to determine which LODR provisions have been relaxed and whether any filing, disclosure, or timing relief applies to them. The NSE notice is dated May 16, 2022 and is addressed to the Company Secretary of all listed companies. It also notes that the SEBI circular is enclosed and available on the NSE website for reference and necessary action.

rows.title: Reduction of timelines for listing of units of Infrastructure Investment Trust (InvIT)
rows.summary: This notice is a transmittal from the National Stock Exchange of India Limited to all listed companies, informing them of SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHS_Div3/P/CIR/2022/55 dated April 28, 2022, which revises the timeline for listing units of Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs). The document itself does not spell out the detailed procedural change; it simply states that SEBI has issued a circular titled “Reduction of timelines for listing of units of Infrastructure Investment Trust (InvIT)” and sends a copy “for your information” and “necessary action.” For compliance purposes, the key point is that entities involved in InvIT issuances/listings, and any listed company that may be sponsoring, managing, or otherwise participating in such transactions, should review the April 28, 2022 SEBI circular because the listing timetable has been shortened and the updated timing requirements are now mandatory. No specific deadline dates, day-counts, thresholds, or monetary amounts are included in this notice itself, so any exact compliance obligations must be taken from the referenced SEBI circular.

rows.title: Reduction of timelines for listing of units of Real Estate Investment Trust (REIT)
rows.summary:
This communication is a forwarding notice from the National Stock Exchange of India Limited to all listed companies, pointing them to SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHS_Div3/P/CIR/2022/54 dated April 28, 2022, titled “Reduction of timelines for listing of units of Real Estate Investment Trust (REIT).” The only substantive change identified in the text is that SEBI has reduced the timeline for listing REIT units; however, the NSE notice itself does not reproduce the revised timing details, so the specific shortened period must be taken from the attached SEBI circular.

For compliance purposes, the affected entities are issuers/listed companies involved in REIT-related transactions and the associated listing process for REIT units. The notice says the SEBI circular is enclosed “for your reference and for necessary action,” which indicates recipients should review the SEBI circular and update any internal issuance/listing procedures, timelines, and transaction documentation to reflect the reduced REIT unit listing timeline. No monetary thresholds, rates, or other numerical compliance limits are stated in this covering letter beyond the date of the SEBI circular itself (April 28, 2022). The letter is informational in tone and does not impose any additional requirements beyond directing attention to the SEBI circular.

rows.title: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) – Disclosure of Related Party Transactions under regulation 23 of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015
rows.summary:
This NSE circular dated April 25, 2022 is not itself a new substantive rule, but an explanatory FAQ note to SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/CMD1/CIR/P/2021/662 dated November 22, 2021 on disclosure of related party transactions (RPTs) under Regulation 23 of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015. NSE tells all listed companies to comply with the listing regulations and any other applicable regulations as amended from time to time, and notes that the FAQs are guidance only; the operative requirements are those in SEBI’s circular and annexed disclosure format.

For reporting format and period, listed entities must use SEBI’s new RPT disclosure format starting with the half-year reporting period from 1 October 2021 to 31 March 2022. The disclosure is required on a six-month-end basis for both the first and second half-year, rather than on a year-to-date basis for the second half. The FAQ also clarifies that if a transaction is undertaken within the consolidated entity, such as between the listed entity and its subsidiary or between subsidiaries, it should be reported only once and not duplicated from each entity’s perspective; for example, a sale by the holding company to its subsidiary may be disclosed either as a sale by the holding company or as a purchase by the subsidiary, but not both.

The circular makes clear that the new format is intended to capture related party transactions of the listed entity and its subsidiaries, so the old standalone-versus-consolidated distinction is effectively removed for disclosure purposes. Companies must also disclose opening and closing balances, including commitments, for existing related party transactions even if no new transaction occurred during the reporting period. Banks are explicitly included and must file RPT disclosures in the new format as well.

On effective dates, the FAQ distinguishes between the reporting format and the substantive rule changes: provisions that SEBI stated would be effective from 1 April 2022 apply only to transactions entered into on or after that date, not to transactions in the half-year ended 31 March 2022. For brand usage or royalty transactions, the applicable materiality test is the specific threshold in Regulation 23(1A); even if the separate threshold substituted in the proviso to Regulation 23(1) effective 1 April 2022 is crossed, the transaction is disclosed only if it exceeds the Regulation 23(1A) threshold. The FAQ also points out a carve-out for acceptance of fixed deposits by banks and NBFCs at terms uniformly applicable/offered to all shareholders/public, which is not treated as a related party transaction but still has to be disclosed every six months to the stock exchange in the prescribed format.

rows.title: XBRL based filing of Investor Grievance for Listed Companies at NSE
rows.summary:
The NSE has mandated that all listed companies file their quarterly Investor Grievance Report under Regulation 13(3) of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015 only in XBRL format through the NSE’s Electronic Application Processing System (NEAPS). This report must continue to be filed within 21 days from the end of each quarter and must disclose the number of investor complaints pending at the start of the quarter, received during the quarter, disposed of during the quarter, and unresolved at quarter-end.

To support this change, NSE is introducing an offline Excel utility that generates the XML/XBRL file in the prescribed format; the utility is attached as Annexure 1. The filing process requires users to go to NEAPS, navigate to Compliance > Common XBRL upload, choose “Investor Grievance” from the Modules dropdown, select the relevant quarter, upload the XML file, and then confirm successful submission via the upload acknowledgment and the email sent to the registered address. If there are any issues, companies are instructed to contact nsexbrl@nse.co.in.

The circular makes clear that NSE will recognize only those Investor Grievance disclosures that are filed through the specified NEAPS path in XBRL mode. Companies that may already have submitted this disclosure in XBRL format previously are told to follow the new process starting from the next quarter. The effective compliance expectation is immediate from the date of the circular, April 11, 2022, for future quarterly filings.

rows.title: FAQ’s - LODR amendments dated August 03, 2021
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India issued this April 8, 2022 circular to all listed companies to circulate updated FAQs on the LODR amendments dated August 3, 2021, following an earlier FAQ circular issued on December 22, 2021. The exchange’s message is that companies must continue complying with the Listing Regulations as amended from time to time, and the FAQs are provided only for guidance rather than as a substitute for the regulations themselves.

The substantive issue addressed is newly inserted Regulation 17(1C), which requires a listed entity to obtain shareholder approval for the appointment of a person to the Board of Directors at the next general meeting or within three months from the date of appointment, whichever comes earlier. The FAQ clarifies that this amended requirement applies only to director appointments made on or after January 1, 2022; directors appointed on or before December 31, 2021 remain subject to the earlier, pre-amendment provisions.

The FAQ also confirms that Regulation 17(1C) applies not only to fresh appointments but also to re-appointments of directors. In addition, while the timing for shareholder approval is governed by the new three-month/next general meeting rule for covered appointments, the form of resolution to be passed—ordinary or special—must be determined according to the provisions of the LODR that are otherwise currently in force.

rows.title: Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) for dispute resolution available under the stock exchange arbitration mechanism for disputes between a listed company and its shareholder(s)/investor(s)
rows.summary:
This NSE circular dated April 8, 2022 is a transmittal notice to the Company Secretary of all listed companies, sent through recognized stock exchanges, and it directs companies to note and act on the underlying SEBI circular on “Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) for dispute resolution available under the stock exchange arbitration mechanism for disputes between a listed company and its shareholder(s)/investor(s).” The NSE document itself does not set out the substantive arbitration rules, deadlines, or thresholds; instead, it states that the attached SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/SSEP/CIR/P/2022/48, also dated April 8, 2022, contains the operative requirements and should be followed for necessary action. The notice confirms that the SEBI circular is enclosed with the communication and is also available on the NSE website (www.nseindia.com), indicating that listed companies should review that circular directly to understand the dispute-resolution procedure, affected parties, and any compliance obligations.

For compliance purposes, the key point from this document is that it applies to listed companies and concerns disputes with their shareholders/investors that may be taken up under the stock exchange arbitration mechanism. However, because this NSE letter is only an information and forwarding communication, it does not itself specify implementation steps, procedural timelines, filing formats, or any monetary limits; those details would need to be taken from the referenced SEBI circular.

rows.title: Clarification on applicability of Regulation 23(4) read with Regulation 23(3)(e) of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 in relation to Related Party Transactions
rows.summary:
This circular is a transmission notice from the National Stock Exchange of India Limited dated April 8, 2022, sent to the Company Secretary of all listed companies through the recognized stock exchanges. It does not itself create new substantive requirements; rather, it forwards and calls attention to a SEBI circular of the same date, SEBI/HO/CFD/CMD1/CIR/P/2022/47, titled “Clarification on applicability of Regulation 23(4) read with Regulation 23(3)(e) of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 in relation to Related Party Transactions.”

For compliance purposes, the key point is that SEBI issued a clarification regarding when Regulation 23(4), read together with Regulation 23(3)(e), applies to related party transactions under the LODR Regulations. The NSE notice does not restate the clarification’s detailed substance, thresholds, or procedural changes; it simply states that the SEBI circular is enclosed for reference and “necessary action” and is also available on the NSE website. Accordingly, listed companies should review the referenced SEBI circular directly to determine whether their related party transaction approval, disclosure, or compliance processes need to be updated under the clarified interpretation.

No separate effective date, transition period, numerical threshold, or deadline is stated in the NSE notice itself beyond the circular date of April 8, 2022. The affected entities are all listed companies, and the subject matter is related party transactions governed by Regulation 23 of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015, especially the interaction of sub-regulation 23(4) with 23(3)(e).

rows.title: Processing of waiver applications by the Exchanges in case of commonly listed entities
rows.summary:
The circular changes how waiver requests for SOP fines are handled for **commonly listed entities**—that is, companies listed on **more than one stock exchange**. Effective **April 1, 2022**, when such a company submits a waiver application, the request will be **segregated so that only one exchange processes it**, and the decision taken by that exchange will be **binding on all other exchanges** that levied penalties for the same non-compliance. The exchanges will also charge a **nominal processing fee** for handling the waiver application, and the detailed procedure and fee structure are set out in **Annexure I**.

The circular is issued in the context of SEBI’s SOP framework, under which exchanges are required to monitor listed-entity submissions and may impose actions such as **penalties, shifting securities to the “Z” category, freezing promoter holdings, and suspending trading** for non-compliance. SEBI has also directed that if an exchange deviates from the prescribed SOP actions, it must **record the reasons in writing**. In addition, the exchanges have jointly formulated a **“Policy for Exemption of Fines,”** which was noted by SEBI on **January 22, 2020**, and this policy is the basis on which waiver requests are evaluated.

For compliance purposes, the company should note that a waiver application may be filed **only after the company has achieved compliance** with the relevant listing regulations. NSE also says companies should review the **Policy for Exemption of Fines** and an **illustrative list of scenarios that may lead to rejection of waiver requests**, which is provided in **Annexure II**. The circular states that the process, the rejection scenarios, and the allocation of companies between exchanges for the period **April 1, 2022 to September 30, 2022** are available on NSE’s website.

The mechanism applies **only to companies listed on more than one exchange**. For **exclusively listed companies**—companies listed on only one exchange—the waiver application will be processed by that single exchange, but the processing will still follow the procedure in **Annexure I**. The circular directs all listed companies to take note and ensure compliance, and it became effective on **April 1, 2022**.

rows.title: Clarification on applicability of Regulation 23 of  SEBI  (Listing  Obligations  and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 in relation to Related Party Transactions
rows.summary: This NSE circular is a forwarding notice to all listed companies, informing them of SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/CMD1/CIR/P/2022/40 dated March 30, 2022, which clarifies the applicability of Regulation 23 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 in relation to related party transactions. The NSE letter itself does not impose a new requirement or change the text of Regulation 23; rather, it directs companies to the SEBI clarification for necessary action and indicates that the SEBI circular is enclosed and also available on the NSE website. The affected entities are all listed companies receiving the circular through recognized stock exchanges, and the subject matter is compliance around related party transactions under Regulation 23. The only explicit date in the NSE communication is March 31, 2022, which is the date of the NSE circular, while the referenced SEBI clarification is dated March 30, 2022. No specific thresholds, approval limits, numerical tests, or procedural steps are stated in this NSE notice itself, so a compliance team should treat this as a notification to review the underlying SEBI circular for the operative obligations.

rows.title: Automation of disclosure requirements under SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011 - System Driven Disclosures - Ease of doing business
rows.summary:
This notice is an informational forwarding circular from the National Stock Exchange of India Limited, dated March 7, 2022, addressed to the Company Secretary of all listed companies through recognized stock exchanges. It does not itself introduce new obligations in the NSE letter, but it directs recipients to SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/DCR-3/P/CIR/2022/27, also dated March 7, 2022, for the operative requirements. The subject of the SEBI circular is the automation of disclosure requirements under the SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011, described as “System Driven Disclosures” aimed at ease of doing business.

For compliance purposes, the key point is that disclosure obligations relating to substantial acquisition/takeover-related holdings are being automated through the system, so the relevant disclosures will be generated or facilitated through stock exchange/market infrastructure rather than relying solely on manual company filing processes. The document identifies listed companies as the addressed audience and indicates that the circular has been enclosed for “necessary action,” implying that compliance teams should review the SEBI circular itself and update internal reporting/monitoring processes accordingly. No specific thresholds, deadlines, or rate changes are stated in the NSE covering letter itself, and no implementation date other than March 7, 2022 is provided here.

rows.title: Extension to SEBI Circular on “Relaxation in adherence to prescribed timelines issued by SEBI due to Covid 19” dated April 13, 2020
rows.summary: This NSE circular is a transmittal notice to all listed companies, issued on February 25, 2022, informing them that SEBI had that same day released Circular No. SEBI/HO/MIRSD/MIRSD_RTAMB/P/CIR/2022/26, titled “Extension to SEBI Circular on ‘Relaxation in adherence to prescribed timelines issued by SEBI due to Covid 19’ dated April 13, 2020.” The NSE letter itself does not set out the substance of the SEBI extension or impose any new standalone requirement; it simply forwards the SEBI circular for “necessary action” and points recipients to the attached SEBI document and NSE website for the operative details. From a compliance perspective, the key point is that listed companies should review the enclosed SEBI circular because it extends the earlier Covid-19-related relaxation of prescribed timelines, but this NSE notice does not specify which timelines were extended, the duration of the extension, or any additional filing or procedural obligations beyond acting on the SEBI circular.

rows.title: Approach to securities market data access and terms of usage of data provided by data sources in Indian securities market
rows.summary:
The NSE circular dated February 25, 2022 is a forwarding notice to all REITs and InvITs informing them of a SEBI circular of the same date, titled “Approach to securities market data access and terms of usage of data provided by data sources in Indian securities market.” The NSE does not itself set out new operational requirements in this communication; it states that the SEBI circular is enclosed for reference and “necessary action” and is also available on the NSE website.

For compliance purposes, the key point is that SEBI has issued the underlying framework on market data access and terms of use, and the covered entities here are all Real Estate Investment Trusts and all Infrastructure Investment Trusts. However, this NSE notice does not summarize the substantive rules, deadlines, thresholds, or specific obligations contained in the SEBI circular, so those details would need to be reviewed in the attached SEBI document itself to determine any actual compliance actions, implementation dates, or restrictions on data access/use.

rows.title: Release of New Digital Portal for filing of Information with the Exchange – for Equity Announcements and Disclosures under SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) announced that its new Digital Portal for exchange filings will go live on **February 19, 2022**, replacing paper/legacy handling only for certain items in **Phase 1**. For now, the portal must be used only for **(1) Equity Announcements** and **(2) disclosures under the SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011 (SAST)**; **all other filing types must continue to be submitted through the existing NEAPS portal**.

NSE directed all listed entities to **log in to the new Digital Portal by February 18, 2022** to prevent delays in filing from the go-live date onward. Access is through **https://digitalexchange.nseindia.com**, using the **existing NEAPS login username** and the **default password “Welcome@12345”** (with reference to a “Continuation Sheet” in the notice). NSE also said it had arranged a **demo on Friday, February 18, 2022 at 11:00 a.m.** to show users how to access the portal, and that the invitation link had been emailed to listed entities.

For operational support, NSE set up a **dedicated help desk** for questions and issues related to the new portal, available at **toll-free 1800 266 0050 (IVR Option 4)** and **compliancecustomersupport@nse.co.in**. The circular is addressed to **all listed entities**, so any issuer making NSE filings should ensure relevant compliance and listing teams can access the portal and transition the specified filings on time.

rows.title: Conversion of Private Unlisted InvIT into Private Listed InvIT
rows.summary:
This communication from the National Stock Exchange of India Limited is addressed to all Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) and serves as a forwarding notice for SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHS_Div3/P/CIR/2022/16 dated February 9, 2022, titled “Conversion of Private Unlisted InvIT into Private Listed InvIT.” The document itself does not restate the substantive rules of the SEBI circular, set out any new requirements, or specify any operational deadlines or thresholds; it only indicates that the enclosed SEBI circular should be reviewed and action taken as necessary by recipients.

For compliance purposes, the key point is that the notice confirms a regulatory framework exists for converting a private unlisted InvIT into a private listed InvIT, and it is being circulated to all InvITs for awareness and implementation. However, because the body of this document is purely a covering letter, the actual compliance obligations, eligibility conditions, procedural steps, approvals, disclosures, and effective dates would be found in the attached SEBI circular rather than in this notice itself.

rows.title: Disclosures in the abridged prospectus and front cover page of the offer document
rows.summary:
This notice is a forwarding communication from the National Stock Exchange of India Limited to all issuers proposing to list specified securities. It refers issuers to SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/SSEP/CIR/P/2022/14 dated February 04, 2022, titled “Disclosures in the abridged prospectus and front cover page of the offer document,” and states that a copy of that SEBI circular is enclosed for reference and necessary action.

From the text provided, the NSE notice itself does not introduce any new requirements, thresholds, deadlines, or effective dates beyond directing compliance with the referenced SEBI circular. The compliance obligation for affected issuers is therefore to review the February 04, 2022 SEBI circular and implement whatever disclosure changes it prescribes for the abridged prospectus and the front cover page of the offer document when preparing offer documents for specified securities listings. No additional quantitative limits, procedural steps, or implementation timetable are stated in this notice.

rows.title: Framework for conversion of Private Listed InvIT into Public InvIT
rows.summary:
This communication is a forwarding notice from the National Stock Exchange of India Limited to all Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs), highlighting SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHS_Div3/P/CIR/2022/15 dated February 09, 2022, titled “Framework for conversion of Private Listed InvIT into Public InvIT.” The document itself does not set out the conversion framework’s substantive rules; it simply confirms that SEBI has issued a circular establishing the process and that the circular is enclosed “for your reference and for necessary action at your end.”

For a compliance team, the key point is that this notice is relevant to InvITs, particularly those that are privately listed and may seek to convert into a public InvIT under SEBI’s framework. Because the actual requirements, conditions, forms, timelines, and thresholds are contained in the referenced SEBI circular rather than in this note, the compliance action is to review the enclosed SEBI circular in full and assess whether the trust is eligible for or planning such a conversion. No separate effective date, deadline, numeric threshold, or procedural requirement is stated in this NSE covering communication beyond the instruction to take necessary action as applicable.

rows.title: Schemes of Arrangement by Listed Entities
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India issued this circular on February 1, 2022 to all listed companies, forwarding SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/DIL2/CIR/P/2022/11 of the same date on “Schemes of Arrangement by Listed Entities.” The NSE communication itself does not set out new substantive requirements; it is a transmittal notice advising listed entities that SEBI has issued the referenced circular and that the enclosed SEBI circular should be reviewed and acted on as necessary.

For compliance purposes, the document matters because it applies to listed companies contemplating or implementing schemes of arrangement and indicates that there are SEBI requirements in force as of February 1, 2022 governing those transactions. However, this NSE notice does not state any specific procedural changes, thresholds, filing requirements, effective transition dates, or deadlines of its own; those details would need to be taken from the enclosed SEBI circular it references.

rows.title: Issuance of Securities in dematerialized form in case of Investor Service Requests
rows.summary: The National Stock Exchange of India is notifying all listed companies, through the recognized stock exchanges, of a SEBI circular dated January 25, 2022 titled “Issuance of Securities in dematerialized form in case of Investor Service Requests.” The NSE circular itself does not set out the full operational requirements, but it formally alerts listed companies that SEBI has issued new instructions requiring action on their part and encloses the SEBI circular for implementation. The compliance impact is therefore on **all listed companies** that handle **investor service requests** relating to securities issuance, with the key substantive change being that such issuance must be addressed in **dematerialized form** rather than physical form, as set out by SEBI in the referenced circular. The NSE circular is dated **January 27, 2022** and is intended for immediate information and necessary action; no separate deadline, threshold, fee, or numerical compliance standard is stated in the NSE notice itself.

rows.title: Launch of Digital Portal for filings done with the Exchange
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India Limited (NSE) announced the launch of a new Digital Portal for exchange filings, replacing the current NEAPS (NSE Electronic Application Processing System) workflow in a phased transition. For now, the first phase covers two filing types: announcements submitted to the Exchange and disclosures submitted under the SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011. NSE states that, ultimately, all filings to the Exchange by listed entities will be routed through the Digital Portal, and that further circulars will be issued describing the submission process in more detail as the migration proceeds.

All listed entities are required to migrate to the Digital Portal when they receive an email from the NSE Digital Portal address, noreply@digitalexchange.nse.co.in; the circular says that this email would be sent on or before January 08, 2021. The document also says webinars will be conducted to explain how to access and use the portal. The annexed migration instructions require the Company Super User and Company Sub User to use the activation link in the email sent to the address registered on the NEAPS portal, set up their user ID and password on the new platform, and then log in through the “Exchange” button on the Digital Exchange Platform.

The procedure is operationally specific: after clicking the email link, the user enters the Super/Sub User ID and password as prompted, saves the changes, is redirected to the portal, clicks “Exchange,” re-enters the chosen credentials, and then receives an OTP to the registered mobile number and email address for final authentication. Only after entering the OTP successfully does the user reach the dashboard. NSE also notes that the Super User can create sub-users for the organization in accordance with the user manual available on the portal.

rows.title: Extension of facility for conducting annual meeting and other meetings of unitholders of REITs and InvITs through Video Conferencing (VC) or through Other Audio-Visual means (OAVM)
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India informed all listed InvITs, listed REITs, and all parties to REITs/InvITs that SEBI issued a circular on December 22, 2021 extending the facility to conduct annual meetings and other unitholder meetings through video conferencing (VC) or other audio-visual means (OAVM). This NSE communication, circular NSE/CML/2022/02 dated January 5, 2022, does not itself set out new procedural text; it forwards the SEBI circular for necessary action and reference, and notes that the SEBI circular is available on the NSE website.

For compliance purposes, the key point is that the VC/OAVM option for REIT and InvIT unitholder meetings remains available under the extended arrangement, so affected entities should continue to follow the SEBI-issued requirements governing such virtual meetings. The document does not specify any new numeric thresholds, filing deadlines, or changed voting/notice mechanics in the NSE letter itself, so the operative compliance obligations would come from the referenced SEBI circular dated December 22, 2021 rather than from this NSE cover notice.

rows.title: Schemes of Arrangement by Listed Entities - Clarification w.r.t. timing of submission of NOC from the lending scheduled commercial banks/ financial institutions/ debenture trustee
rows.summary:
This NSE circular, issued on January 3, 2022, is a clarification for all listed companies that file schemes of arrangement and are required to obtain a no-objection letter under Regulation 37(1) of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015. The key change is timing: where the earlier SEBI circulars of November 16, 2021 and November 18, 2021 required a no-objection certificate (NOC) from the lending scheduled commercial banks, financial institutions, or debenture trustee, SEBI has now clarified that this NOC must be submitted to the stock exchange **before** the exchange issues its no-objection letter under Regulation 37(1). In other words, listed entities cannot expect the exchange’s no-objection letter to be issued until the lending bank/financial institution/debenture trustee NOC has already been filed with the exchange.

The circular does not introduce a numeric threshold or rate, but it does impose a procedural compliance requirement on any listed company proposing a scheme of arrangement that falls under Regulation 37. Companies are also reminded to comply with NSE Circular NSE/CML/2021/43 dated November 2, 2021, which sets out the Standard Operating Procedure for applications filed under Regulation 37 of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015. For compliance teams, the practical obligation is to ensure the NOC is obtained and submitted in advance of the exchange’s review completion so that the scheme application is not delayed or rejected for missing documentation. The circular is for immediate information and necessary action; no separate future effective date is stated, so the clarification applies from the date of the SEBI circular referenced as January 3, 2022.

rows.title: FAQ’s - LODR amendments dated August 03, 2021
rows.summary:
This NSE circular dated December 22, 2021 issues FAQs on the SEBI amendments to the LODR Regulations notified on August 3, 2021 and is addressed to all listed companies. The key clarification concerns newly inserted Regulation 17(1C), which requires listed entities to obtain shareholder approval for the appointment of any person to the Board of Directors at the next general meeting or within three months from the date of appointment, whichever is earlier.

The FAQ clarifies the effective-date treatment: the amended Regulation 17(1C) applies only to director appointments made on or after January 1, 2022. Director appointments made on or before December 31, 2021 remain subject to the existing provisions in force before the amendment.

The circular also notes that, for approvals under this provision, the type of shareholder resolution required—ordinary or special—must be determined according to the LODR provisions prevailing at the relevant time. Listed companies are instructed to comply with the LODR and any other applicable regulations as amended from time to time; the FAQs are only for assistance and do not override the regulations themselves.

rows.title: Clarification with respect to Circular dated November 03, 2021, on Common and simplified norms for processing investor’s service request by RTAs and norms for furnishing PAN, KYC details and Nomination
rows.summary: This NSE circular is a forwarding notice to all listed companies, informing them of SEBI Notification No. SEBI/HO/MIRSD/MIRSD_RTAMB/P/CIR/2021/687 dated December 14, 2021, titled “Clarification with respect to Circular dated November 03, 2021, on Common and simplified norms for processing investor’s service request by RTAs and norms for furnishing PAN, KYC details and Nomination.” The NSE advises that the SEBI clarification is enclosed and should be referred to for “necessary action,” but the NSE text itself does not set out any substantive new compliance steps, deadlines, thresholds, or procedural changes beyond this reference. The audience is all listed companies routed through recognized stock exchanges, typically through their Company Secretary/compliance function. rows.title: Master Circular for Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs)
rows.summary:

For a compliance team, the key point is that this applies to all listed REITs and indicates that any obligations, procedures, filing requirements, disclosures, or compliance standards are contained in the SEBI master circular referenced above, rather than in the NSE cover notice. The NSE communication is informational only, but it signals that listed REITs should review the enclosed SEBI circular immediately and align internal compliance processes with whatever updated or consolidated requirements that master circular imposes as of November 29, 2021.

rows.title: Master Circular for Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs)

No. NSE/CML/2021/51**. rows.title: Non-compliance with certain provisions of SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018.
rows.summary:

For compliance purposes, the only clear obligation conveyed in this note is to review the attached SEBI circular and assess whether the listed company has any exposure under the referenced ICDR Regulations provisions. No specific effective date, filing deadline, monetary penalty, or procedural requirement is set out in the NSE covering letter itself, beyond the fact that the cited SEBI circular is dated November 23, 2021. Because the substance of the requirements is contained in the annexed SEBI circular rather than in this note, a compliance team would need to read that circular directly to determine what non-compliance is covered and what action is required.

rows.title: Payment of fees in connection with filings made with SEBI
rows.summary:
This NSE circular informs **all listed companies** that SEBI has issued updated instructions on **payment of fees for filings made with SEBI** under the **SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018**, **SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011**, and **SEBI (Buyback of Securities) Regulations, 2018**. The circular states that fees for these filings are **currently being paid through the payment gateway available on the SEBI Intermediary Portal**.

For filings or specific applications **not supported on the SEBI Intermediary Portal**, listed companies must follow the payment process set out in SEBI’s attached communication (dated **October 13, 2021**). The key compliance point is that **with effect from October 13, 2021**, filings where payment is made through **any mode other than the specified payment method** may be **delayed**. Companies should therefore ensure that fee payments are made only through the prescribed route for supported filings, and for unsupported applications they should use the alternate procedure referenced by SEBI to avoid processing delays.

In practical terms, the circular does **not introduce a new fee amount or threshold**, but it does create an operational compliance obligation: companies must verify whether the relevant filing is supported by the SEBI Intermediary Portal and use the correct payment method accordingly. The NSE is effectively warning that improper payment routing could slow down SEBI’s processing of the underlying filing, which could have knock-on effects for time-sensitive capital market actions such as issue-related filings, takeover-related filings, and buyback-related filings.

rows.title: Master Circular on Scheme of Arrangement
rows.summary: This NSE circular is a forwarding notice to all listed companies, informing them of SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/DIL2/CIR/P/2021/0000000665 dated November 23, 2021, titled “Master Circular on Scheme of Arrangement.” The NSE letter itself does not introduce new requirements, deadlines, thresholds, or procedures; it simply encloses the SEBI master circular and directs recipients to review it and take “necessary action” as applicable.
