rows.title: Order in the matter of Coffee Day Enterprises Limited for FY 2019-20 against M/s Venkatesh & Co. and CA Dasaraty & CA Desikan G.
rows.desc: Order in the matter of Coffee Day Enterprises Ltd (CDEL) for the FY 2019-20 'lTI'ffl � I Government of India ����IN ational Financial Reporting Authority 7th-8th Floor, Hindustan Times House, Kasturba Gandhi Marg, New Delhi File No. 02312024 Date: 10th October, 2024 Order In the matter of Mis Venkatesh & Co., CA Dasaraty V. and CA Desikan G., uls 132 (4) (c) of the Companies Act, 2013. 1. This Order disposes of the Show Cause Notice ('SCN' hereafter) no. NF-23/1412022 dated 17.01.2024 issued to Mis Venkatesh & Co., Chartered Accountants, Firm No: 004636S ('Firm' hereafter), an audit firm registered with the Institute of Chartered Accountants oflndia ('ICAI' hereafter), CA Dasaraty V. ICAI Membership No-026336 ('EP' hereafter) and CA Desikan G. ICAI Membership No-219101 ('EQCR' hereafter), who are members of ICAI and were members of Engagement Team for the statutory audit of Coffee Day Enterprises Limited ('CDEL' hereafter) for the Financial Year ('FY' hereafter) 2019-20. The Firm and the EP are collectively called as the Auditor/s or Principal Auditor/s). 2. This Order is divided into the following sections: A. Executive Summary B. Introduction & Background C. Major lapses in the Audit D. Omission and Com.mission by the Audit Firm E. Finding on the Articles of Charges of Professional Misconduct F. Penalty & Sanctions A. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY 3. NFRA suo moto examined the professional conduct of the statutory auditors of Coffee Day Enterprises Limited under Section 132(4) of the Companies Act 2013 ('the Act' hereafter), pursuant to the Securities and Exchange Board of India ('SEBI' hereafter) shared its investigation report regarding diversion of funds worth Rs 3,535 crores from seven subsidiary companies of Coffee Day Enterprises Limited to Mysore Amalgamated Coffee Estate Limited ('MACEL' hereafter), an entity owned and controlled by the promoters of CDEL. Coffee Day Enterprises Limited is listed on stock exchanges. A Show Cause Notice was issued to to Mis Venkatesh & Co., the auditor for the FY 2019-20; CA Dasaraty V., the EP for the audit engagement and CA Desikan G, the EQCR. 4. Late Shri V. G. Sidhartha (VGS - the then Chairman of CDEL) reportedly committed suicide in July 2019 after leaving a note about financial irregularities in Coffee Day Group. Thereafter, Page 1 of34 Order in the matter of Coffee Day Enterprises Ltd (CDEL) for the FY 2019-20 as per direction of the Board of Directors of CDEL, the matter was investigated by retired Deputy Inspector General of Central Bureau of Investigation (DIG of CBI) and a legal firm. The Auditors had access to the investigation report ofretired DIG of CBI, which had a number of red flags of fraud committed in the company. This investigation report spoke about loans/advances made by the subsidiaries of CDEL to MACEL (a promoter company which was 91 % held by father of VGS) without any commercial sense, evergreening of loans/advances given to MACEL and VGS keeping pre-signed blank cheques of CDEL's subsidiaries to facilitate diversion of funds and evergreening of loans/advances. These all constitutes red flags of fraud in CDEL. 5. The Auditors had given disclaimer of opinion on Consolidated Financial Statements (CFS) about inter aha appropriateness of transections with and recoverability of Rs 3,512 crores from MACEL, a promoter entity. NFRA's examination revealed that the CDEL's Auditors for the FY 2019-20 inter alia ignored all the red flags of frauds available in the above stated investigation report and chose not to exercise statutory access to the books of accounts and records of CDEL's subsidiaries. Further, there were many red flags in the CFS, which were ignored by the Auditors. They failed to meet the relevant requirements of the Standards on Auditing ('SA' hereafter) and provisions of the Companies Act 2013 and also demonstrated a serious lapse and absence of due diligence on the part of the Auditors and EQCR in following matters. 5.1 The Auditors failed to exercise professional judgement & skepticism, thus failed to evaluate fraud risk during audit of (a) fraudulent diversion of Rs 3,512 crores through subsidiaries of CDEL to a promoter's entities named MACEL; (b) evergreening of loans through structured circulation of funds; and ( c) provision made for doubtful land advances of Rs 245 crores given to related parties and others. Diversion of funds to promoter entity without commercial sense and evergreening of loan were clearly visible from the investigation report of DIG of CBI mentioned above; (Section C-1 of this order). 5.2 The Auditors also failed to perform any audit procedure to verify whether CDEL passed special resolution in the general meeting before giving loan of Rs 1,841.46 crores and guarantee of Rs 100 crores to subsidiaries. rows.desc: SA 600 (REVISED) Request for Public Comments by 30.10.2024 (Refer accompanying note on NFRA website) SA 600 (Revised), SPECIAL CONSIDERATIONS—AUDITS OF GROUP FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (INCLUDING THE WORK OF COMPONENT AUDITORS) (Applicable to PIEs under Rule 3 of NFRA Rules 2018 except PSUs, PSBs and PSIs and their branches) Introduction Scope of this SA 1. The Standards on Auditing (SAs) apply to an audit of group financial statements (a group audit). This SA deals with special considerations that apply to a group audit, including in those circumstances when component auditors are involved. The requirements and guidance in this SA refer to, or expand on, the application of other relevant SAs to a group audit, in particular SA 220 (Revised), 1 SA 230, 2 SA 300, 3 SA 315 (Revised), 4 and SA 330. 5 (Ref: Para. A1–A2) 2. Group financial statements include the financial information of more than one entity or business unit through a consolidation process, as described in paragraph 14(k). The term consolidation process as used in this SA refers not only to the preparation of consolidated financial statements in accordance with the applicable financial reporting framework, but also to the presentation of combined financial statements, and to the aggregation of the financial information of entities or business units such as branches or divisions. (Ref: Para. A3–A5, A27) 3. As explained in SA 220 (Revised), 6 this SA, adapted as necessary in the circumstances, may also be useful in an audit of financial statements other than a group audit when the engagement team includes individuals from another firm. For example, this SA may be useful when involving such an individual to attend a physical inventory count, inspect property, plant and equipment, or perform audit procedures at a shared service center at a remote location. Groups and Components 4. A group may be organized in various ways. For example, a group may be organized by legal or other entities (e.g., a parent and one or more subsidiaries, joint ventures, or investments accounted for by the equity method). Alternatively, the group may be organized by geography, by other economic units (including branches or divisions), or by functions or business activities. In this SA, these different forms of organization are collectively referred to as “entities or business units.” (Ref: Para. A6) 5. The group auditor determines an appropriate approach to planning and performing audit procedures to respond to the assessed risks of material misstatement of the group financial statements. For this purpose, the group auditor uses professional judgment in determining the components at which audit work will be performed. This determination is based on the group auditor’s understanding of the group and its environment, and other factors such as the ability to perform audit procedures centrally, the presence of shared service centers, or the existence of common information systems and internal control. (Ref: Para. A7–A9) Involvement of Component Auditors 6. SA 220 (Revised) 7 requires the engagement partner to determine that sufficient and appropriate resources to perform the engagement are assigned or made available to the engagement team in a timely manner. In a group audit, such resources may include component auditors. Therefore, this SA requires the group auditor to determine the nature, timing and extent of involvement of component auditors. 7. The group auditor may involve component auditors to provide information, or to perform audit work, to fulfill the requirements of this SA. Component auditors may have greater experience with, and a more in-depth knowledge of, the components and their environments (including local laws and regulations, business practices, language, and culture) than the group auditor. Accordingly, component auditors can be, and often are, involved in all phases of the group audit. (Ref: Para. A10–A11) 8. Audit risk is a function of the risks of material misstatement and detection risk. 8 Detection risk in a group audit includes the risk that a component auditor may not detect a misstatement in the financial information of a component that could cause a 1 SA 220 (Revised), Quality Management for an Audit of Financial Statements 2 SA 230, Audit Documentation 3 SA 300, Planning an Audit of Financial Statements 4 SA 315 (Revised), Identifying and Assessing the Risks of Material Misstatement 5 SA 330, The Auditor’s Responses to Assessed Risks 6 SA 220 (Revised), paragraph A1 7 SA 220 (Revised), paragraph 25 8 SA 200, Overall Objectives of the Independent Auditor and the Conduct of an Audit in Accordance with Standards on Auditing, paragraph A34 (A32 in existing SA 200). rows.title: Note for public consultation with rationale and background on proposed revisions to SA 600-inviting comments
rows.desc: NFRA PROPOSED REVISION IN SA 600 FOR PUBLIC COMMENTS SA 600 (REVISED), SPECIAL CONSIDERATIONS- AUDITS OF GROUP FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (INCLUDING THE WORK OF COMPONENT AUDITORS) Public Consultation and Request for Comments NFRA invites individuals and organisations to comment on all aspects of the proposals in respect of revision in SA 600 and, particularly, on the specific questions requested in this document. The revisions being proposed are to be applied to audits of Public Interest Entities (PIEs) that fall under Rule 3 of NFRA Rules 2018, except Public Sector Enterprises, Public Sector Banks, Public Sector Insurance Entities, and their respective branches. It would be most helpful if the comments identify and clearly explain the issue or question to which they relate and if possible are supported by empirical data and a clear rationale. Those who disagree with any proposal are requested to describe their suggested alternative(s), supported by specific reasoning, and data as may be applicable. It is requested that the comments in this regard to NFRA may be captioned as “Comments on proposed SA 600 (Revised)” for ease of reference. The draft of the proposed SA 600 (Revised) can be accessed at link below: https://cdnbbsr.s3waas.gov.in/s3e2ad76f2326fbc6b56a45a56c59fafdb/uploads/2024/09/20240917131 3688475.pdf Last date for receiving the comments is 30 October 2024. Email nfra-comments@nfra.gov.in captioned “Comments on proposed SA 600 (Revised)” Postal Captioned “Comments on proposed SA 600 (Revised)” to Secretary, National Financial Reporting Authority 7th-8th Floor, Hindustan Times House, 18-20, Kasturba Gandhi Marg, New Delhi 110001. NFRA PROPOSED REVISION IN SA 600 FOR PUBLIC COMMENTS SA 600 (REVISED), SPECIAL CONSIDERATIONS- AUDITS OF GROUP FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (INCLUDING THE WORK OF COMPONENT AUDITORS) Purpose of this Public Consultation This note covers the background and rationale for NFRA seeking public consultation regarding changes proposed in SA 600-Using the work of Another Auditor, on the lines of the corresponding international standard, ISA 600 issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board (IAASB), pursuant to the decisions taken in the 17 th Meeting of the National Financial reporting Authority, held on 26.08.2024 (the record notes/minutes of Authority Meetings are available on NFRA website under ‘Disclosures’ tab). This Standard is applied in case of audit of companies which have subsidiaries and associates, with the holding company being audited by a principal or main auditor and the subsidiaries and/or associates by ‘other’ or ‘component’ auditors. The standard outlines the responsibilities of the principal auditor vis a vis those of the component auditor. Some of the largest corporations and companies with significant exposure to capital markets, investors, creditors and thereby involving huge public interest, operate through a network of subsidiaries, joint ventures, branches and associates which makes the requirements of this standard very significant. The quality of audit opinion on the consolidated financial statements (CFS), which is relied upon by investors, creditors and other stakeholders, hinges in significant part on how robust this standard is and how it is applied by auditors in discharge of their audit responsibilities. The revisions being proposed are to be applied to audits of Public Interest Entities (PIEs) that fall under Rule 3 of NFRA Rules 2018, except Public Sector Enterprises, Public Sector Insurance Companies, Public Sector Banks and their respective branches. rows.title: Annual Transparency Report by Statutory Auditors of PIEs-Invitation for public comment
rows.desc: / Government of India � � � � � � � /National Financial Reporting Authority ***** 7 th Floor, Hindustan Times House, Kasturba Gandhi Marg, New Delhi Dated: 16.01.2023 Invitation for Comment To Statutory Auditors of the NFRA Regulated Public Interest Entities (PIEs) Subject: Publication of Annual Transparency Reports (ATR) by Auditors/Audit Firms Auditors have a critical role in the financial reporting supply chain of PIEs. Audit of financial reports of PIEs by Independent Auditor enhances the credibility and integrity of the general purpose financial reports of PIEs. Therefore, the need for high-quality comprehensive financial information covering both financial and non-financial aspects of PIEs cannot be overemphasised. 2. Regulators have been prescribing obligations for PIEs to provide high-quality comprehensive financial and non-financial information commensurate with the nature, size and complexity of their operations to the various stakeholders. The role and responsibilities of the independent auditors of such entities have also evolved significantly with focus on the need to build commensurate professional and operating capabilities within the auditing profession. Audit professionals have been augmenting their capabilities and resources including building a network or alliances of firms, domestically and globally, developing in-house multi-disciplinary professionals or professional units, delivering variety of non-audit services, increasing use of digital audit tools and techniques, separating management and governance structures and so on. 3. In this backdrop, Regulators and Oversight Authorities in some overseas jurisdictions 1 require audit firms carrying out audit of PIEs to prepare and publish information in the form of Transparency Reports on annual basis. Accordingly, the audit firms in those jurisdictions have been publishing the Transparency Reports 2 4. Indian companies have become significant constituents of the global economy and India has evolved as global centre of excellence in the delivery of financial reporting and audit services to a large number of multi-national corporations raising expectations for sound and high-quality codes and practices comparable to global benchmarks. 1 Refer Rule 13 of REGULATION (EU) No 537/2014 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 16 April 2014 (EU Audit Regulation 2014) and Section 322 of Corporations Act 2001, Australia and Schedule7A of Corporations Regulations 2001, Australia 2 https://www.pwc.co.uk/who-we-are/transparency-report.html, https://www.pwc.com.pk/en/assets/document/Transparency%20Report%202022.pdf, https://www.ey.com/en_uk/about-us/transparency-report, https://www.ey.com/en_us/2022-ey-us- transparency-report, https://assets.kpmg/content/dam/kpmg/uk/pdf/2022/02/kpmg-uk-transparency- report-2021-a.pdf, https://www.grantthornton.co.uk/globalassets/1.-member-firms/united- kingdom/pdf/annual-reports/transparency-report-2021.pdf, https://www.bdo.com.au/en- au/about/about-bdo-in-australia/transparency, https://www2.deloitte.com/uk/en/pages/annual-review- 2022/audit-transparency-report.html 5. Rule 8(2) of the NFRA Rule 2018 empowers the NFRA to require an auditor to report on its governance practices and internal processes designed to promote audit quality, protect its reputation and reduce risks including risk of failure of the auditor and may take such action on the report as may be necessary. The Committee of Experts 3 appointed by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Government of India in 2018 pursuant to Supreme Court 4 direction had also recommended inclusion of similar requirement in respect of every auditor and audit firm operating in India as a part/member of an international network. 6. In accordance with Rule 8(2) of the NFRA Rule 2018, NFRA considers it appropriate to prescribe publication of Annual Transparency Report containing certain critical information about the auditor’s operational activities, management, governance and ownership structures, policies and procedures necessary to deliver high-quality audits etc. This requirement of an annual transparency report will be implemented in a gradual manner across the audit profession engaged in the audit of PIEs falling within the purview of NFRA, starting with the auditors/audit firms performing audit of top 1000 listed companies (by market capitalisation) from the financial year ending 31 March 2023. Annexure to this document may be referred for the details of the reporting requirements. 7. NFRA requests views/comments of stakeholders on the contents of the Annual Transparency Report given in the annexure so that the suggestions of the stakeholders and public can be considered while finalising its contents. The last date for receipt of comments is 16 February 2023. rows.summary: India’s audit regulator is seeking public comments on requiring statutory auditors of public interest entities to publish annual transparency reports.

It has been noted from these documents that the ICAI had embarked on a project to revise the existing Accounting Standards (ASs) in the background of implementation of Indian Accounting Standards (Ind ASs) for certain class of Companies (called as Public Interest Entities). It has also been noted while discussing Ind AS recommendations during 2010 to 2014 some members of the Core Group set up by MCA for Ind AS Implementation were of the view that the recognition and measurements in accounting standards should be by and large the same for all Companies. Accordingly, ICAI had developed an Approach Paper during 2014-15 for formulating 2 nd set of accounting standards for non-Ind AS companies and this Approach Paper was revised recently in 2020. 3.It can be noted that these Revised ASs will be applicable for Companies to whom the Ind ASs are not mandatory. As a result, these Revised ASs will be mandatory to large number of Micro, Small and Medium-size Companies (MSMCs) and will replace the existing ASs notified under Companies (Accounting Standards) Rules 2006 notified under erstwhile Companies Act, 1956 and which were recently re-notified as Companies (Accounting Standards) Rules 2021 under Companies Act, 2013. CII’s views on NFRA’s Consultation Paper on Enhancing Engagement with Stakeholders (“the Paper”) Background The Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) greatly acknowledge the contribution made by the National Financial Reporting Authority (NFRA) in protecting the public interest and the interests of investors, creditors and others associated with public interest entities falling within the NFRA jurisdiction, by establishing high quality standards of accounting and auditing, and exercising effective oversight of accounting functions performed by the companies and bodies corporate and auditing functions performed by auditors. The NFRA is the first independent Regulator for accounting and auditing in India. It is indeed heartening to recognize that the NFRA is a unique body considering the scope of its functions and duties encompassing a wide engagement with the financial reporting aspects of public interest entities (PIEs) i.e., right from a critical role in Standard-setting, to ensuring effective compliance with those Standards by stakeholders. The NFRA has greatly contributed to improve the quality of corporate financial reporting in the country. CII greatly appreciate and welcome NFRA’s initiative to set up a Technical Advisory Committee (TAC) with regard to enhancing engagement with stakeholders and for providing inputs from the perspective of users, preparers, and auditors of financial statements and advise on suitable methods for promoting awareness relating to compliance with accounting and auditing standards. It is valued that the NFRA is seeking comments and suggestions of stakeholders on the TAC recommendations. It is also encouraging that NFRA has expressed its preliminary views/proposed actions thereon, to provide clarity and thought process. While thanking NFRA for providing the opportunity, CII has engaged with relevant stakeholders on the Consultation Paper on the issues outlined therein, viz., stakeholder engagement, inspection policy of NFRA, communication and advocacy, roadmap for NFRA functioning, building regulatory capacity etc. and submit the comments for kind consideration. Key objectives of the Paper The key objectives of the Paper are to seek inputs from various stakeholders on certain identified areas, which are critical to enhance the stakeholders’ engagement. It is also noted that many of the identified areas and related recommendations are aligned with the best practices followed by other global regulators. The areas covered through this Paper will go a long way in building and enhancing trust and confidence of various stakeholders in NFRA and will help in aligning the processes and systems of NFRA, in line with the global regulators. 3 Our suggestions on the questions raised in the Consultation Paper, have been summarized in the below section: Question # 1 Formation of Stakeholder Consultation and Advisory Groups (a)What would be a suitable list of subjects that should form the standing agenda of the Stakeholder Advisory Group? The formation of a single Stakeholders Advisory Group, with an objective to extend the dialogue with corporates, investors, auditors, and other stakeholders, and give them additional and tangible opportunities to assist NFRA in accomplishing its mission, is a welcome step. Under this mandate, NFRA initiated audit quality inspections of the Chartered Accountants firm M/s CNK & Associates LLP in March 2025. The scope of the inspection included a review of firm-wide quality controls to evaluate the Audit Firm’s adherence to SQC-1 and a review of selected audit documentation of the annual statutory audit of financial statements for the year ending 31.03.2024. Two focus areas, namely Revenue Recognition and Loans and Advances, and one engagement-specific area selected based on risk, were taken for inspection in each audit engagement. The on-site inspection was conducted in October/November 2025. During the inspection, the Inspection Team held discussions with the Audit Firm personnel, reviewed policies and procedures and examined documents to arrive at the prima facie observations. These observations were conveyed to the Audit Firm in writing. The Audit Firm's responses and documents have been reviewed, and the Final Inspection Report has been issued after consideration of all submissions. This public version of the final inspection report excludes confidential or proprietary information, as pointed out by the Audit Firm. rows.title: The PCAOB will hold an open meeting to consider adopting proposed amendments to QC 1000, the PCAOB’s quality control standard, and related proposed amendments to PCAOB forms and the QC reporting rule, set to become effective on December 15, 2026.
rows.desc: At September 9 Open Meeting, PCAOB to Consider Adopting Amendments to Quality Control Standard WASHINGTON, Sep. 3, 2026 The Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (PCAOB) will hold an open meeting at 10:00 a.m. ET on Wednesday, September 9, 2026. At the meeting, the Board will consider adopting proposed amendments to QC 1000, A Firm’s System of Quality Control, the PCAOB’s quality control standard, and related proposed amendments to PCAOB forms and the QC reporting rule set to become effective on December 15, 2026. The meeting is open to the public and will take place in the PCAOB’s Multi-Purpose Room (301) at 1666 K Street NW, Washington, DC. The public may also view the meeting via a livestream on the PCAOB’s event page, and a recording will be available after the meeting concludes.*****About the PCAOBThe PCAOB is a nonprofit corporation established by Congress to oversee the audits of public companies in order to protect investors and further the public interest in the preparation of informative, accurate, and independent audit reports. The PCAOB also oversees the audits of brokers and dealers registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission, including compliance reports filed pursuant to federal securities laws. Related Topics About the PCAOB
rows.summary:
The PCAOB announced that it will hold an open Board meeting on **Wednesday, September 9, 2026, at 10:00 a.m. ET** to consider **adopting proposed amendments to QC 1000, “A Firm’s System of Quality Control,”** along with related amendments to **PCAOB forms** and the **QC reporting rule**. The notice says those amendments are **set to become effective on December 15, 2026**, so firms subject to PCAOB oversight should treat that date as the operative compliance date if the Board adopts the proposals as described. The meeting will be **open to the public**, held in the PCAOB’s **Multi-Purpose Room (301) at 1666 K Street NW, Washington, DC**, and will also be available by **livestream on the PCAOB’s event page**, with a **recording posted after the meeting**.

For compliance purposes, the document does not describe the substantive contents of the amendments themselves, but it does identify the affected regulatory framework: **PCAOB-registered audit firms** and the PCAOB’s **quality control reporting regime**. Because QC 1000 governs a firm’s system of quality control, any adopted changes may affect how firms design, document, operate, and report on their quality control systems, as well as what information must be filed on PCAOB forms under the revised reporting requirements. The only explicit deadline in the notice is the **December 15, 2026 effective date**, so firms should monitor the meeting outcome closely to determine whether implementation work, form updates, or reporting process changes will be needed before then.

rows.title: The PCAOB posted select materials shared for discussion purposes with the Inspections Modernization Council for its meetings in July and August 2026.
rows.desc: PCAOB Posts Discussion Materials From Summer 2026 Meetings of the Inspections Modernization Council WASHINGTON, Aug. 24, 2026 The Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (PCAOB) today posted select materials shared for discussion purposes with the Inspections Modernization Council (IMC) for its meetings in July and August 2026. The discussion materials – which address topics including the development of a QC-informed inspection approach, use of technology, inspection reporting, and remediation – are available at the IMC’s page on the PCAOB website.Launched in May 2026, the IMC is a resource group composed of outside parties with capital markets expertise and knowledge of the PCAOB’s inspection activities. The IMC’s objective is to provide perspectives to inform the PCAOB’s efforts to modernize its inspection program, as part of the PCAOB’s continued efforts to improve audit quality.“The PCAOB’s inspection program has contributed meaningfully to improving audit quality over time, and, to build on these accomplishments, we need to continue to evolve,” said PCAOB Chairman Demetrios (Jim) Logothetis. “Since its formation, the IMC has provided us with excellent input to inform our work in this area, and we thank all IMC members for sharing their time and perspectives.”The PCAOB is posting the IMC discussion materials as part of its commitment to transparency and stakeholder engagement as it works on inspections modernization. Stakeholders with questions or ideas regarding the PCAOB’s inspections modernization efforts are encouraged to contact the PCAOB at [email protected].Note: the materials posted today were prepared by PCAOB staff for discussion purposes. Except for the Board’s authorization to share and post the materials, the materials have not otherwise been approved, adopted, requested, directed, selected, or authorized by the Board.*****About the PCAOBThe PCAOB is a nonprofit corporation established by Congress to oversee the audits of public companies in order to protect investors and further the public interest in the preparation of informative, accurate, and independent audit reports. The PCAOB also oversees the audits of brokers and dealers registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission, including compliance reports filed pursuant to federal securities laws. Related Topics Inspections
rows.summary:
The PCAOB announced on August 24, 2026 that it posted select discussion materials used for the Inspections Modernization Council (IMC) meetings held in July and August 2026. These materials were prepared by PCAOB staff for discussion only and cover the PCAOB’s contemplated inspection-modernization topics, including a quality-control–informed inspection approach, expanded use of technology, inspection reporting, and remediation. The posting itself does not announce a new rule, deadline, or binding compliance requirement; rather, it is a transparency and stakeholder-engagement action tied to the PCAOB’s ongoing effort to modernize its inspections program and improve audit quality.

The IMC was launched in May 2026 and is described as a resource group made up of outside parties with capital markets expertise and knowledge of PCAOB inspection activities. Its role is to provide perspectives to inform the PCAOB’s modernization work, but the group’s materials are not Board-approved policy and have not been adopted, requested, directed, selected, or otherwise authorized by the Board beyond permission to share and post them. For compliance teams, the practical significance is that the PCAOB is signaling possible future inspection-process changes, especially around QC-based inspection methods, technology use, reporting, and remediation expectations, but the document does not impose current operational obligations.

The PCAOB invites stakeholders with questions or ideas about inspections modernization to contact it at [email protected]. The posting is part of the PCAOB’s broader oversight mission over audits of public companies and brokers/dealers registered with the SEC, including compliance reports filed under federal securities laws. Compliance officers should treat this as an advance notice of policy development and a source of insight into the PCAOB’s direction, not as an enforceable requirement at this stage.

rows.desc: PCAOB Posts New Resource to Help Auditors Implement Quality Control Standard QC 1000 Questions and Answers is the latest in the PCAOB’s efforts to provide implementation information and resources WASHINGTON, Aug. 17, 2026 Today, the PCAOB released QC 1000 Questions and Answers, a new staff resource that provides answers to questions about certain matters related to the implementation of QC 1000, A Firm’s System of Quality Control, ahead of the standard’s December 15, 2026, effective date. This resource does not address provisions that are the subject of the proposed or conforming amendments that the Board issued for public comment on June 9, 2026. QC 1000 Questions and Answers is the latest in a range of materials – including videos, online knowledge checks, and more – that the PCAOB has released to assist firms and auditors with the implementation of QC 1000 and other new standards and rules in order to improve audit quality and protect investors. To find these resources and other important information, visit the Implementation Resources for PCAOB Standards and Rules page. For further questions regarding the application of the requirements of QC 1000, contact the PCAOB’s Office of the Chief Auditor (OCA) at 202-591-4395. Registered public accounting firms may also request a consultation with OCA through the Firm Consultation Process on the interpretation and application of PCAOB standards, including QC 1000.*****About the PCAOBThe PCAOB is a nonprofit corporation established by Congress to oversee the audits of public companies in order to protect investors and further the public interest in the preparation of informative, accurate, and independent audit reports. The PCAOB also oversees the audits of brokers and dealers registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission, including compliance reports filed pursuant to federal securities laws.
rows.summary:
The PCAOB announced on August 17, 2026 that it has published a new staff resource, **“QC 1000 Questions and Answers,”** to help firms and auditors implement **QC 1000, A Firm’s System of Quality Control**, ahead of the standard’s **December 15, 2026 effective date**. The resource provides answers to questions about **certain implementation matters** related to QC 1000, but it **does not address provisions covered by the proposed or conforming amendments** the Board issued for public comment on **June 9, 2026**.

For compliance purposes, the key point is that the PCAOB is signaling that firms subject to QC 1000 should use this Q&A as implementation guidance now, before the standard becomes effective, and should also review the broader implementation materials the PCAOB has issued, including videos and online knowledge checks. The PCAOB says these materials are intended to assist **firms and auditors** in implementing QC 1000 and other new standards and rules to improve audit quality and protect investors. If questions remain about how to apply QC 1000, firms can contact the PCAOB’s **Office of the Chief Auditor (OCA) at 202-591-4395** or request a consultation through the **Firm Consultation Process** for interpretation and application of PCAOB standards, including QC 1000.

The document does not announce a new substantive rule change by itself; rather, it is an implementation aid tied to an existing quality control standard with a fixed effective date. Compliance teams at registered public accounting firms should therefore treat this as a prompt to continue implementation work for QC 1000, while noting that any issues associated with the June 9, 2026 proposed/conforming amendments are **not** addressed in this Q&A and would need to be handled separately.

rows.title: The PCAOB announced that Kyle S. Hauptman was sworn in as a Board Member.
rows.desc: Kyle S. Hauptman Sworn In as PCAOB Board Member WASHINGTON, Aug. 10, 2026 The Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (PCAOB) announced today that Kyle S. Hauptman was sworn in as a Board Member. The ceremony took place at the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). "I am pleased to welcome Kyle to the PCAOB,” said PCAOB Chairman Demetrios (Jim) Logothetis. “His deep expertise and extensive experience will be invaluable as we advance our efforts to modernize the PCAOB and strengthen its role as a durable regulator prepared to meet the opportunities and challenges of the next 25 years and beyond.” Board Member Hauptman was appointed by the SEC on January 30, 2026. His current term will expire on October 24, 2029. “I’m honored to join the PCAOB and look forward to working with my colleagues to strengthen the capital markets,” said Board Member Hauptman. “Of particular interest will be the technological changes that are transforming both the audit industry and the PCAOB itself.” Prior to his swearing in as a PCAOB Board Member, Board Member Hauptman was the Chairman of the National Credit Union Administration (NCUA). He was originally appointed by President Donald J. Trump and confirmed by the U.S. Senate to serve as an NCUA Board Member in December 2020. He was elevated to Chairman of the NCUA in January 2025. Before joining the NCUA Board, Board Member Hauptman served as Senator Tom Cotton’s advisor on economic policy, as well as Staff Director of the Senate Banking Committee’s Subcommittee on Economic Policy. He has also held positions at the American Enterprise Institute, Jefferies and Co., and Lehman Brothers. Board Member Hauptman holds an MBA from Columbia Business School and a B.A. from University of California, Los Angeles. *****About the PCAOBThe PCAOB is a nonprofit corporation established by Congress to oversee the audits of public companies in order to protect investors and further the public interest in the preparation of informative, accurate, and independent audit reports. The PCAOB also oversees the audits of brokers and dealers registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission, including compliance reports filed pursuant to federal securities laws. Related Topics About the PCAOB
rows.summary:
The Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (PCAOB) announced on August 10, 2026 that Kyle S. Hauptman was sworn in as a PCAOB Board Member at the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. He had already been appointed by the SEC on January 30, 2026, and his current term as Board Member is scheduled to expire on October 24, 2029.  

For compliance purposes, this is primarily a governance/leadership update rather than a new rule, standard, or filing obligation. The announcement indicates that Hauptman previously served as Chairman of the National Credit Union Administration (NCUA), was elevated to that role in January 2025, and before that held various policy and financial-industry roles; the PCAOB Chairman stated that his experience will support efforts to modernize the PCAOB and strengthen its regulatory role. Hauptman specifically highlighted technological changes affecting both the audit industry and the PCAOB, suggesting continued PCAOB focus on modernization and technology-related oversight, but the document does not announce any immediate compliance changes, deadlines, thresholds, or requirements for public companies, auditors, brokers, or dealers.  

The only compliance-relevant entity context in the release is the PCAOB itself, which oversees audits of public companies and of SEC-registered brokers and dealers, including related compliance reports under federal securities laws. There are no new substantive obligations described in this notice; it is informational and confirms a change in Board membership and the board member’s term.

rows.title: Advancing its strategic planning process, the PCAOB has requested public input on draft goals and objectives for its 2026-2030 strategic plan.

For the next phase of the strategic planning process, the Board is seeking input regarding PCAOB’s Draft 2026-2030 Strategic Plan Goals and Objectives. Additional input from our stakeholders will help the Board and staff further refine the strategic direction, goals and objectives before the final Plan is presented for Board consideration. rows.summary:
The PCAOB has issued a public request for comment on the draft goals and objectives for its 2026–2030 Strategic Plan, which will guide the agency’s priorities for the next five years and also serve as the basis for its annual budget development. This is not a rulemaking that imposes immediate compliance obligations on registrants, auditors, or audit committees; instead, it is a strategic-planning document seeking stakeholder input before the final plan is presented to the Board. The PCAOB says feedback from its earlier March 31, 2026 comment request on strategic priorities was used to shape the draft goals and objectives now out for comment, and all comments submitted in this round will be made public on the PCAOB website.

Interested parties may submit written comments by email to comments@pcaobus.org, through the PCAOB website, or by mail to the Office of the Secretary, PCAOB, 1666 K Street NW, Washington, DC 20006-2803. Commenters are instructed to reference “PCAOB Release No. 2026-006” in the subject or reference line, and submissions must be received by September 4, 2026. The Board encourages—but does not require—commenters to identify themselves and their professional affiliation. The release was adopted by the Board on July 20, 2026, and the contact for questions is Lorene Rosenberg, Chief Strategy Officer, Office of the Chief Operating Officer (202-372-5926, rosenbergl@pcaobus.org).

Substantively, the draft strategic plan is organized around three overarching priorities: “Advance Audit Quality and Investor Protection,” “Clarify Expectations and Our Bases for Decisions Leading to Understandable Outcomes,” and “Transform How Oversight Is Delivered.” Under the first priority, the PCAOB says it will focus oversight on the areas with the greatest effect on audit quality, including promoting a high-quality standard-setting approach, modernizing inspections through a quality-control-focused approach, and targeting enforcement toward conduct that creates meaningful risk to investors. Under the second, the Board emphasizes clearer articulation of the principles that guide standard setting, inspections, and enforcement so that expectations are understandable and decision-making is more consistent. Under the third, the PCAOB plans to invest in technology and data capabilities, strengthen internal coordination and governance, and invest in personnel to make oversight more effective, efficient, and fit for purpose. The draft then begins with Goal 1, “Modernize Standard Setting and Implementation,” which is intended to advance audit quality and clarify what constitutes a high-quality standard by ensuring standards are designed to meaningfully improve audit quality, be implementable, and remain aligned with the public interest.

rows.title: The PCAOB has announced the members of the Inspections Modernization Council, a resource group composed of outside parties with a stake in the PCAOB’s inspection activities.
rows.desc: PCAOB Announces Members of the Inspections Modernization Council WASHINGTON, Jul. 9, 2026 The Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (PCAOB) today announced the members of the Inspections Modernization Council (IMC). A resource group composed of outside parties with a stake in the PCAOB’s inspection activities, the IMC will provide perspectives to inform the PCAOB’s efforts to modernize its inspection program and thereby improve audit quality. Potential changes that the IMC will consider include generating more meaningful outputs for consumers of inspection reports, leveraging technological innovations such as automation and artificial intelligence, and focusing inspections on firms’ systems of quality control. “I was pleased with the tremendous number of high-quality applicants we received for the Inspections Modernization Council. Over 100 people from across the financial reporting ecosystem applied to be part of the IMC, and choosing among them was not an easy task,” said PCAOB Chairman Demetrios (Jim) Logothetis. “We thank all those who applied, and we look forward to hearing more from the experts who have been chosen to serve on the IMC,” Chairman Logothetis added. rows.summary:
The PCAOB announced, on July 9, 2026, the members of its new Inspections Modernization Council (IMC), which is an outside resource group intended to advise the Board on modernizing its inspections program. The IMC is not itself a rulemaking or enforcement body, but it will provide stakeholder perspectives to help the PCAOB improve audit quality by changing how inspections are conducted and how their results are communicated. The PCAOB said the modernization topics the IMC will consider include producing more meaningful inspection-report outputs for users, using technology such as automation and artificial intelligence, and shifting inspection emphasis toward firms’ systems of quality control.

For compliance teams, the key takeaway is that the PCAOB is actively exploring changes to inspection methodology rather than announcing a final rule. That means registered public accounting firms, and indirectly audit committees and public companies relying on PCAOB-inspected audits, should expect possible future adjustments in inspection scope, documentation expectations, use of data analytics/AI in the inspection process, and the way inspection findings are presented. No effective date, deadline, or immediate new compliance obligation was announced in this notice, and the document does not identify any firm-specific requirements or transition periods.

The PCAOB also emphasized the breadth of interest in the council, noting that more than 100 people from across the financial reporting ecosystem applied. The announced IMC members come from accounting firms, public companies, governance organizations, academic institutions, and related oversight bodies, including representatives from Forvis Mazars, Ford Motor Company, Grant Thornton Advisors, Aarya Capital, the Canadian Public Accountability Board, Protiviti, RJI International, the International Corporate Governance Network, Northeastern University, Instacart, S.R. Snodgrass, and COSO. The notice directs readers to the PCAOB website for more information on the IMC and is framed as an informational update within the PCAOB’s inspections topic area.

rows.title: The PCAOB announced the appointment of George Kostolampros as General Counsel.
rows.desc: George Kostolampros Named PCAOB General Counsel WASHINGTON, Jul. 1, 2026 The Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (PCAOB) today announced that George Kostolampros has been appointed the PCAOB’s General Counsel. As General Counsel, Mr. Kostolampros will provide legal advice and counsel on all PCAOB operations and will manage the Office of the General Counsel (OGC). “OGC’s work underpins the PCAOB’s ability to execute its mission to protect investors,” said PCAOB Chairman Demetrios (Jim) Logothetis. “We are grateful that George is joining us to fill this critical leadership role.” Mr. Kostolampros brings more than 25 years of experience advising organizations and senior leaders on complex legal, regulatory, governance, compliance, and risk-management matters. Prior to his appointment as General Counsel, Mr. Kostolampros was a partner at Venable LLP, where he advised public companies, boards of directors, audit committees, financial institutions, and senior executives on compliance, governance, and regulatory matters, and represented clients in internal investigations, government enforcement matters, regulatory proceedings, and complex litigation. Before returning to private practice, he served as Senior Counsel in the Division of Enforcement at the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. Mr. Kostolampros received his J.D., magna cum laude, from Widener University School of Law and his B.A. from Syracuse University. “I am honored to join the PCAOB, and I look forward to working with the talented OGC staff to advance the PCAOB’s priorities and mission,” said Mr. Kostolampros. Matt Goldin, who was named Acting General Counsel in January 2026, will resume his role as Deputy General Counsel, advising the Board on PCAOB programs and operations and assisting with OGC’s management. “Matt is a valued member of the OGC team, and we thank him for his distinguished service as Acting General Counsel,” said Chairman Logothetis.*****About the PCAOBThe PCAOB is a nonprofit corporation established by Congress to oversee the audits of public companies in order to protect investors and further the public interest in the preparation of informative, accurate, and independent audit reports. The PCAOB also oversees the audits of brokers and dealers registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission, including compliance reports filed pursuant to federal securities laws. The announcement does not describe any new rulemaking, filing requirement, deadline, threshold, or compliance obligation for registrants, audit firms, brokers, or dealers; it is an internal leadership appointment rather than a substantive regulatory change.

rows.title: The PCAOB announced the appointment of Dr. Ying Li Compton as its Chief Economist and Director of the Office of Economic and Risk Analysis.
rows.desc: Dr. Ying Li Compton Named PCAOB Chief Economist and Director of Its Office of Economic and Risk Analysis WASHINGTON, Jun. 29, 2026 The Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (PCAOB) today announced the appointment of Dr. Ying Li Compton as the PCAOB's Chief Economist and Director of its Office of Economic and Risk Analysis (OERA). At the PCAOB, OERA conducts independent, evidence-based economic and risk analyses to inform the organization’s oversight activities, including inspections, investigations, rulemaking, standard setting, and post-implementation reviews. “Evidence-based economic and risk analyses are critical to strengthening the PCAOB’s oversight and, by extension, its ability to accomplish its investor-protection mission,” said PCAOB Chairman Demetrios (Jim) Logothetis. “Dr. Compton brings to the PCAOB a strong combination of analytical experience and accounting expertise.” Dr. Compton joins the PCAOB from PwC International Limited, where she served as a managing director advising the Global Assurance Leadership Team. Before that, she was chief of staff to the PwC US Assurance Leader. Prior to joining PwC, Dr. Compton served as Senior Accounting and Economic Advisor to the Chief Accountant in the SEC’s Office of the Chief Accountant, after beginning her time at the agency as a financial economist in the Division of Economic and Risk Analysis. Previously, Dr. Compton worked as an assistant professor of accounting at the George Washington University and Baruch College. She holds a Ph.D. in accounting from Massachusetts Institute of Technology. “It is an honor to join the PCAOB and my OERA colleagues, and I look forward to our work together to build on the PCAOB’s reputation for high-quality analysis,” said Dr. Compton. Dr. Erik Durbin, who was named the Acting Chief Economist and Acting OERA Director in December 2025, will resume his role as OERA’s Deputy Chief Economist, Economic Analysis, responsible for the process and teams that develop the economic analysis for standard-setting and rulemaking projects and for the post-implementation review of their effectiveness. “We thank Erik, both for stepping in as Acting Director during a transition period and for his continued contributions as an important member of the OERA team,” added Chairman Logothetis. *****About the PCAOBThe PCAOB is a nonprofit corporation established by Congress to oversee the audits of public companies in order to protect investors and further the public interest in the preparation of informative, accurate, and independent audit reports. rows.title: Chief Auditor Barbara Vanich will leave the PCAOB after more than 17 years of service.
rows.desc: Chief Auditor Barbara Vanich to Depart the PCAOB WASHINGTON, Jun. 26, 2026 The Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (PCAOB) today announced that Chief Auditor Barbara Vanich will leave the PCAOB on July 15, 2026, after more than 17 years of service. “I have greatly valued Barb’s expert advice – her accomplishments at the PCAOB have been extraordinary,” said PCAOB Chairman Demetrios (Jim) Logothetis. “We thank her for her leadership and dedication, and we wish her well as she embarks on a new professional opportunity.” Ms. Vanich joined the PCAOB in February 2009. After serving in several roles at the PCAOB – including Associate Chief Auditor, Special Adviser to a Board Member, Deputy Chief Auditor, and Acting Chief Auditor – she was named Chief Auditor in October 2022. During her tenure as Chief Auditor, the PCAOB adopted several new standards that represented important milestones in the PCAOB’s work to improve audit quality and protect investors. Most notably, the PCAOB in May 2024 adopted QC 1000, A Firm’s System of Quality Control. The standard, which will become effective December 15, 2026, features a risk-based approach designed to drive continuous improvement in audit quality. Additionally, Ms. Vanich oversaw the development of other major standard-setting projects, the creation of resources to help audit firms with implementation of new standards, the launch of the PCAOB’s Audit Practitioner Fellowship Program, the PCAOB’s first-ever request for comment on potential future areas of focus for standard setting, and the creation of a Firm Consultation Process through which registered public accounting firms can submit standards-related questions directly to PCAOB staff and receive informal staff views. “It has been an honor to advance the PCAOB’s investor-protection mission, together with my talented colleagues in the Office of the Chief Auditor and so many others across the PCAOB,” said Ms. Vanich. The PCAOB is beginning a search to fill the Chief Auditor role and will solicit applications from qualified candidates soon. *****About the PCAOBThe PCAOB is a nonprofit corporation established by Congress to oversee the audits of public companies in order to protect investors and further the public interest in the preparation of informative, accurate, and independent audit reports. The PCAOB also oversees the audits of brokers and dealers registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission, including compliance reports filed pursuant to federal securities laws. Related Topics About the PCAOB
rows.summary:
The PCAOB announced on June 26, 2026 that Chief Auditor Barbara Vanich will depart the organization effective July 15, 2026, after more than 17 years of service. Vanich joined the PCAOB in February 2009 and served in multiple leadership roles before becoming Chief Auditor in October 2022.

For compliance teams, the substantive regulatory item highlighted in the announcement is the PCAOB’s adoption of QC 1000, “A Firm’s System of Quality Control,” which was adopted in May 2024 and is scheduled to become effective on December 15, 2026. The standard uses a risk-based approach intended to drive continuous improvement in audit quality, so firms subject to PCAOB oversight should be tracking implementation readiness against that effective date.

The announcement also notes several related PCAOB initiatives led during Vanich’s tenure that may affect audit firms’ compliance planning and engagement with the PCAOB: development of other major standard-setting projects, creation of implementation resources for firms adopting new standards, launch of the Audit Practitioner Fellowship Program, the PCAOB’s first request for comment on future standard-setting priorities, and the creation of a Firm Consultation Process. Under that process, registered public accounting firms may submit standards-related questions directly to PCAOB staff and receive informal staff views, creating a formal channel for interpretive consultation. The PCAOB said it has begun searching for a new Chief Auditor and will solicit applications from qualified candidates soon; no other immediate compliance deadline is announced beyond the January 15, 2026 departure date and the December 15, 2026 QC 1000 effective date.

rows.title: The PCAOB today announced the establishment of a Firm Consultation Process designed to provide timely and consistent guidance from PCAOB staff.
rows.desc: PCAOB Staff Launches Firm Consultation Process to Enhance Clarity and to Support Application and Implementation of PCAOB Standards WASHINGTON, Jun. 25, 2026 The Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (PCAOB) today announced the establishment of a Firm Consultation Process, led by its Office of the Chief Auditor (OCA), designed to provide more timely and consistent guidance from PCAOB staff. The new process will allow registered public accounting firms to submit questions directly to OCA staff and receive informal staff views regarding the implementation of new standards and application of existing standards. “Delivering clear guidance is essential to the PCAOB’s efforts to drive further improvement in audit quality,” said Chairman Demetrios (Jim) Logothetis. “This staff-led consultation process is designed to help firms implement new standards and apply our standards more consistently, which will ultimately fulfill the PCAOB’s mission to protect investors.” As part of the Firm Consultation Process, registered firms may request a consultation with OCA on the interpretation and application of PCAOB auditing, attestation, and quality control standards and related rules and forms, as well as PCAOB standards and rules on ethics and independence. If the firm decides to proceed with a consultation under this new process, a request for consultation should be submitted by completing the Consultation Intake Form. OCA does not plan to make consultation requests public but may publish public guidance for questions that are frequently asked or may be of use more generally.*****About the PCAOBThe PCAOB is a nonprofit corporation established by Congress to oversee the audits of public companies in order to protect investors and further the public interest in the preparation of informative, accurate, and independent audit reports. The PCAOB also oversees the audits of brokers and dealers registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission, including compliance reports filed pursuant to federal securities laws.
rows.summary:
On June 25, 2026, the PCAOB announced a new **Firm Consultation Process** administered by the Office of the Chief Auditor (OCA) to give registered public accounting firms a more direct way to obtain **informal staff views** on how PCAOB requirements should be interpreted and applied. The process is intended to improve the **timeliness and consistency** of PCAOB guidance, particularly for questions involving the **implementation of new standards** and the **application of existing standards**.

The process is available to **registered public accounting firms** and covers questions about PCAOB **auditing, attestation, and quality control standards**, as well as related **rules and forms**, and PCAOB **ethics and independence** standards and rules. If a firm wants to use the process, it must submit a request by completing the **Consultation Intake Form**. The PCAOB stated that it does **not plan to make individual consultation requests public**, although it may later issue **public guidance** if it receives questions that are asked frequently or that would be broadly useful. There are no specific compliance deadlines, numerical thresholds, or effective-date phase-ins stated beyond the announcement date itself; the key operational change is the availability of this new consultation channel for firms seeking interpretive guidance.

rows.summary:
The PCAOB’s **Annual Report on the Interim Inspection Program Related to Audits of Brokers and Dealers** (PCAOB Release No. **2026-003**, dated **June 11, 2026**) summarizes the Board’s **2025 inspections approach** and **2025 inspection observations** for auditors of SEC-registered broker-dealers. The report is issued under **PCAOB Rule 4020T**, which governs the interim inspection program for broker-dealer audits and related reporting.

For compliance purposes, the document restates the core broker-dealer annual reporting framework under **Exchange Act Rule 17a-5**: broker-dealers registered with the SEC generally must file annually with the SEC a **financial report** (financial statements plus supporting schedules/supplemental information), either a **compliance report** or an **exemption report** depending on whether they claim an exemption from the **Customer Protection Rule (Exchange Act Rule 15c3-3)**, and the related **independent public accountant reports**. If the broker-dealer does **not** claim an exemption from the Customer Protection Rule, it must file a **compliance report** and its auditor must issue an **examination report** under **PCAOB Attestation Standard No. 1 (AT No. 1)**. If the broker-dealer **does** claim an exemption, or is otherwise eligible to do so under SEC rules, it must file an **exemption report** and the auditor must issue a **review report** under **PCAOB Attestation Standard No. 2 (AT No. 2)**. The report emphasizes that these AT No. 1 and AT No. 2 engagements are collectively referred to as **attestation engagements**.

The report also clarifies which broker-dealers are typically in each bucket. Broker-dealers that **carry customer accounts, maintain custody or control of customer cash or securities, or clear securities transactions for customers** generally **cannot** use the exemption and therefore must file **compliance reports**. By contrast, **most broker-dealers, including introducing broker-dealers**, file **exemption reports**. The document notes that broker-dealer audit attestation engagements are complex and involve professional judgment, and that any deficiency described in the annual report reflects information communicated to the PCAOB by the inspection team rather than a final Board determination that the firm committed sanctionable conduct.

From a compliance-team perspective, this document does **not** announce a new rule or deadline change; rather, it is an annual PCAOB inspection report that reinforces the existing filing and auditor-reporting structure and signals how the PCAOB is supervising broker-dealer audit work. The most important operational takeaway is that a broker-dealer must ensure it has correctly determined whether it is required to file a **compliance report** or an **exemption report**, because that decision drives the type of auditor engagement and the required PCAOB report under the relevant attestation standard.

This supplemental request for comment seeks commenters’ views on proposed amendments and other matters discussed in this release. Public Comment: Interested persons may submit written comments to the Board. Comments should be sent by e-mail to comments@pcaobus.org or through the Board’s website at pcaobus.org. Comments also may be sent to the Office of the Secretary, PCAOB, 1666 K Street, NW, Washington, DC 20006-2803. rows.summary:
The PCAOB issued this June 9, 2026 supplemental request for comment on targeted amendments to QC 1000, the standard governing a firm’s system of quality control, plus conforming changes to the QC reporting rule and PCAOB forms. This is not yet a final rule: it is a public-comment release seeking views on specific proposed revisions and related issues, with comments due by July 9, 2026 and submitted by email, web portal, or mail, referencing PCAOB Rulemaking Docket Matter No. 057. The release applies to PCAOB-registered firms and, where relevant, to the persons responsible for firm quality control governance, including firms that will need to design, implement, operate, evaluate, and document a QC system under QC 1000.

The supplemental request indicates the Board is considering amendments in several areas of QC 1000, including the requirement to design, implement, and operate the QC system, roles and responsibilities, the use of an external QC function, information and communication processes, monitoring and remediation, evaluation and reporting on the QC system, and documentation. It also proposes related changes to Rule 2203A and Form QC, as well as amendments to other PCAOB forms to align reporting and filing requirements with the revised QC framework. Because this is a proposal, no new compliance deadline is imposed yet beyond the comment deadline, but firms should review whether the proposed changes would require new governance, escalation, monitoring, and recordkeeping procedures if adopted.

The document’s operative compliance point at this stage is to identify whether a firm’s existing QC program would need redesign or enhancement under the proposed amendments, especially in the areas of accountability, use of outside QC resources, communications within the firm, remediation of QC deficiencies, and formal evaluation/reporting of QC effectiveness. The Board also flags “implementation support efforts” and “recent rulemaking history,” suggesting the proposal is part of a broader QC 1000 rollout and refinement process. For a compliance team, the immediate action item is to assess the proposal against current internal QC policies and, if desired, submit comments before July 9, 2026.

rows.title: The PCAOB will hold an open meeting to consider issuing proposed amendments related to QC 1000, the PCAOB’s quality control standard, for public comment.
rows.desc: At June 9 Open Meeting, PCAOB to Consider Issuing Proposed Quality Control Related Amendments for Public Comment WASHINGTON, Jun. 3, 2026 The Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (PCAOB) will hold an open meeting at 10:00 a.m. ET on Tuesday, June 9, 2026. At the meeting, the Board will consider issuing for public comment proposed amendments to QC 1000, A Firm’s System of Quality Control, the PCAOB’s quality control standard that is set to become effective on December 15, 2026, and related amendments to PCAOB forms and the QC reporting rule. The meeting is open to the public and will take place in the PCAOB’s Multi-Purpose Room (301) at 1666 K Street NW, Washington, DC. The public may also view the meeting via a livestream on the PCAOB’s event page, and a recording will be available after the meeting concludes. *****About the PCAOBThe PCAOB is a nonprofit corporation established by Congress to oversee the audits of public companies in order to protect investors and further the public interest in the preparation of informative, accurate, and independent audit reports. The PCAOB also oversees the audits of brokers and dealers registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission, including compliance reports filed pursuant to federal securities laws.
rows.summary:
The PCAOB announced that it will hold an open meeting on **Tuesday, June 9, 2026, at 10:00 a.m. ET** to consider whether to **issue proposed amendments for public comment** relating to **QC 1000, “A Firm’s System of Quality Control,”** which is the PCAOB’s quality control standard. The notice also says the Board will consider related amendments to **PCAOB forms** and the **QC reporting rule**.

For compliance purposes, the key timing point is that **QC 1000 is currently set to become effective on December 15, 2026**, and the Board is now considering whether to modify that framework before the effective date. The announcement does **not** itself adopt any new requirements or change any obligations yet; it only signals that proposed amendments may be released for public comment after Board consideration at the meeting.

The meeting is **open to the public** and will be held at the PCAOB’s **Multi-Purpose Room (301), 1666 K Street NW, Washington, DC**. It will also be available via **livestream on the PCAOB’s event page**, and a **recording will be posted after the meeting**.

The PCAOB’s oversight scope, as restated in the notice, includes audits of **public companies** and audits of **brokers and dealers registered with the SEC**, including compliance reports filed under federal securities laws. No filing deadline, transition date, or quantitative threshold is stated in this notice beyond the December 15, 2026 effective date for QC 1000.

rows.title: The PCAOB is seeking investors, audit committee members, auditors, financial executives, and other experts to serve on a new advisory body: the Inspections Modernization Council. Applications are due on June 15, 2026.
rows.desc: PCAOB Announces Inspections Modernization Council, Seeks Participation From Outside Experts Focused on modernizing PCAOB inspections, the new advisory body will leverage perspectives from a cross-section of capital markets experts; Deadline for applications is June 15, 2026 WASHINGTON, May 28, 2026 The Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (PCAOB) announced today that it is forming a new advisory body, the Inspections Modernization Council, and is seeking outside parties with a stake in the PCAOB’s inspection activities to participate in its work. Since its creation more than 20 years ago, the PCAOB inspection program has played a significant role in enhancing audit quality. Today, opportunities exist to modernize PCAOB inspections so they remain relevant and resilient. Consultation with outside experts can facilitate such modernization. For the Inspections Modernization Council, the Board seeks participants with capital markets expertise and knowledge of the PCAOB’s inspection program, including investors, audit committee members, financial executives at public companies, academics, technologists, other regulators, and practitioners from public accounting firms of varying sizes. Applicants should have a demonstrated commitment to the interests of investors and the public. “Modernization of PCAOB inspections has the potential to bring improved audit quality and other significant benefits to investors and other stakeholders,” said PCAOB Chairman Demetrios (Jim) Logothetis. “The Inspections Modernization Council will help us shape the future of PCAOB inspections, and we invite individuals of the highest integrity to join us in this effort.” Application and other information can be found on the Inspections Modernization Council page. The application period will close on June 15, 2026. *****About the PCAOBThe PCAOB is a nonprofit corporation established by Congress to oversee the audits of public companies in order to protect investors and further the public interest in the preparation of informative, accurate, and independent audit reports. The PCAOB also oversees the audits of brokers and dealers registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission, including compliance reports filed pursuant to federal securities laws. Related Topics About the PCAOB
rows.summary:
The PCAOB announced on May 28, 2026 that it is creating a new advisory body called the **Inspections Modernization Council** to help modernize the PCAOB’s inspection program so it remains “relevant and resilient” after more than 20 years of operation. This is not a new rule or enforcement action; it is a request for outside experts to participate in shaping how PCAOB inspections work going forward. The PCAOB says the Council will draw on a cross-section of capital markets expertise, specifically seeking **investors, audit committee members, financial executives at public companies, academics, technologists, other regulators, and practitioners from public accounting firms of varying sizes**.

For compliance teams, the main relevance is that the PCAOB is inviting stakeholders with experience in or affected by audit oversight to apply, and it is emphasizing that applicants should have a **demonstrated commitment to the interests of investors and the public**. The PCAOB highlights that the Council will help inform future inspection modernization, which could have downstream implications for audit quality expectations, inspection practices, and regulator-industry engagement. The announcement does not describe any immediate changes to inspection requirements, reporting obligations, deadlines for regulated entities, or enforcement procedures.

The only deadline stated is that **applications close on June 15, 2026**. Interested individuals can find application materials and additional information on the Inspections Modernization Council page. The notice also reiterates the PCAOB’s statutory role: it oversees audits of public companies to protect investors and further the public interest, and it also oversees audits of SEC-registered brokers and dealers, including related compliance reports filed under federal securities laws.

rows.title: The PCAOB announced the appointment of George G. Demos as Director of its Division of Enforcement and Investigations.
rows.desc: George G. Demos Named Director of the PCAOB’s Division of Enforcement and Investigations WASHINGTON, Jun. 15, 2026 The Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (PCAOB) today announced that George G. Demos has been named Director of the PCAOB’s Division of Enforcement and Investigations (DEI). In this role, he will oversee and direct the PCAOB’s investigations and enforcement of violations of its rules, professional standards, and other applicable securities regulations. “Detecting and deterring misconduct is an essential part of how the PCAOB works to improve audit quality and protect investors,” said PCAOB Chairman Demetrios (Jim) Logothetis. “George’s enforcement experience will help the PCAOB advance its goals and fulfill its mission.” Mr. Demos was formerly a litigation partner at DLA Piper LLP, where he represented companies under federal and state investigation and conducted internal corporate reviews. Previously, he served as Senior Counsel at the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission’s Division of Enforcement – leading investigations and prosecutions into accounting fraud, insider trading, and market manipulation – and has been an adjunct professor at UC Davis School of Law. Mr. Demos received a B.A. from Columbia University and a J.D. from Fordham University School of Law. “I am thankful for the opportunity to join the PCAOB, and I look forward to working with the exceptional attorneys, accountants, and other experts on the PCAOB’s enforcement staff,” said Mr. Demos. William Ryan, who was appointed Acting DEI Director in December 2025, will resume his role as DEI’s Chief Counsel, a position to which he was named in 2023. “I want to thank Bill Ryan for his distinguished service over the last six months as Acting Director,” said Chairman Logothetis. “We are fortunate to have Bill on the DEI team.” Learn more about the PCAOB’s enforcement program on the PCAOB website. *****About the PCAOBThe PCAOB is a nonprofit corporation established by Congress to oversee the audits of public companies in order to protect investors and further the public interest in the preparation of informative, accurate, and independent audit reports. The PCAOB also oversees the audits of brokers and dealers registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission, including compliance reports filed pursuant to federal securities laws. Related Topics About the PCAOB
rows.summary:
The PCAOB announced on June 15, 2026 that George G. Demos has been appointed Director of its Division of Enforcement and Investigations (DEI). In this role, he will be responsible for overseeing and directing PCAOB investigations and enforcement actions involving violations of PCAOB rules, professional standards, and other applicable securities regulations.

For compliance purposes, the announcement does not create a new rule, filing obligation, or deadline, but it signals continued and potentially strengthened enforcement focus by the PCAOB. Chairman Demetrios (Jim) Logothetis emphasized that detecting and deterring misconduct remains central to the PCAOB’s mission, which is relevant to public company auditors and broker-dealer audit firms subject to PCAOB oversight. Demos brings prior SEC enforcement experience, including leading investigations and prosecutions involving accounting fraud, insider trading, and market manipulation, and prior private-practice experience representing companies in federal and state investigations and conducting internal corporate reviews.

William Ryan, who had served as Acting DEI Director since December 2025, will return to his prior role as DEI Chief Counsel, a position he has held since 2023. The PCAOB’s broader oversight mandate remains unchanged: it oversees audits of public companies and SEC-registered brokers and dealers, including compliance reports filed under federal securities laws.

rows.summary:
The PCAOB’s January 13, 2026 Order against Zwick CPA, PLLC and owner Jack Zwick arises from violations of PCAOB rules and auditing standards in connection with the audit of one issuer client’s financial statements. The Board accepted the Firm’s and Zwick’s settlement offers and, without them admitting or denying the findings (other than PCAOB jurisdiction), imposed significant sanctions: a censure of both Respondents, revocation of the Firm’s PCAOB registration, a bar on Zwick from being an associated person of any registered public accounting firm, and a joint-and-several civil money penalty of $50,000 against the Firm and Zwick. The Order also requires the Firm to implement specified remedial quality-control measures before it can submit any future PCAOB registration application, and to provide evidence of those measures with any such application.

The Order further restricts future professional activity by making clear that the Firm may not reapply for PCAOB registration until three years from the date of the Order, and Zwick may not petition for Board consent to associate with a registered public accounting firm until three years from the date of the Order. In addition, Zwick must complete 40 hours of continuing professional education focused on PCAOB auditing standards, in addition to any CPE otherwise required for his professional license, before he may file any future petition for Board consent to associate with a registered public accounting firm. The PCAOB states that the sanctions were imposed under Section 105(c) of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act and PCAOB Rule 5200(a)(1) because the conduct met the statutory standard for intentional, knowing, or reckless violations, or repeated negligent violations.

The document identifies Zwick CPA, PLLC as a PCAOB-registered public accounting firm headquartered in Southfield, Michigan, licensed in Michigan and Connecticut, and Jack Zwick as the Firm’s owner and engagement partner responsible for all issuer audits. It also notes that Jeffrey Hoskow was an audit manager at the Firm and an associated person during the relevant period, indicating the violations involved firm personnel beyond the owner. The key compliance takeaway is that this is not merely a monetary sanction: the firm’s PCAOB registration is revoked, future registration is conditioned on remedial quality-control evidence, and Zwick’s future association with any registered firm is barred unless and until the Board later consents after the stated three-year period and completion of the required PCAOB-focused CPE.
